USAGE The additional heater is optional on all versions of this vehicle. It is the Webasto Thermo Top C. model This device makes it possible to: pre-heat the engine coolant reduce the time the engine takes to warm up heat the passenger compartment The advantages of having an additional heater are: less engine wear a reduction in harmful emissions improved comfort increased safety DESCRIPTION OF THE SYSTEM The system is illustrated in the diagram below: 1. Heater. 2. Exhaust pipe. 3. Fuel pump. 4. Fuel supply pipe. 5. Outside air temperature sensor. 6. Heater radiator. 7. Inertia switch. 8. Fuel tank. 9. Integrated electric pump for engine coolant circulation. The system interfaces with the vehicle by means of the engine cooling, fuel supply and electrical systems. interface with the engine cooling system: the coolant leaving the power unit is directed to the heater and is returned to the circuit by a dedicated electric pump. Interface with the fuel supply system: The heater burner is supplied with fuel, taken directly from the tank (9) by means of an electric pump and conveyed in a special pipe (5). Interface with the electrical system: the heater is fitted with dedicated connectors which ensure the supply for the two electric pumps (fuel and coolant), the burner heater plug, the management control unit and the interconnection with the NCL. DESCRIPTION OF THE MAIN COMPONENTS Heater The heater is the central unit of the system. It ensures the heating of the engine fluid and the management of the system operating parameters. The heater includes the various components which are vital for the operation of the system. Burner (1): this includes the inlet connectors (7) and outlet connectors (8) for the engine coolant, the fuel intake (9), the exhaust fumes outlet (10) and the burner. The combustino of the air/fuel mixture, which produces the heat for heating the engine coolant, inside the heat exchanger (2) takes place in the burner. The supply for the burner is consistent with that of the vehicle. It is adapted for the fuel that the vehicle runs on (petrol or diesel) replacing the evaporator mesh and adjusting the ignition plugs operating logic. The combustion exhaust fumes are expelled through a dedicated pipe which has a silencer. Engine coolant circulation electric pump (3): its function is to allow the circulation of the coolant in the system with the engine switched off. Spark plug (4): it is electrically supplied, absorbs a power of 100 W and has a resistance of 0.3 Ohm (± 10%). It has multiple functions. The main function is to start combustion in the burner. It also acts as: a combustion control sensor, measuring the temperature of the actual combustion. According to the value recorded, the control unit varies the speed (flow rate) of the air intake fan, in order to ensure the optimum stoichiometric ratio. In these conditions the spark plug also acts as a safety device. In effect, if the temperature of the flame exceeds 125°C, the electrical supply to the fuel pump is interrupted and the control unit memorizes an error. Flame presence control sensor, in other words it checks the existence of the combustion flame and records the temperature in the combustion chamber. If the flame goes out, the control unit stops the supply of fuel and commands a new ignition cycle. After the third ignition attempt which results in failure, the control unit stops: it removes the supply to the electric fuel pump. It keeps the comburent air intake fan working for a few seconds, facilitating the combustion of the remaining fuel inside the burner. Comburent air intake fan (5): it has the function of introducing the air required for combustion inside the combustion chamber. The fan unit consists of the fan air intake connector (11), the intake fan assembly and the air supply connector for the combustion chamber. The burner incorporates the management electronic control unit (6). It has the task of managing the system, ensuring that combustion takes place normally. The control unit integrated in the heater does not have direct connections with the CANs. The heater is deactivated in the following conditions: combustion flame temperature above 125°C. Failed ignition of the fuel. Combustion cutting out during operation. Battery voltage below 10.5 V or above 15 V measured by the integrated control unit. The efficiency of the components associated with the burner is controlled for each ignition and in the case of problems with the control unit that inhibit the operation of the burner. The control unit interfaces with the NCL via three signals: HS: on/off in Parking Heater/REST mode. ZA: on/off in Additional Heater/REST mode. Status: PWM signal signalling heater malfunctions. The control unit is ventilated by a flow of air introduced by the fan and sent via a small internal connecting pipe. Electric fuel metering pump The fuel metering pump is the impulse type with an electrical supply. It has the task of providing the fuel for the burner, taking it from the tank. The fuel is taken via a dedicated pipe 2 mm in diameter which connects the pump directly to the tank. Outside air temperature sensor This sensor has the function, in accordance with the coolant temperature thermal sensor, of enabling the switching on of the heater as an additional heater. This situation occurs if the power unit is operating and the temperature of the outside air is below 5°C. Under these circumstances the sensor sends a 12 V electrical signal to the heater control unit. THERMO TOP C HEATER TECHNICAL DATA HEATER DIMENSIONS Length ¿¿¿ 235 mm Width ¿¿¿ 106 mm Height ¿¿¿¿.. 168 mm Weight 2,9 Kg POWER Reduced ¿¿¿¿.. 2,5 Kw Max ¿¿¿¿5 Kw Petrol / Diesel CONSUMPTION Reduced ¿¿¿¿.. 0,25 Kg/h Max ¿¿¿¿0,5 Kg/h FLUID DELIVERY 250 l/h OPERATING VOLTAGE 9,7 - 15 V NOISE 51 db SYSTEM OPERATING LOGIC The Webasto heating system operates either with the engine running or switched off. These two conditions determine the system operating mode: with the engine switched off, the additional heater works in Parking Heater, Rest (Restore) or Immediate operation mode. With the engine running, the system operates in Additional heater mode. Irrespective of the operating mode, the procedure for switching on the heater is always as follows: activating the comburent air fan for about 30 secs in order to ventilate and oxygenate the combustion chamber. The fan speed is increased gradually until the average operating value is reached. When 30 secs have elapsed, the heater control unit activates the fuel metering pump and the comburent air fan is switched off for 3 secs to facilitate the ignition of the fuel. The spark plug initiates combustion in the burner. A combustion stabilizataion stage lasting 15 secs is begun during which the fan operates at medium speed. Over the next 50 secs the control unit operates the fan at almost full speed. When the combustion is definitively stabilized, the heater control unit deactivates the spark plug and the fan operates at top speed. From this point the spark plug is used by the system as a combustion control sensor and a flame presence control sensor. Irrespective of the operating mode, the procedure for switching off the heater always involves the ventilation of the combustion chamber for a period of 30 secs with the aim of definitively removing all combustion residues. if the system is switched OFF, automatically or manually, it cannot be reactivated (switched ON) for a period of 3 mins known as Cool Down. Operation with the engine switched off Parking Heater mode In this mode the heater pre-heats the engine coolant and the passenger compartment in advance of ignition. This mode is controlled by a timer, from a radiocontrol signal or manually The system operates in this mode if the following conditions exist: °T passenger compartment < 22°C. Key-OFF (engine rpm = 0 ). No critical battery votlage. During operation in Parking Heater mode, the heater is deactivated by the NCL, completely resetting the function when one of the following conditions occurs: Key-ON. Critical battery voltage. End of the timer. OFF signal from radiocontrol. Manual switching off by the user via the NIT. Heater cotnrol unit status informing of a malfunction The operation of the heater in this mode involves the "waking up" of the NCL by the CAN (at the start of the timer or later on by remote control) irrespective of the starting of the vehicle and consequently: °T passenger compartment < 22°C. air distribution control in HEAT position (DEF/FLOOR). recirculation control closed. air flow rate 20% of seasonal maximum. ON command sent by NCL at HS intake. Webasto control unit waiting status. Switching on/off of heater by timer The switching on of the heater, operating in Parking Heater mode, can be managed by the timer. The timer is set by the user according to their requirements and controls the switching on and off of the heater. The system allows the programming of two daily timers for activating the Parking Heater. The timers are managed by the NIT, not by the NCL. Each timer defines the moment of activation and the duration of the operation of the heater in Parking Heater mode, both with a resolution of 5 mins. The programming of the timers is independent of the key. It can, in effect, be set in either Key-ON or Key-OFF conditions. The duration of the timer cannot exceed 60 mins. If it is not programmed then the pre-defined setting is 15 mins. The timer must, by law, be programmed/confirmed each time it is enabled and confirmed within 24 hours of programming. In addition the repeat function is forbidden by law, therefore the user is obliged to reconfirm the enabling of the timer each time. There is no automatic correction with summertime. A timer can be in one of the following states: disabled: the timer can be programmed in this condition. The parameters can be entered/modified. The parameters entered are evaluated and approved by the NIT. Enabled: the parameters validated by the NIT are memorized. The user confirms the timer, which remains awaiting the start time. The timer is indicated on the NIT display. Activated: The heater is operating in Parking Heater mode controlled by the timer. The timer is indicated on the NIT display. When the timer is activated the NIT "wakes up" the B-CAN and records the system conditions. Zeroed: no parameter entered or enabled. During the operation of the Parking Heater managed by the timer, the system conditions are under the control of the NIT, therefore the B-CAN is always activated. The timer is automatically disabled if: the operation in Parking Heater mode is stopped by the NIT because of the system conditions no longer exists. If the Parking Heater mode is activated using the remote control unit when the timer starts. If the user manually activates the heater during the operation of the timer. If the timer is activated within the heater cool down period. If the user manually disables the timer. If the fuel is in the reserve condition when the timer is activated. This condition is signalled by a message from the system and the user has to confirm the activation. If they do not do so, the timer is disabled. The level of the fuel is supplied by the NBC to the NIT via the B-CAN, if this information is not available then the last reading before the previous Key-OFF is used. If the timer is activated during the operation of the heater through the remote control. The timer is automatically switched off if: the heater is not operating immediately when the timer is activated. The timer parameters are stored in the memory. If the timer is disabled or switched off, it cannot be automatically reactivated but this has to be done manually by the user. Switching on/off of heater by remote control The switching on of the heater, operating in Parking Heater mode, can be managed by the remote control. The switching on command is transmitted by the remote control, with a signal flow rate of around 900 m in an open area and 600 if there are obstacles and is received by the dedicated aerial on the vehicle, transmitted to a Webasto receiver and sent to the NIT. This command is only accepted by the NIT if: Key - OFF. Timer disabled REST (Restore) mode. The REST heater operating mode involves the use of thermal energy from the engine coolant, with the power unit switched off, through the operation of the Webasto unit electric water pump only. This operation is enabled at the NIT by a dedicated meny (with Key-ON and engine started or switched off) whilst it is only activated if the engine rpm = 0. The activation is carried out by sending an ON command, from the NCL, simultaneously to the HS and ZA intakes of the Webasto control unit. When the temperature of the engine coolant is below 50 °C, the Webasto control unit switches on the heater to ensure that the water in the climate control unit radiator becomes and remains sufficiently hot to guarantee the required comfort conditions. The Webasto control unit switches off the heater when the temperature of the H2O is above 70°C leaving only the electric water pump operating. The system cycle therefore operations between 50 °C and 70 °C. In REST mode the NCL automatically controls the mixture and the distribution (unless it has been requested manually), whilst the flow rate value is a display bar. The recirculation is conditioned by the Stop and Go function. The NCL sends the OFF commands to the HS and ZA inputs, completely resetting the REST function, if even only one of the following conditions occurs: engine rpm ¹ 0. Actuvation lasting longer than a limited period (30 mins operation of the heater and/or water pump). Switching off request made by the user using the STOP control at the NIT. Webasto control unit status informing of a malfunction Critical electrical balance (problems with the battery or the alternator). Immediate operation The user can switch the heater on or off manually. The NIT switches the heater off automatically after 30 mins if it is not switched off first by the user. When the heater is switched on in immediate operation, the NIT prevents the programming of the timers. If the user commands it to be switched on in immediate operation during a timer counting, the latter is stopped and the heater continues to work. The remaining time plus the duration of immediate operation cannot exceed 60 mins. If the user activates immediate operation and the fuel is in the reserve condition, a message informs of this situation. They are asked whether they want the heater to operate. If the user confirms this wish, the heater is operated, otherwise it is not activated. This procedure is also activated if the fuel is in the reserve condition during immediate operation. Operation with engine on Additional heater mode. This operating mode involves the switching on of the heater following a signal sent by the climate control unit to the Webasto control unit ZA intake. This mode is activated by the NCL if the following conditions exist at the same time: Key - ON engine rpm > 700 RPM °T coolant fluid < 30 °C °T set at the NIT (for right or left zone) > °T effective in passenger compartment An OFF command is sent from the NCL at the Webasto control unit ZA intake, completely resetting the function (until the next Key-ON/OFF), if: °T coolant fluid > 70 °C Control unit status informing of a heater malfunction.

SPECIFICATIONS The system is designed to clean and wash the windscreen. There is also a device for washing the front light clusters. COMPOSITION The system comprises the following Assemblies: A windscreen wiping assembly consisting of: a control unit (Windscreen Wiper Control Unit - CTC) an electric motor two wiper arms with blades an electronic rain sensor A windscreen washing assembly consisting of: a windscreen washer and headlamp washer reservoir an electric pump operated by the right steering column switch unit lever A headlamp washer assembly consisting of: a reservoir shared with the windscreen washer system a specific electric pump two headlamp washer jets located in the front bumper connecting pipes between the reservoir and the headlamp washer jets 1 - Windscreen wiper blade 2 - Wiper arm 3 - Windscreen wiper mechanism 4 - Windscreen wiper motor 5 - Windscreen wiper control unit 6 - Windscreen washer jets 7 - Reservoir 8 - Windscreen washer pump 9 - Headlamp washer pump 10 - Headlamp washer jets 11 - Rain sensor 12 - Control device OPERATION By operating the right steering column switch unit lever the user sends signals for activating and selecting the following components to the Windscreen Wiper Control Unit (CTC): front windscreen wiper arm electric motor windscreen washer pump headlamp washer pump windscreen wiper speed in continuous operation mode windscreen wiper activation frequency in intermittent operation mode rain sensor sensitivity MULTIFUNCTION SWITCH OR RIGHT LEVER It includes the front wiper controls. All the controls are activated using the lever or the ring nut on the actual lever. Below is a list of the right lever controls: 0 - Rest position 1 - Single impulse position 2 - Intermittent position 3 - First speed position 4 - Second speed position RESERVOIR The reservoir, located on the right front side panel, allows the windscreen washer system pump to take the water/anti-freeze mixture for cleaning the front windscreen; in addition, it also supplies the headlamp washer system through a specific pump. Services provided The reservoir has a capacity of around 5 litres and guarantees a minimum of 25 washing cycles for both the front windscreen and the front light clusters. Structure The reservoir, made from plastic, is fitted with a level sensor and external housings for the windscreen washer and headlamp washer pumps. 1 - Windscreen washer fluid reservoir 2 - Two-way pump supplying fluid to the jets 3 - Fluid level sensor 4 - Headlamp washer pump system RAIN SENSOR ELECTRONIC UNIT Specifications The rain sensor (which comes in one piece with the dusk sensor) works on an infrared wavelength, based on the principle of refracting a light beam through the windows and allowing the automatic adjustment of the number of windscreen wiper blade strokes in proportion to the intensity of the rain. Continuous timing at 2 windscreen wiper speeds by the rain sensor The rain sensor is activated by operating the steering column switch unit lever in the intermittent position. In this position there are 4 possible settings for the sensor which is adjusted using the ring nut on the lever. The transmission of messages between the sensor and the CTC takes place via the A-BUS serial line. Rain sensor failure management If there is a fault in the rain sensor or if the Windscreen Wiper Control Unit does not receive information via the A-BUS serial line, the CTC operates in manual mode depending on the position of the ring nut/lever, sending a malfunction signal to the Instrument Panel Node via the Body Computer Node (through the B-CAN). For more information see [DF5540]. (See subassembly ) 5540 EXTERIOR LIGHTING WINDSCREEN WASHER ELECTRIC PUMP The electric windscreen washer pump is activated through the right steering column switch unit lever. HEADLAMP WASH/WIPE The headlamp wash/wipe system is designed to clean the surfaces of the front light clusters and keep them clean. 1 - Electric headlamp washer pump 2 - Headlamp washer fluid reservoir 3 - Right and left jets 4 - Pipe 5 - Three-way connector Headlamp washers The headlamp washer system consists of: a specific electric pump on the windscreen washer fluid reservoir two devices with jets which are recessed in the bumper three connecting pipes between the pump and the devices inside the bumper Type The system, which is the pressure fluid washing type, uses the fluid in the windscreen washer reservoir and is automatically activated thanks to the presence of a 12V timer which is supplied when the user activates the windscreen washer with the dipped headlamps switched on. Operation The headlamp washer function is only activated if the dipped or main beam headlamps are switched on. The headlamp washer command is not a specific command, it is the same one given by the steering column switch unit to carry out the front windscreen washer function. Each time the windscreen washer is activated, the Body Computer Node implements the headlamp washer function for a duration of 440ms +/- 10 ms. System details The headlamp wash/wipe system uses two telescopic type jets that, in the rest position, are recessed in the upper part of the front bumper. The force applied to the jet by the pressurized liquid when the pump is operated causes the upwards movement of the jet. Activating the device twice in succession produces optimum washing of the headlamps.

DIAGRAM The composition of the automatic climate control system is illustrated in the diagram below: 1. Compressor. 2. Condenser. 3. Drier filter. 4. Four stage pressure switch. 5. Expansion valve. 6. Fan. 7. Evaporator. 8. Pollen filter. 9. Heater radiator. 10. Distributor unit By analyzing the pressure values inside the system, two circuits are defined: High Pressure circuit, comprising the section of the system including the compressor, the condenser, the drier filter and the expansion valve. The pressure values in this circuit vary between 10 and 17 bar (80-100°C). Low Pressure Circuit, comprising the section of the system incuding the expansion valve and the evaporator. The pressure values in this circuit vary between 0.5 and 2 bar (1-5°C). As can be seen the expansion valve is the same for both circuits and joins them. In effect, the coolant fluid inside the valve undergoes a drastic fall in pressure. DESCRIPTION OF THE COMPONENTS 1. Compressor This is the operating machine for the climate control system that uses the mechanical energy fro the engine via a pulley and the electro-magnetic clutch to circulate the coolant fluid in the circuit. Depending on the version, this vehicle is equipped with either SANDEN or NIPPODENSO variable capacity compressors. These compressors make it possible to gradually alter the flow rate of the coolant fluid reaching the evaporator. The adoption of these compressors makes the presence of the frost sensor redundant and it is therefore no longer fitted. The adjustment of these compressors is based on the intake pressure value according to the following logic: low pressure, the capacity of the compressor tends towards the minimum value. High pressure, the capacity increases. This adjustment logic refers to the following practical conditions: "low intake pressure" means that he load on the climate control system is such that it does not require a high fluid flow rate. Therefore the intake pressure for the compressor is reduced compared with normal operation and the capacity of the compressor is reduced. "high intake pressure" means that there is an increased load on the climate control system and the amount of coolant fluid required is high. Therefore the pressure at the compressor intake is increased compared with normal operation and the capacity of the compressor increases to increase the flow rate of the fluid in the circuit. These compressor operate at maximum capacity in normal operating conditions. The compressors for self-driven climate control systems take their power directly from the crankshaft by means of a poly-V belt. The poly-V belt is wound around the compressor pulley (1). The pulley is not in one piece with the compressor shaft, but is fitted on it by means of a ball bearing (2). The pulley is fitted between the electro-magnet (3) and the front disc by an electro-magnet coupling (4). The front disc is in one piece with the end shaft of the shaft through the coupling with the splined profile. When the climate control system is not working, the pulley freewheels on the ball bearing, driven by the poly-V belt. The front disc is located 0.6 - 0.8 mm from the pulley. The compressor is therefore inactive (A). When the system is switched on, the electro-magnet is supplied and produces a magnetic field. The resulting force attracts the front disc against the pulley, joining it to the coupling and, consequently, the compressor shaft. This therefore causes the latter to rotate (B). The management of the engagement of the compressor is entrusted to the Climate Control Node (NCL). The NIPPODENSO ND7SB16 compressor is the alternating piston type. It is fitted on all versions excluding the 3.0 V6 petrol. The capacity of this type of compressor can vary as a result of: variations in the load required from the system, changes in the outside temperature and/of humidity conditions, sharp alterations in the engine load conditions. The main features of the compressor are: direction of rotation: clockwise Max continuous number of revs: 8500 rpm. Max non-continuous number of revs: 9200 rpm. Number of pistons: 7. Min stroke: 4.5 mm. Max stroke: 28.69 mm. Min capacity: 8 cm³/rev Max capacity: 161 cm³/rev Quantity of lubricant: 140 ± 10 cm³ . Type of oil: ND 8. The compressor consists of seven pistons (1) fixed to a connecting rod holder oscillating plate (2). The pistons move inside the cylinders housed in the compressor casing and are moved by the oscillations of the connecting rod holder plate. The movement of the plate is produced by the transmission shaft (3). The latter is rotated by the pulley with the electro-magnet clutch, consequently by the crankshaft. The flow rate of the coolant fluid is regulated by altering the capacity of the compressor. This is achieving by varying the angle of the connecting rod holder plate, in other words by altering the piston stroke. The inclination angle (?) of the connecting rod holder plate is determined by the regulating valve (4), which allows the alteration in the pressure inside the compressor casing (Pc) depending on the intake pressure. In normal operating conditions, the intake pressure (Ps) acting on the diaphragm (1) overcomes the force exerted by the spring (2). The ball (3) closes the flow for the supply pressure (Pd) and the pressure inside the compressor casing (Pc) remains unchanged. The capacity does not alter, in other words it remains at the maximum value. In the case of "low intake pressure" it does not manage to overcome the force of the spring (2), therefore the ball (3) is moved and releases the flow of the supply pressure (Pd). The pressure chamber (4) (Pd) is in contact with the the entire compressor casing: the pressure inside the compressor (Pc) increases. Under these circumstances (Pc) > (Ps), in other words the pressure acting under the piston skirt is greater than that at the piston crown, means that the connecting rod holder plate and (?) tends to be reduced thereby reducing the capacity of the compressor and, consequently, the flow rate. The SANDEN SD7V16 compressor is the alternating piston, variable capacity type. It is fitted on the 3.0 V6 petrol engine. The capacity of this type of compressor can vary as a result of: variations in the load required from the system, changes in the outside temperature and/of humidity conditions, sharp alterations in the engine load conditions. The main features of the compressor are: direction of rotation: clockwise. Max continuous number of revs: 7000 rpm. Max non-continuous number of revs: 8000 rpm. Number of pistons: 7. Min stroke: 2.2 mm. Max stroke: 34.2 mm. Min capacity: 10.4 cm³/rev Max capacity: 161.3 cm³/rev Quantity of lubricant: 135 cm³. Type of oil: ND 8. The compressor is caused to rotate by the power unit through the pulley (1) and the electro-magnetic clutch (2). The compressor propeller shaft (3) causes the rotation of a circular shaped rotor (7). The rotor is not fitted on the shaft, but is connected to it by means of a bearing (11), in one piece with the shaft, that engages with a slotted plate (12) fastened to the rotor. There is a circular plate known as the "connecting rod holder" (6) fitted on the rotor hub to which the connecting rods (5) for the pistons (4) are connected by means of ball joints. The rotor - connecting rod holder plate coupling is achieved by means of an axial thrust bearing (9) fitted between the rotor ring gears and the plate and a radial bearing (10) between the rotor hub and the plate inner ring. The connecting rod holder plate, in addition to being connected to the rotor, is secured to the compressor casing by means of splining in the edge of the ring gear, which houses an adjustable bush made from a low friction material which engages the end of a slide made from a low friction material (13). The other end of the slide is inserted in an adjustable housing in the compressor casing. The alternating motino of the pistons is produced as a result of the angle of the rotation axis of the rotor-connecting rod holder plate assembly in relation to the compressor shaft. It is necessary to point out that, given the fitting described previously, the connecting rod holder plate does NOT rotate with the rotor, but obtains the oscillating movement produced by the rotation of the rotor in relation to a tilted axis from it. The inclination of the assembly is made possible by the opportunity for the shaft bearing to slide inside the rotor plate slot. The angle of the plate is determined by a regulation valve (8) according to the difference in pressure between the intake and the supply. In normal operating conditions, the compressor works at maximum capacity, whilst with a low intake pressure the angle of the plate decreases and there is a reduction in capacity. 2. Condenser The condenser is a heat exchanger located in front of the engine cooling radiator and therefore air comes into contact with it whilst the vehicle is moving forward. The condenser is positioned between the compressor outlet and the inlet for the drier filter and has the function of liquifying the refrigerant in a gaseous state coming from the compressor: The refrigerant fluid in a gaseous state and at a high temperature passes throug the condenser coils and liquifies, on average, at a temperature of 60°C. When the vehicle is stationary or driving in traffic, the air is moved by the engine cooling circuit radiator fan. An insufficient thermal exchange in the condenser causes the incomplete condensation of the fluid and, therefore, an increase in the system pressure, considerably reducing the efficiency of the actual system. 3. Drier filter The drier filter is connected to the condenser outlet and the inlet for the evaporator and has the following functions: filtering any impurities in the refrigerant fluid (containing some of the compressor oil), separating the fluid from possible dampness, acting as a reserve reservoir for the actual refrigerant. The impurities that could block the expansion valve are trapped by two filtering layers. The possible dampness is absorbed by a chemical compound known as silicagel. The refrigerant fluid enters through the intake (1) in a liquid state (coming from the condenser), passes through the first of the two filtering layers (3), which traps any impurities, is filtered by the silicagel (4), which retains the dampness and then, lastly, passes through the second filtering layer. The fluid comes out of the filter through the outlet pipe (2) and flows to the expansion valve. The intake for the pipe (2) is positioned at the base of the filter to guarantee that the refrigerant fluid sent to the expansion valve is in a liquid state. In effect, it can happen that there are some saturated vapours at the filter inlet (condenser outlet). In this case, the refrigerant fluid in a gaseous state remains in the top part of the filter. The introduction of refrigerant fluid in a gaseous state into the evaporator (via the expansion valve) will reduce the efficiency of the system. A certain amount of compressor lubircation oil, which normally circulates mixed with the refrigerant fluid, is also deposited at the bottom of the filter. The outlet pipe also draws in lubrication oil in addition to refrigerant fluid in a liquid state. The level of the fluid inside the drier filter mainly depends on the temperature of the actual fluid and the system load conditions. the filter must be kept with the connectors sealed in a dry environment until the moment it is fitted in order to prevent dampness from entering. 4. Multi-stage pressure switch (4 STAGE) Located on the high pressure inlet pipe on the drier filter. 1. Multi-stage pressure switch This is a 4 stage pressure switch that controls the safe and correct operation of the system. The 4 pressure stages allows the compressor and the cooling fan to be switched on/off: 1st stage (about 2.5 bar): minimum pressure that the compressor can be switched on at. 2nd stage (about 15 bar): pressure that requires the engagement of the first fan speed. 3rd stage (about 20 bar): pressure that requires the engagement of the second fan speed. 4th stage (about 28 bar): maxmum pressure that switches off the compressor. 5. Expansion valve The expansion valve is fitted on the evaporator inlet and outlet ducts with the task of regulating the flow and expansion of the R134a fluid at the evaporator intake. The refrigerant fluid undergoes a sudden and drastic fall in pressure and temperature inside the valve. This results from the fluid entering being made to pass through an opening at high pressure (10 - 17 bar). The section of the opening is determined by the position of the shutter (4), which is automatically modified by the actual valve. The automatic adjustment of the section through which the refrigerant fluid passes, inside the expansion valve, is carried out by a sensitive bulb (1) which is affected by the pressure of the refrigerant fluid coming out of the evaporator. Depending on the latter, the valve suitably regulates the narrow section (2) acting, by means of a rod (6), on the shutter, opposed by a spring (3) and determines the extent of the refrigerant fluid flow. The opposing spring is pre-loaded via a regulation screw (5) in production. The valve regulation logic is as follows: the increase in pressure at the evaporator outlet, detected by the bulb, ensures that the valve tends to close with a consequent decrease in the flow rate of the fluid in the evaporator. A low evaporator outlet pressure involves an increase in the narrow section and, therefore, the flow of refrigerant fluid. The valve regulation screw is calibrated during production and should NOT be tampered with to avoid adversely affecting the efficiency of the system. 1. Sensitive bulb 2. Narrow section 3. Spring 4. Shutter 5. Adjustment screw 6. Rod 6. Fan The fan has the function of sending outside or recirculation air to the evaporator. It is activated by a brushless electric motor with a 12 V supply and operated at different speeds by a PWM signal coming from the NCL. It is located inside the climate control system assembly near the evaporator. The different fan speeds determine the different air flow rate values in the passenger compartment. 7. Evaporator The evaporator is a heat exchanger housed inside the distributor unit. It consists of an aluminium structure with fins to increase the heat exchange surface area. The evaporator has the task of removing heat and humidity from the air introduced into the passenger compartment, taking advantage of the change in state of the refrigerant fluid, from a liquid to a gas, which takes place inside it. This change in state is determined by the air directed towards the evaporator by the fan. The air comes from the outside or from the passenger compartment via the recirculation function. As the air is at a higher temperature than the refrigerant, it gives off some of its heat, thereby cooling down. The heat given off causes the vaporization of the refrigerant fluid (change of state) inside the evaporator. The humidity, present in the air, condenses on the evaporator fins, in the form of droplets, as a result of the decrease in temperature. These are collected in a chamber and moved away, as appropriate. This produces cool, dehumidified air. The process is extremely quick since the refrigerant fluid enters the coil atomized at a low pressure and low temperature. The evaporator is chemically treated to be resistant to the corrosion caused by the condensation process. 8. Pollen filter This is a combination type passenger compartment air filter: PARTICLES + ACTIVE CHARCOAL. It is designed to filter the air entering the passenger compartment. The first layer (particles) prevents the intake of pollen and pollutant particles into the passenger compartment; the second layer (active charcoal) reduces the annoying sensation caused by unpleasant smelling substances due to dampness forming on the surface. 1. Pollen filter The main specifications of the filter element are: high filtering capacity: the filter traps more than 50% of particles between 0.5 ¸ 1 micron in size, more than 80% between 1 ¸ 1.5 micron and about 98% bigger than 2 micron. 9. The function of the heater is to supply the heat needed to heat up the air introduced into the passenger compartment. 10. (Diesel versions only). Flap actuators. Air temperature sensors. Pollen filter. Fan. The air inside the distributor unit is moved by the fan. The direction created by the position of the flaps determines the temperature of the air coming out of the vents. In the DUAL ZONE system there are two areas managed separately inside the distributor unit. This is made possible by a vertical partition that divides the unit into two compartments which can be regulated independently. The division of the volume inside the distributor unit is about 1/3 for the left zone (driver's zone) and 2/3 for the right zone (front and rear passengers zone). Refrigerant fluid The fluids suitable to be used in a refrigerant circuit, such as the one used for the climate control system, are known as refrigerants. They are fluids capable of producing a considerable decrease in temperature and, therefore, suitable for absorbing a large amount of the heat present in the air, changing from a liquid state to a gaseous stage. 'The main specifications of a refrigerant fluid should be: LOW BOILING POINT at normal pressure. A LOW FREEZING POINT, to prevent solidification even in the harshest climates. A LOW EVAPORATION TEMPERATURE (change from a liquid state to a gaseous state). A LOW CRITICAL TEMPERATURE (temperature above whch it is no longer possible to liquefy the gas, whatever the pressure applied). COMPATIBLE WITH THE ENVIRONMENT. MIXABLE with the lubricants used in these systems. In addition, they should not be: EXPLOSIVE AND FLAMMABLE; to prevent danger in the case of leaks inside the engine comparment. TOXIC OR HARMFUL; in order not to cause injury to people. OXIDIZING AND/OR CORROSIVE; not to damage the system components. The fluid whose properties are current best suited to the needs of the climate control systems used on motor vehicles is hydrofluorocarbon (HCF) CH2F CF3 or R134a. The specifications of this fluid are: boiling point at a pressure of 1 bar: -26.5 °C. Freezing point: -101 °C. Latent heat vaporization: 175.05 kj/kg (about 42 kCal/kg). Ozone destruction potential: 0. The system on this vehicle is pressurized with: 730 ± 25 g of R 134a fluid for the 3.0 V6 version 650 ± 25 g of R 134a fluid for all the other versions. Lubrication The climate control system compressors that use HFC R134a refrigerant fluid are lubricated using synthetic oils. The main feature of these oils is their ability to mix with the refrigerant fluid because they circulate throughout the system transported by the R134a. In reality, the compressor oil also lubricates the expansion valve and the connector seals. The following synthetic oils are used: P.A.G. (polyalkaligycols) and N.D. (Nippondenso). They are oils produced through the atomization of alcohol with ethylene and propylene oxides. They are very hygroscopic (capacity to absorb humidity) and therefore the compressors need to be kept well sealed to prevent the oxidation of the oil. In the case of operations that involve replacing the system components, special oil must be added, in the quantities indicated below, before refitting: Drier filter: 15 cm³ Pipes: 5 cm³/m Evaporator: 40 cm³ Condenser: 40 cm³ If the compressor is being replaced, proceed as follows: Pour the oil contained in the compressor to be replaced into a graduated container. Repeat the previous operation for the new compressor. the replacement compressor is supplied pressurized with nitrogen to prevent the intake of humidity; therefore, when fitting the inlet and outlet connector plugs must be removed slowly with the compressor positioned with the cover facing upwards. It should be noted that the quantity of oil removed from the new compressor is greater than that removed from the compressor being replaced. Equalize the two levels, removing the excess amount of oil from the new compressor and reintroduce the quantity of oil remaining. The amount of oil eliminated corresponds to that remaining inside the climate control system circuit components. The following WARNINGS must always be taken into account: do not use the oil used in systems pressurized with R12 or Freon 12 for systems pressurized with R134a. The level of the oil in the compressor does not have to be checked periodically unless leaks have been noticed or there are breaks in the pipes or one of the components has to be replaced. It should be remembered that, with the circuit switched off and the outside temperature between 20 and 25°C, the pressure in the entire circuit is 5-6 bar. If the level of the oil has to be checked, drain the system to prevent a jet of oil or coolant from escaping.

The automatic climate control system fitted on this vehicle is the dual zone type, in other words the temperature inside the passenger compartment is managed in two zones: the driver's zone (1) and the (front and rear) passenger zone (2), in other words the system allows the occupants in each of these zones to set different temperature values. The flow rate, on the other hand, is the same in the two zones. 1. Driver's zone 2. Passenger zone The control of the temperature is based on the "thermal balance" principle, i.e. the climate control system develops sufficient thermal power to keep the inside temperature set by the user constant and compensate for the thermal energy which the vehicle exchanges with the outside depending on the climate conditions (including radiation). This automatic climate control system has a function that allows the occupants in the front of the vehicle (driver and passenger) to request the intake of "diffused" air into the passenger compartment. In this configuration the climate control system operates using three additional vents, located in the dashboard, and makes it possible to employ a different internal temperature maintenance strategy which has the following advantages: increased thermal exchange surface with the ambient inside the vehicle. Less impact speed between the air and the passengers. Less air flow noise.

F.L.ORE.N.C.E. ELECTRICAL AND ELECTRONIC SYSTEM In conventional electrical systems, functions are activated with the aid of dedicated point-to-point lines The increase in the number of electrical/electronic devices on board new cars has given rise to heavier and more complex connections. This is partly due to the complexity of the functions implemented in the burgeoning number of electronic units - which also need to exchange data continually: all this makes new electrical systems more difficult to install and increases the complexity of fault diagnosis. Many problems have been overcome and new electrical systems have been optimised compared to conventional systems by using a network form of connection. This provides a more effective means of managing communication on the board the car and of transferring data between the various subsystems. Information is distributed via serial pathways (buses) that may take the form of: individual wires, twisted wire pairs or even optical fibres. Conventional solution The three control units (electronic nodes) require a number (N) of wires for each input/output data item in order to perform their function. This multiplied the amount of cable required to the point that systems are made more complex (design and manufacture) and more voluminous (weight, bulk, cost). Some 40 kg of wiring looms are required that stretch for more than 2 km - and this figure could double every 10 years because even now a car could be equipped wiht 20 to 40 electronic control units (ECUs). Tx - information to be transmitted from nodes A (A1,A2) B (B1, B2) C (C1, C2) Rx - information to be received from nodes A (B1, B2, C1) B (A1, A2, C2) C (A2, B1, B2) The first step towards reducing the volume and complexity of wiring looms was to group several electronic functions in a single unit: fewer control units = fewer wires. Examples of integation Engine control unit (NCM) manages: injection, ignition, pollution system, engine cooling control etc. 1 - Engine management control unit 2 - Engine cooling fan, 1st speed 3 - Engine cooling fan, 2nd speed 4 - Injectors (injection) 5 - Coils (ignition) 6 - Lambda sensor Integration of electrical/electronic functions in a single electronic control unit (ECU) has allowed us to improve: current uptake management (lowe battery wear); operation of appliances, because they are managed by a single control unit; troubleshootng due to self-diagnosti functions in the control units. This first stage allowed us to reduce the number of electronic units but not to reduce the volume of wiring to a sufficient extent. Multiplexing solution This involves exchanging various data signals between various ECUs on a single transmission channel (a principle already used for phone, radio and TV networks): 1 BUS (2 wires) for all data. A-B-C - Nodes (ECU) A1-A2-B1-B2-C1-C2 - Communication bus D - Body Computer master ECU The second stage allowed us to make a decise leap in terms of: Reducing and simplifying the wiring Reducing the number of sensors (information sharing) Allowing ECUs to communicate among themselves. As more and more systems require interconnection, the MULTIPLEXING solution becomes more and more attractive. In general terms, in order to transmit data via a multiplexing system we need to define the following with precision: transmission channel (wires, optical fibres, radio waves etc.); type of signal sent via the channel (voltage, current, light etc.); the communication protocol (all the rules that allow management of analogue or digital transmission type, code type, address, transmission order, error detection etc.). The transmission support or channel on the car is a pair of wires known as a BUS. The system therefore transmits batches (packages of information sent one after another. This is not done in any particular set order but in accordance with the needs of the control unit). The signals are voltage signals and the protocol used is CAN (Controller Area Network), a system that was developed and introduced by Robert Bosch in 1983. F.L.ORE.N.C.E. ARCHITECTURE The "F.L.ORE.N.C.E." (Fiat Luxury-car OrientEd Networks and Control Electronics) was designed for optimal management of electrical and electronic functions on top-of-the-range car models. The system interacts with all electrical system functions to directly control body functions (visibility, access, on-board information, comfort, communications etc.) and supports information exchange between traction control systems (engine, braking, gearbox etc.). To optimise the system, each control unit (electronic or electromechanical) is located in a central position in relation to the functions it manages. This allows the power and signal distribution system to be minimised. This is also made possible through extensive use of serial communication networks that allow us to overcome problems of space-saving, reliability, weight and cost. Power is distributed via the junction units and/or fuse boxes. These are connected to control elements (relays and static actuators) to ensure maximum electrical protection and minimum complexity. The wiring architecture is reduced because each system function requires fewer dedicated wires. This is because the wires (ABS, airbag, sidebag) are integral with the front, facia and rear wiring loom to simplify installation operations. Systems of this type offer innumerable benenfits, for example: sensors included in the various subsystems are available to the network; information may be shared; sensor duplication is eliminated; system flexibility is increased; new functions may be added simply by changing the software (developments throughout the car’s lifetime); wiring design is simplified and the number of connectors reduced; the operational safety of electronic devices is increased to improve the reliability of information transmitted; because a diagnostic function is built-in, service operations on electric/electronic components are easier. The architecture developed is compatible with various user interface solutions (control arrangement, information allocation and display method). CAN structure (CONTROLLER AREA NETWORK) The electric/electronic systems in the FLORENCE network exchange information by communicating via three physically separate networks known as B-CAN low speed, C-CAN high speed and I-CAN network. The latter is used solely to exchange information between the TV tuner node and CONNECT. The data to be shared by the B-CAN and C-CAN networks are managed by the Body Computer that is equipped with both interfaces and acts as a network gateway. The Body Computer transfers information from the B-CAN category network (low speed) to the C-CAN category network (high speed) and vice versa. Transfer may take place in two ways: directly: i.e. the entire message is copied to the other network exactly as it is; indirectly: with this type of data transfer, the Gateway composes a message for the target network out of the various source messages. One or more messages received from the source network are broken down, the various signals they contain are recomposed in a new message and then sent to the target network. The Gateway function is active only when the system is in KEY-ON mode The physical medium used for automotive CAN networks is double copper electrical cable type, where one wire is associated with a higher voltage level than the other. By convention, the wire associate with the higher voltage level is indicated by: H Can for the C-Can network, A can for the B-Can network (Can L). By convention, the wire associate with the lower voltage level is indicated by: L Can for the C-Can network, B Can for the B-Can network, In order to transfer and receive information, all electrical/electronic units are connected to the network by means of switching interfaces built into the electronic units that are known as transceivers. Binary The language of the electronic units is binary - compatible with the electronic circuits (high low) (open closed etc.): to transmit information, data must therefore be handled in accordance with specific codes. Various codes have therefore been developed to meet all requirements. One of the most common codes is ASCII (American Standard Code for Information Interchange). This alphanumerical code uses coded groups of bits. It is able to represent the 26 letters of the English alphabet plus the ten decimal numbers in addition to punctuation marks and instruction commands. ASCII is an eight bit binary code. Seven bits are used to code information and the eighth is used to check errors. By using seven bits per character, it is posible to code no fewer than 128 information including decimal numbers, upper and lower case letters of the alphabet, punctuation marks etc. Once the numbmer of bits making up a word (i.e. the word length) has been fixed by a data code, this number must not be altered. A group of eight bits is called a byte and represents 256 values: this number is obtained by testing all possible combinations of (0) and (1) in the eight positions availalbe per byte, for example 00000001, 00001111, 11111111 etc. The numbmer 256 (2 exp. 8) can be used to represent the set of alphabetical characters, punctuation marks, accented or special characters etc. In effect, therefore, a single byte may represent a number, a letter of the alphabet, a punctuation mark or a special character. The byte is used as a unit of measure in saved data quantities and memory device storage capacity. As with any unit of measure, bytes are also defined as multiple amounts: 1 kilobyte (kb) = 1024 bytes = 2 exp. 10 (210) 1 megabyte (Mb) = 1024 kb (about one million bytes) = 2 exp. 20 (220) 1 gigabyte (Mb) = 1024 kb (about one billion bytes) = 2 exp. 30 (230) 1 terabyte (Mb) = 1024 Gb (about one trillion bytes) = 2 exp. 40 (240) Analogue: "Linear" electronics is the term applied to analogue effects, i.e. effects that are proportional and continuous. A water tap is an example of an analogue switch. This is because it can used to shut off the water flow completely, turn the flow to maximum and also obtain all the other intermediate positions that occur on the continuum between the closed state and the fully open state. The Tester mobile coil instrument is also analogue: the pointer may indicate the measurement position from zero to full scale deflection, by moving continuously along the entire graduated scale and passing through all the points on its way. Digital: Digital electronic, on the other hand, denotes progress by discrete quantities in quantifiable steps. A light switch is an example of digital operation because the only possible statuses are well-defined and distinct. In this case there are two: on and off, with no intermediate positions. In practice, a digital gauge (whether it operates using warning lights or numbers) increases in steps. It is not possible to determine, for example, the exact level of a fluid between a stage when one warning light on the level gauge is lit and the next is still turned off. The sensitivity is therefore one step, i.e. the interval between one warning light and the next. The reading is, however, precise and non-subjective. It is possible to interpose a series of steps between one warning light and the next containing an equal number of warning lights and so on until the discrete measurement steps can practically be equated with the continuous line of an analogue instrument. The similarity is, however, more apparent than real because each step on the digital guage, however small, determines a well-defined position and represents an unequivocable value. Above all, it is not subject to parallalax or interpolation reading errors. To sum up, the sensitivity of a digital instrument is equivalent to that of an analogue instrument but the reading accuracy is always higher. OPERATION OF MULTIPLEXING NETWORK The designer of the Florence system allocated control functions to the Body Computer. The additional Body Computer functions allow it to provide information on: network activities status; operational failure status of individual electronic units (nodes); a possible CAN fault. The Body Computer Node is given the task of "waking up" the network when the ignition key is turned on. In the case of a fault in the NBC, the Instrument Panel Node (NQS) is given the task of waking up the network. The NQS cuts in only if it is not woken up by the Body Computer after a certain length of time with the ignition key. This prevents network conflicts All the the "Node" electronic units process the various signals from associated sensors for individual management purposes and also to manage other control units. On latest-generation electrical systems, the number of electronic unit that are interconnected, and thus the number of data packages that need to be handled, is very high. For this reason, one or more CAN networks are used in these systems. Compared to conventional wiring, these allow more effective information exchange between the various electronic units. The physical medium used for the B- CAN (low transmission speed) network is double copper electric wire (not necessarily twisted), whle the wires in the C-CAN (high transmission speed) network must be twisted. In this case, one of the two wires is associated with a high level (H) and the other with a low level (L). The BUS CAN signals are differential, i.e. the value allocated to the bits is represented by the difference between voltage levels of CAN (H) and CAN (L). To sum up, the combined use of two wires and differential signals allow data packages to be exchanged between different control units on the CAN network. This is even possible in the presence of electromagnetic interference. Transmission and exchange of data on the respective B- CAN and C- CAN networks and the transfer of data between the lower speed network and the high speed network and vice versa takes place in the Body Computer node (gateway function). The message issued to a CAN network (multiplexing) by an electronic unit or node is known as a "raster" (data package). It takes the form of a series of pulses, as mentioned previously (known as bits) that take the value (1) or (0). This denotes the presence of absence of a transmitted signal. Before the analogue rpm sensor signals can be used by the electronic unit microprocessor, they must be amplified if they are weak (when ring gear speed is low or tooth number is low) and converted to digital signals by the trigger circuit. The binary counter than numbers them; one pulse for each tooth. To prevent the numbering continuing to infinity, a time signal (clock) produced by a transistorised circuit goverened by a quartz crystal resets the count to zero each second and then begins again. Because the number of ring gear teeth is known, the crankshaft speed of rotation can be calculated. If a ring gear has 240 teeth and turns at 1000 rpm, in one second the following number of teeth will pass in front of the sensor (1000 x 240: 60 = 4000 teeth) corresponding to 4000 pulses. If a binary counter accumulates 4000 pulses (bits) in one second, crankshaft speed is 1000 rpm. If more than 4000 bits are accumulated, the speed will be higher than 1000. The rpm signal reduced to digital form is one of the many information items used by microprocessor (7) to process data. By using a program stored in the control unit memories, the microprocessor is able to convert the results of its processing into signals that are used as input for the working circuits: ignition point, current intensity and duration in the coils, operation of the injectors or supply of other actuators designed for various functions. Because this signal is destined to be used by other nodes, the engine control unit makes it available on the C-CAN network via its CAN node. In practice, the control unit converts the rpm signal into binary numbers, the only ones that can be analysed by the microprocessor: they are then forwarded to the CAN controller (10), whose task is to prepare a raster (data package) made up of several blocks or fields (contained between a beginning and an end) that contain a series of information to be sent to other nodes. The task of the final interface, the CAN transceiver (11) is to decode the raster and send it on the BUS network. In practice, it receives from the controller a series of pulses referred to as bits of value one (1) zero (0) that determine voltage levels that are dominant or recessive for the entire time that the node is transmitting. All other nodes that receive the raster correctly confirm reception on the BUS. All receiving nodes also carry out a test to find out whether the raster (message) affects them. Nodes that find the data in the raster to be of significance accept it and process it. Otherwise they ignore it. Communication protocol Circulation or transmission of a message known as a frame or data package on a multiplexing network (B-CAN and C-AN network) is possible only if a transmission protocol is adopted. This the set of rules that allows the exchange of data and controls between two or more electronic units (control units or, better still, nodes). 1 - Frame 2 - Blocks A - Identifies the beginning of transmission or start of a new frame (START OF FRAME. SOF) consists of 1 dominant bit and indicates to all other interfaced nodes that they must synchronise with this SOF bit (awake the BUS that may be in stand by). B - Iidentifier marks and identifies the message content. Also contains information on message recipients. Arbitrage of transmitted frames is carried out in this field. This means that the indentifier code allows frame content and priority allocated by the network architect to be uniquely identified. (the lower the identification number, the higher the priority) C - Control field indicates frame or message structure D - Data to be trasmitted (may be orders or information to be transmitted) E - Control field; allows a check to be run that the data transmitted are unaltered (message validity). The node or nodes that detect the presence of an error first issue a series of dominant warning bits. The transmitting node eliminates the message and emits a new frame after a certain time lapse. F- Reception confirmation. All receiving nodes that use the message and detect the correct sequence from the transmission node (recessive bit) overwrite the recessive bit with a dominant bit. In this way, the transmitting node is assured that the message has been received correctly by at least one recipient. Each node checks the incoming frame. If the frame is relevant to the node, it accepts and processes it. Otherwise it ignores it. G - End of frame, message over. The end of frame allows the network (BUS) to switch to IDLE status (unless a node begins a new transmission to the network. FRAME FORMAT Priority management (Superimposition or collision of non-destructive frame) The Florence system protocol allows superimposition problems to be handled when several nodes need to emit a frame simultaneously. Each control unit possesses an identification code that also expresses its priority. In practice, when a node (control unit) expresses its intention to transmit a frame on the network (BUS) by means of its initial bit and another node (control unit) simultaneously carries out the same operation, because both read (as well as transmit) the signals emitted by the network, the node that detects a difference between the emitted signal and the received signal detects that another node is emitting a higher priority frame. The node that transmits the lower priority message immediately interrupts its transmission and makes way for the node that is transmitting a higher priority message. In practice, the high priority message is sent to the network without any interruption or delay. Naturally, the control units (nodes) that intended to transmit messages with lower priority must suspend transmission to become receivers and then re-attempt to send the frame when transmission is complete. This non-destructive superimposition is regulated by bit arbitrage. One bit is called the dominant bit and allocated a value of zero (0) while the other bit is known as a recessive bit and its value is equal to one (1). The higher priority frame gains the right to be transmitted on the BUS. A dominant level (0) always takes precedence over a recessive level (1). Serial line operating principles Transmission protocol Circulation or transmission of data packages on serial lines is possible only if a transmission protocol is adopted. this is a set of rules that allows the exchange of data and commands between various electronic units (control units or nodes). Each control unit connected to a serial network is identified by a unique address that is inserted in the package to identify the recipient. Data packages are transmitted from a transmitting control unit to a receiving unit, i.e. transmission is one-way. This operation is carried out by sending a question package, which is followed by a response package. Data package format The data package format (A) is unique and includes the two following main parts: outcome (C): represents confirmation of reception and execution of a command by the control unit to which it is sent A - Package B - Command ESI - Outcome. T - Time within which the control unit send the outcome The outcome is sent within sufficient time to end before T time elapses (value of time T is: T=10±1ms). Command format A frame (1) consists of several blocks (2) or fields: 1 - Frame 2 - Block A - 1 byte identifies the start of data transmission B - address of the receiving control unit (ECU) is entered B - address of the sending control unit (ECU) is entered D - identifies the command sent E - identifies the command data F1- F2...Fn - sequence of all data associated with the command G - Checksum (CKS) Part of the command contains a set of information expressed in bytes, namely: Section A (HDR): this is the first byte of package and is used to identify the beginning of the transmission. This is used to wake up and synchronise the other control units and prepare them to begin receiving the data or information package. Section B (RECIPIENT) or “recipient indicator”: used to identify the control unit to which the data package is destined. It is possible to identify up to 63 control units connected on the line: each control unit is allocated a different address to ensure that data package transfer is unique. Address allocation is set by the network architect. Section C (MITT) sender control unit address: identifies the control unit sending the command. Section D (CMD) data to be transmitted: identifies a command sent on a serial line. It is possible to identify up to 255 different commands that may travel on the network. The command list is set by the network architect. Section E (NBD) number of command data bytes: identifies the number of bytes in the data relating to the command sent (CMD) on the serial line. Each command can be associated with up to 255 data bytes that make up the parameters. The values that may be assumed by each command are set by the network architect. Section F1-F2…FN, identifies the (NBD) sequence associated with the command. Section G (CKS) or CHECKSUM is verification of correct data package reception. This is calculated as the sum of all data package bytes (from HDR to FN). Outcome format Once the data package has been received, the receiving control unit sends the outcome to the transmitting unit within a very specific time (T=10±1ms) to bring data pckage exchange to a close. The outcome may assume the following configurations: ACK command recognised and carried out NACK command not recognised NAP command not applicable The outcome consists of a byte organised as follows: Bit 7 Bit 6 Bit 5 Bit 4 Bit 3 Bit 2 Bit 1 Bit 0 ESI_1 ESI_0 ECU ECU ECU ECU ECU ECU BIT 5, BIT 4, BIT 3 - BIT 2, BIT 1, BIT 0 identify the address of the receiving control unit (ECU). The value of bit 7 and 6 identifies the true outcome. ACK (ESI_1=0 ESI_0=0): command is recognised and executed. The control unit responds ACK if the following conditions are satisfied: the command can be executed by the control unit (it is one of its commands) the control unit has executed the command. NACK (ESI_1=0 ESI_0=1): command not recognised. The control unit responds NACK if it has not received the command sent correctly (CKS incorrect). NAP (ESI_1=1 ESI_0=0): command not applicable. The control unit responds NAP if the following conditions are satisfied: the command has been correctly received (CKS correct) The command can be carried out by the control unit (it is one of its commands) but cannot be executed with the control unit in its current status or the command cannot be executed by the control unit (it is not one of its commands). The combination ESI_1=1 ESI_0=1 is not allowed for. The other six bits (from BIT 6 to BIT 0) identify the address of the receiving control unit with reference to the command. In this way, it is possible to address up to 64 control units. Serial line statuses During system operation, the serial line assumes two different statuses: FREE LINE: identifies rest status or free status of serial line, i.e. absence of transmission on the line The control unit may begin a transmission under these circumstances. LINE ENGAGED: identifes situation where a transmission is in progress on the line. Under these circumstances, each control unit (except the transmitting control unit) switches to listening mode and remains in this mode to the end of the data package. Access to the line Two or more control units may begin to send information simultaneously. This simultaneous access may give rise to conflict on the line. Transmission conflict During transmission, the control units check whether each individual byte making up the data package has been sent correctly on the line. In practice, they compare to see whether what they have sent is the same as what they have simultaneously read on the line. If the result of comparison is negative, a transmission conflict occurs. The transmission conflict immediately interrupts transmission of the data package. Under these circumstances, the control untis immediately stop using the line for a set time period (programmed) to ensure all the other control units detect the interruption of the data package. Once this time has elapsed, the transmitting control units consider the line to be free again and gain access to it for transmission using the priority mechanism. Priority access Each control unit is allocated an access priority code that determines the sequence in which the control units will gain access to the line after detected a conflict. (the priorities are established by the network architect). In practice: the control unit (node) that is preparing to transmit expresses its intention to the other control units (nodes) by means of an intial bit. If two control units (nodes) carry out this operation simultaneously, they do not realise immediately. As soon as a transmitting control unit (node) detects a dominant symbol on the BUS, however, it immediately suspends transmission of lower priority messages to make way for the control unit (node) sending the higher priority message. In practice, the high priority message is sent to the network without any interruption or delay. The control units (nodes) that intended to send lower priority messages naturally stop sending and become receivers. They re-attempt to send their messages when transmission is complete. Access to the line following conflict obeys the following rules: the control unit waits for a certain time (to be programmed) from the movment when conflict takes place and declares the line to be free. once free line status has been established, the control unit waits for a further time period (that alters according to the priority code) before gaining access to the line. Line free status is not a precursor to the beginning of transmission but is the condition that activates priority access and in turn transmission. Transmission is carried out firstly by the control unit with the highest priority code, which takes control of the line to prevent further conflict. The other control units with lower priority codes that gave rise to the conflict thus set themselves to listening mode. Once the data package has been transmitted, they re-attempt access to the line to send the data package that was interrupted previously. Package transmission Package transmission begins with an HDR byte (first byte of the command package used to wake up and synchronise the control units) and continues with the command contents: each control unit connected to the network sets itself to listening mode and finds out whether the package is addressed to itself by means of the DEST byte. Each control unit in stand-by mode that identifies a package not addressed to itself remains in stand-by mode to the end of the package (ESI included) so that the line is not engaged. At the end of command transmission, the receiving control unit processes the command and sends the command outcome. OUTCOME - YES/ OUTCOME- NO The outcome is sent within sufficient time to end before T time elapses T=10±1ms). If an outcome is not sent, the package is not properly completed. Therefore: the control unit that sent the command: has not received the outcome (has not responded or has received NACK) treats the command sent as not executed and re-attempts to send the command twice. It does not repeat the command if it receives NAP as an outcome. the other control units consider the data package to have ended once the time within which the outcome is sent has elapsed (T+10±1ms). From that moment, they can use the line again to send new data packages. Example of data transmission. A - Package format B - Command: represents the information sent by a control unit and contains a command and the relevant parameters/data ESI - Outcome: represents confirmation of reception and execution of a command by the control unit to which it is sent D - Line free T - Time (ms) within which the outcome must be sent Ta - Time instant as a consequence of which a control unit with higher priority access will take control of the line to prevent new conflict. Features of A-BUS serial line STAND-BY MODE A stand-by mode is included so that several control units (even if not directly involved in command exchange) can use information sent on the A-BUS serial line. In stand-by mode, the control units read the data and information packages travelling along the line but do not send an outcome (NAP, NACK, ACK) at the end of the package. They may, however, check its validity by means of the package checksum. A-BUS DEVICES FAULT DIAGNOSIS Devices interconnected via the A-BUS line are able to carry out self-diagnosis upon the request of any control unit connected to the line. Following self-diagnosis, the devices communicate the result to the requesting control unit by means of a command followed by a certain number of associated bytes that contain the actual outcome.
