At the end of the display cycle the NAVIGATION information is restored and a reduced size fault symbol reappears in the area of the display dedicated to showing symbols. If the ACC function is activated, the display logic depends on the fault priority: a - Priority 0, the ACC information disappears definitively and is replaced by the fault display cycle or by the fault symbol only if the ESCAPE button is pressed. If the ACC system communicates "braking power limit" information, the display of the ACC function, complete with the "Brake in safety" message is automatically suggested again (the duration of the display is established by the NAC - Adapative Cruise Control Node). At the end of this display, the warning cycle (or the symbol only) for the fault in progress is shown. b - Priority 2, the ACC information is interrupted and the fault display cycle takes its place (tot. At the end of the display cycle (tot. 20 secs. of if the ESCAPE button is pressed) the ACC information is restored. If there is a priority 1 fault, the main ACC information is displayed in the top area of the zone and the fault symbol remains in the centre area. If there is a priority 2 fault, the fault symbol is summarized, in a reduced size, in the area of the display dedicated to showing symbols, whilst the display of the ACC function returns to being the default one. If, during the 20 seconds that the fault message is displayed, the ACC system needs to communicate the following information: "braking power limit" "functional limits reached" the display of the ACC function is automatically suggested again with the corresponding messages: "Brake in safety" (duration of the display established by the NAC) "ACC OFF" or "ACC not activated" (duration of the display 5 seconds) At the end of the display of the "ACC OFF" or "ACC not activated" messages the fault warning cycle previously in progress continues until it is terminated. If faults occur in the sub-systems (Braking/Engine management/VDC/Automatic transmission), the ACC system is deactivated and the following are displayed, in order: the screen for the fault in progress and the screen notifying the customer of the ACC deactivation stage, in rolling mode; the standard screen (or the one activated prior to the activation of the ACC). The warning message that the SPEED LIMIT has been exceeded is always displayed with a buzzer. The DOOR OPEN information is signalled synchronized with the vent, in other words the display is activated immediately as soon as one or more doors is opened and remains open until all the doors of the vehicle are properly shut. If faults (of any priority) are in the process of being displayed, the DOORS OPEN information is displayed in rolling mode with the other screens. Second level priority: ACC/navigation When the ACC function is activated, the display of all messages corresponding to the functions activated by the centre console (e.g. radio, climate control, telephone, etc.) is inhibited . However, the display of messages corresponding to the following functions (which can be activated using the special buttons on the steering wheel) remains activated: navigation system telephone radio Information coming from the outside is also displayed in relation to the telephone functions (e.g.: incoming SMS messages, incoming calls, etc.) . One of these pieces of information should be displayed on the same screen as the ACC primary information. If, during the display of these messages, the ACC system notifies of changes such as "the presence of an obstacle along the route" or "locking onto a vehicle and following it", they are signalled in a reduced format in the area dedicated to the ACC primary information. The corresponding symbols are as follows: "presence of an obstacle": shape of a car (1); "tracking": same shape with red outline; the tracking mode is not specified (2). If one of the following events occurs during the simultaneous display of the ACC and one of the other functions: Braking power limit ("Brake in safety" screen) Functional limits reaches ("ACC OFF" screen) only the ACC information is displayed on the above mentioned screens. If the ACC and NAVI functions are activated on a vehicle with manual transmission, if it is necessary to communicate both "gear change suggestion" and "presence of an obstacle" information at the same time, then these two pieces of information alternate every 0.5 seconds in a rolling format. STANDARD DISPLAY The functions in the standard display are: outside temperature reading (1) time (2) DISPLAY AT KEY-ON Petrol Versions The check stage starts at the key-on and the message "DIAGNOSIS IN PROGRESS" and the icon of the vehicle are displayed with a (microsoft effect) enlargement lens to give an idea of the function in progress (dynamic display for 4 seconds) (1). At the end of the check stage, if: it concludes with a positive outcome, the engine speed is above 704 rpm for at least 1.53 secs. from the moment this level is reached the SERVICE messages, if present, are displayed and should persist for a time of t = 5 seconds (2). the "OK" message + car symbol should appear and remain for 3 secs. (3). If, after 4 seconds have elapsed and the check stage has concluded with a positive outcome, but the engine has not been started up, the standard screen will appear. Diesel Versions The check stage starts at the key-on and the message "DIAGNOSIS IN PROGRESS" + the heater plugs symbol + the icon of the vehicle are displayed with a moving lens to give an idea of the function in progress (dynamic display for 2 seconds) (4). The heater plugs symbol persists until the end of the pre-heating stage, the "oil level" information is displayed after two seconds and remains for 5 secs. (5). At the end of the 5 seconds, in the same way as for petrol versions, either the OK screen or the standard screen is displayed depending on whether or not the engine has been started up. Diesel and Petrol Versions If the check stage highlights faults, then they are displayed as described in the "Display of faults" chapter. If cases of "insufficient engine oil pressure" and/or "inertia switch on" are verified during the diagnostic cycle then they are displayed immediately, whilst in the case of all other faults (priority 0, 1 and/or 2), the "DIAGNOSIS IN PROGRESS" screen is displayed first and then the display cycle for the fault detected. In these cases the display logic for the diagnostic stage is lost and once the fault display cycle is over the standard screen is shown. On vehicles equipped with "Vehicle Protection Systems", if there are messages on the state of the system (a message + an appropriate symbol), then their display takes place at the end of the check stage and lasts for 10 seconds; at the end of this display the matrix shows the standard screen directly whilst the "OK" screen is not displayed. Information relating to the TELEPHONE functions, lighting adjustment, voice recording and ACC functions is displayed, if necessary, during the entire check stage. DISPLAY OF ENGINE OIL LEVEL SIGNAL [F017] The display, at the key-on, of the engine oil information, lasting 5 seconds, includes the "engine oil level" message in the top part of the display whilst the amount of oil in the engine is represented, in the lower part of the display, by six "bars" lighting up/going out (bargraph). The maximum oil level is represented by all the "bars" on (1). The gradually switching off of the "bars" indicates a decreasing oil level. If it is not possible to read the engine oil information as a result of the battery voltage being too low, the value displayed previously is suggested. If the oil level is below the minimum level, the "bars" are all switched off. In this case, the following messages are shown, in order, for 20 secs.: "minimum oil level" + empty bars + insufficient oil level symbol in the special warning light area, accompanied by a buzzer (3 secs.) "insufficient engine oil level - switch off the engine do not continue" (2 secs.) (2) If the oil level is above the maximum level, the "bars" will all be lit up and the "maximum oil level" message + bars will be displayed (3). If there is a break or a short circuit in the detection circuit at the key-on, the "engine oil level sensor failure" message will be displayed for 20 secs (4). DISPLAY OF VEHICLE PROTECTION SYSTEM INFORMATION [F001-F322-F326] The information relating to the "VEHICLE PROTECTION SYSTEM" consists of instructions for the driver or fault messages. Instructions for the driver The display of instructions for the driver concerning the "Vehicle Protection System" takes place at the end of the key-on cycle and lasts 10 seconds. The screen consists of the "Vehicle protection system failure" symbol plus the appropriate message. The possible messages are: REMOTE CONTROL BATTERY RUN DOWN ELECTRONIC KEY BATTERY RUN DOWN BREAK IN ATTEMPT ELECTRONIC KEY NOT RECOGNIZED These indications are displayed, if necessary, for 10 seconds after the key-on cycle. There are no connected acoustic warnings and, if the condition persists, they are put forward again at the next key-on (always after the diagnostic cycle). For vehicles with the key-less go system, in order to remind the driver of the automatic activation of the steering lock, the following screen is displayed for 3 seconds after the key-off. Fault messages The display of faults involving the "Vehicle Protection System" is managed in the same way as for ordinary faults. The screen consists of the "Vehicle protection system failure" symbol plus the appropriate message. The faults displayed at the key-on according to the logic described in the CODE chapter are: ALARM FAILURE SYSTEM NOT PROGRAMMED FAILURE AND SYSTEM NOT PROGRAMMED VEHICLE PROTECTION SYSTEM FAILURE In addition, for vehicles with the key-less go system, in order to warn the driver that the system no longer detects the presence of the CID and therefore if the engine is switched off the vehicle can no longer be started up again, a rolling code lasting 20 seconds is displayed followed by the ideogram illustrated with the message: KEY NO LONGER PRESENT IN THE VEHICLE There is also a buzzer as well at the same time as the display of messages for all the faults listed above. DISPLAY OF ICE DANGER SIGNAL [F192] In order to warn the driver that there may be ice on the road, if the outside temperature is £ 3°C and the engine speed is above 704 RPM, the temperature reading is displayed (flashing - frequency 1 Hz d.c. 50% ON), plus the "snow symbol" + the message "warning danger of ice" for 10 seconds. There is also a buzzer at the same time as the display of the message. At the end of the warning cycle: the message disappears, the temperature reading stops flashing the small sized "snow symbol" is shown in the specially dedicated area of the display (as long as the condition T £ 6°C persists) and the screen prior to the event is put forward. This display only takes one after the outside temperature is recognized to be T £ 3°C and is only repeated if the temperature reaches the value T ³ 6°C and then returns again to T £ 3°C. The "snow symbol" disappears when T > 6°C. If the outside temperature at the key-on is T £ 3° C, then the display shows the entire diagnostic cycle at the key-on and later on it initiates the "warning cycle" described above. During the "DANGER OF ICE" warning cycle the temperature reading does not vary even if the information sent by the climate control unit has changed in the meantime. If the "warning cycle" is interrupted by a fault message (greater priority), the above fault is not seen through to the end. DISPLAY OF LIGHT DIMMER ADJUSTMENT FUNCTION [F041] The brightness of the panel and all the controls that are lit up can be adjusted using the dimmer to the left of the panel in the light panel. The brightness can never be reduced to zero The dimming value (0-10) is transmitted by the NQS via the B-CAN to allow the brightness value to be sent to the other Nodes. If the side lights are deacivated, then the display lighting is 100% and it can be adjusted (dimmed) (high line only). The failure signal LEDs cannot be adjusted/dimmed If the brightness is being adjusted, the message "Control brightness adjustment" is shown in the top part of the active matrix display whilst the lower section shows a histogram with "bars" lighting up/going out one at a time. This screen remains for 5 seconds after the dimmer is adjusted and after this the previous screen is displayed. During the display of fault information (with the exception of "DANGER OF ICE"), the display lighting cannot be adjusted and the brightness level remains at 100%. The dimmer is activated to adjust the brightness of the Instrument Panel and other components on the vehicle. The "CONTROL BRIGHTNESS ADJUSTMENT" screen, is not, however, shown on the display. Brightness adjustment table The relation which governs the connection between the level of brightness and the bars shown on the display is defined in the table below: Number of bars visible Brightness in % Note 1 2,5 minimum brightness > 0 2 5 3 10 4 15 5 20 6 25 7 40 8 55 9 70 10 85 11 100 maximum brightness Behaviour at the key-on: at the key-on with the +lights on, the graph is always lit up at the adjusted light level. Behaviour at the key-off: at the key-off the adjustment value set is memorized and used for the next key-on. Disconnecting the battery or resetting the system does not cause the memory to be lost. When the battery is connected the value set should be the one adjusted prior to the disconnection of the battery. DISPLAY OF SPEED LIMIT FUNCTION [F141] It is possible to set a speed limit (between 30 ÷ 250 km/h in steps of 5 km/h) which, if exceeded, activates the following procedure: The symbol and "speed limit exceeded" message are displayed and the warning screen is displayed in rolling mode accompanied by a buzzer for 10 seconds. The symbol contains the speed limit set/exceeded. When the warning cycle is over the message disappears whilst the symbol remains and only disappears when the speed of the vehicle goes lower than 5 km/h below the speed limit set. This procedure is carried out once after the speed limit is exceeded and can only be repeated if the speed of the vehicle goes at least 5 km/h below the speed limit set and then goes above the speed limit once again. The speed limit is set usint the NIT, but the programming, processing and display of the exceeding of this limit takes place in the NQS. V - Vehicle speed Vlim - Speed limit set by the driver A - Signalling of speed limit exceeded B - message + symbol + buzzer - For example having set a limit of 120 km/h On versions destined for Arab countries, the speed limit is fixed at 120 km/h and cannot be changed by the driver. DISPLAY OF DOORS OPEN FUNCTION [F091] The DOORS OPEN information is signalled synchronized with the vent, in other words the display is activated immediately as soon as one or more doors is opened and remains open until all the doors of the vehicle are properly shut. In the case of DOORS OPEN there is a buzzer and the screen (1) appears on the display. If one or more doors is found to be open during the diagnostic stage at the key-on, the cycle of screens continues as usual, whilst a small "DOORS OPEN" symbol (warning light) is shown on the display without an additional specific message on the state of the doors (2). At the end of the diagnostic cycle, if the DOORS OPEN state persists, the screen for this case is displayed (2D/3D symbol + "DOORS OPEN" message). If, however, the DOORS OPEN state is verified during the diagnostic cycle and the speed of the vehicle is above 4 km/h, then the "DOORS OPEN" screen is displayed immediately. In the case of a key-on with the engine not started up, the DOORS OPEN information is not displayed. If only the boot is open, a specific screen is displayed for 10 seconds after which it is shown in a reduced size in the dedicated warning lights area (3). DISPLAY OF TYRE PRESSURE FUNCTION [F135] All displays are accompanied by a buzzer. System not programmed If the Tyre Inflation Pressure Control Unit has not been programmed, the following information screen appears. 20 seconds after the "SYSTEM NOT PROGRAMMED" screen has been displayed, the previous screen with the icon symbol is put forward again. Insufficient pressure When the Instrument Panel receives the signal from the Tyre Inflation Pressure Control Unit that the pressure in one or more of the tyres is below the recommended value, the following screens are displayed in rolling mode for a total of 20 secs. (1). When this cycle is over the following symbol is displayed in the dedicated warning lights area until the correct inflation pressure is restored. The warning cycle is repeated after 10 minutes (once). The complete cycle is repeated at the next key-on if the inflation pressure is not correct (2). System failure This type of display takes place in the following cases: presence of a fault in the control unit circuit and/or wiring; no signal received from one or more sensors; TPMS control unit faulty; Tyre punctured When the Instrument Panel receives the signal from the Tyre Inflation Pressure Control Unit that the pressure in one or more of the tyres is below the alarm level, the following screens are displayed in rolling mode for a total of 20 secs. When this cycle is over the symbol is displayed in the dedicated warning lights area as in the case of insufficient pressure until the fault is corrected. Following a key-off and then a key-on, if the fault is still present, the instrument panel displays the cycle again indicating the REMAINING RANGE (in km) (1). During a "punctured tyre" state, if the speed of the vehicle exceeds 80 km/h, or if more than 200 km is travelled (maximum distance) then one of the following warning cycles is displayed in accordance with the logic for priority 0 faults (2). DISPLAY OF CLOCK FUNCTION [F162] The display of the time in hours and minutes is shown in both the panel active matrix and the CONNECT display. The values are automatically updated by the CONNECT If there are irregularities as a result of problems with the signal between the CONNECT and the Instrument Panel then dashes (-:-) are shown in place of the time DISPLAY OF OUTSIDE TEMPERATURE INFORMATION [F192] The display of the temperature is shown in both the panel active matrix and the CONNECT display. If there are irregularities as a result of problems with the signal between the CONNECT and the Instrument Panel then dashes (-:-) are shown in place of the temperature expressed in °C or °F DISPLAY OF AUDIO FUNCTION INFORMATION [F155] The following information is displayed with the function activated (an operation that can be carried out using the CONNECT and selecting one of the following sources CD/TAPE/RADIO/CD Changer): radio station information (RDS mesage is available or frequency of station selected) TAPE activated function message (TAPE symbol) with the direction of play, rewinding, fast forward shown. CD function activated message (CD symbol) with the name (if available) and/or the number of the CD selected (by CD - Changer) and the track selected. If the CD function is requested and there is no CD, the message "NO CD" will be shown. DISPLAY OF NAVIGATOR FUNCTION INFORMATION [F176] The following items/information are displayed with the function activated depending on the settings made using the CONNECT: navigation pictograms distance in metres from the next manoeuvre, the possible values are: 2000, 1000, 500, 400, 300, 200, 100, 50, 40, 30, 20, 10 (metres) name of the road about to be entered / name of the road being driven along. Since this information is provided by the CONNECT, if the information about the names of the roads is too long to be displayed on a single line in the display panel, then this information is cut to the last character that can be shown on the active matrix display line. DISPLAY OF TELEPHONE FUNCTION INFORMATION [F209] The following items/information are displayed with the function activated depending on the settings made using the CONNECT: last number dialled (timed screen) last numbers or names dialled (if in the directory, one at a time) telephone directory (internal and/or on SIM card, one name at a time) telephone number being selected or name (if in the directory) telephone number (1) of person being called or name (2) (if in the directory) warning of a second incoming call When a call is being sent, the screen with the name of the person being called appears on the display. This screen is not timed, but remains visible until there is an answer or until the user stops the call using the TELEPHONE OFF function. The same logic applies in the case of an incoming call: the "INCOMING CALL" screen remains on the display until the call is answered or until the person making the call decides to cut it off. DISPLAY OF VOICE BOX FUNCTION INFORMATION [F270] With the function activated (an operation that can be carried out using the CONNECT) it is possible to record messages in the Voice Box with the following screen appearing on the display: This screen is not timed, but remains there for the entire period of the recording (maximum time - 3 minutes). WARNING OF "SMS (SHORT MESSAGE)" BEING RECEIVED [F209] A symbol + an "Incoming message" message is displayed for 10 secs. than the previous screen is displayed with the addition of the "SMS" symbol in the warning lights dedicated area. The message has to be reade using the CONNECT DISPLAY OF PLANNED MAINTENANCE FUNCTION INFORMATION [F269] In order to provide the user with information concerning servicing, the active matrix display in the panel shows a series of messages at each key-on. The "SERVICE DUE IN" message is followed by the number of "kilometres" or "days" until the vehicle is due for a service. There are 9 services in the Planned Maintenance Programme as follows: Service Time Schedule 1 After 20,000 km or one year from purchase 2 After 20,000 km or one year from 1st service 3 After 20,000 km or one year from 2nd service 4 After 20,000 km or one year from 3rd service 5 After 20,000 km or one year from 4th service 6 After 20,000 km or one year from 5th service 7 After 20,000 km or one year from 6th service 8 After 20,000 km or one year from 7th service 9 After 20,000 km or one year from 8th service Service information is supplied in "km" or "days" depending on which is due first (the one excludes the other until the next time). The starting information for the "mileage" is 20,000 km and is set by the supplier of the instrument panel. The starting information for the "days" is 365 days (1 year) and is automatically set by the panel when the total mileage reached is 201 km. The message is displayed directly the first time and only at the key-on when: 1 - the mileage until the next service is equal to or less than 2000 km 2 - there are 30 or less days until the next service Later on the message is only displayed once at the key-on when the value is equal to or less than: 1800, 1600, 1400, 1200, 1000, 800, 600, 400, 200, 100, 50 km . 27, 24, 21, 18, 15, 12, 9, 6, 3 days From the moment the value of 0 km / 0 days is reached, the following messages are displayed again at the key-on: 3 "PLANNED MAINTENANCE DUE - 0 km" 4 "PLANNED MAINTENANCE DUE - 0 days". At each service interval, the Service personnel should: reset the "km" counter and the "days" counter to the starting vlues (20,000 km and 365 days) using the diagnostic equipment. memorize that the service has been carried out, giving the date of the service, service no., total mileage. If the instrument panel is being replaced, the Service personnel should: restore the mileage from the milometer of the panel being replaced on the new panel read the number of services carried out and enter them into the new panel read the mileage/days on the old panel until the next service and enter them into the new panel. DISPLAY OF NEED TO REFILL WITH FUEL INFORMATION [F002] If the fuel level is low, in other words in the "reserve" condition, in addition to the warning light in the panel coming on the relevant message and symbol appear in the display accompanied by a buzzer after which the screen prior to the signal is restored. DISPLAY OF INERTIA SWITCH ON INFORMATION [F005] If the inertia switch is operated, the panel displays the relevant message (1) and symbol accompanied by a buzzer. There is no second image to produce a rolling logic for the display, likewise there is no timed period of 20 seconds: the image remains on constantly in the display unless the user presses the ESCAPE button. The summary symbol (2) is only shown after pressing the ESCAPE button. DISPLAY OF CRUISE CONTROL FUNCTION INFORMATION [F025] When the CC system is activated the display shows the "cruise control on" message and the relevant symbol (1): This screen remains for 5 secs, after which the screen with the cruise control symbol in the top left corner reappears (2). This is valid for all screens that allow the display of this symbol, something which, for example, does not take place in the case of faults (3), where the entire display must be available for this information. DISPLAY OF ADAPTIVE CRUISE CONTROL FUNCTION INFORMATION [F026] When the ACC system is activated the display shows the "cruise control on" message and the relevant symbol (1): This screen remains for 5 secs, after which the screen with the ACC symbol in the top left corner reappears (2). Whilst the system is operating the following information is displayed: Read out (3) of the "speed currently set" Read out (4) of the "presence of an obstacle" in the driving path Read out (5) of "tracking vehicle in front" and driving style selected (headway) Indication (6) of "suggested gear change" (flashing) if there is no automatic or robotized transmission Indication (7) of "system failure state" (in the warning light display area) indication (8) of the ACC system "not ready" following manoeuvres by the driver that are not compatible with the activation of the system (e.g. reverse gear engaged). DISPLAY OF FOLLOW ME FUNCTION [F048] This function is only enabled (with the main beam headlamps off) for a period of 2 minutes after the key-off. During this period of time the side lights and the dipped headlamps can be switched on using the steering column switch unit if the "flasher" position. Each impulse of the steering column switch unit corresponds to a lighting period of 30 seconds and the maximum number of impulses is 7 (maximum period of 210 seconds). The following is shown on the display: "follow me" function message activated the lighting period (in secs) set using the steering column switch unit (number of impulses x 30 seconds) The FOLLOW ME screen is displayed for 20 seconds. If the left or right parking lights function is activated, then the FOLLOW ME HOME function has priority.

INTRODUCTION The instrument panel is inside the B-CAN and is called the NQS (Instrument Panel Node). The task of the NQS is to display the vehicle operating parameters and to notify the driver of any possible faults in the on-board electronic systems. The signals coming from the systems/nodes in the C-CAN are made available to the NQS by the Body Computer Node by means of an interface, known as a Gateway, which has the function of allowing the exchange of information between the two CANs with different operating specifications. The panel comes in one version only which differs according to the engine type and features the following: a negative transreflexive anti-glare type LCD (i.e. during the day it exploits the natural daylight and at night the backlighting maximizes the contrast between the light figures on a dark background) which has the function of a milometer and, on versions with an ACC device or automatic transmission, which has the function of displaying the recommended gear or the gear engaged, respectively. an active matrix reconfigurable colour display. 1 - Coolant temperature gauge 2 - Speed indicator 3 - Active matrix reconfigurable display (for repetition of CONNECT information) 4 - Rpm indicator 5 - Fuel level gauge 6 - Fuel consumption gauge 7 - Operating warning lights 8 - LCD (milometer/automatic transmission gear) 9 - Direction indicator warning lights 1 - 18 pin connector 2 - Inverter 3 - Speaker The rear view is illustrated below. The panel lighting takes advantage of electro-luminescence, in other words the capacity of some materials to light up if an electric current passes through them. The brightness is adjusted by a dimmer that has nine positions and is located to the left of the instrument panel in the lighting control panel. The instrument panel receives information, via the B-CAN line, about the fuel level of the tank capacity expressed in % points calculated by the NBC and this information is then represented by a pointer moved by a stepping motor. Fuel level strategy The Lancia Thesis adopts a strategy designed to ensure that the fuel level reading on the instrument panel is strictly correlated to the mass of fuel actually present in the tank and not affected by: fuel slopping (during vehicle operation) any vehicle manoeuvre or position during normal service/parking (errors due to parking on slopes, steps etc.) It also ensures that refuelling/fuel loss will be correctly identified. The body computer implements this strategy (see table ) by comparing: a signal representing the last fuel level reading on the instrument panel, stored immediately before the vehicle engine was last turned off (signal A) a fuel level signal from the tank sensor a few seconds after the vehicle was last turned off (signal B) a signal from the tank at the time the vehicle is turned on (signal C) Omissions or incorrect download of the 3 signals by the body computer may lead to an incorrect reading on the instrument panel until the next time the car is refuelled (i.e. when at least 10 l of fuel are added to the tank). This situation may occur, for example, when repairs are carried out on the body computer without respecting the rule of disconnecting the battery at the beginning of the operation and reconnecting it when the work on electrical/electronic components is complete. It is therefore important to observe this procedure scrupulously. In any case, if the customer complains that the fuel level gauge is malfunctioning, before doing anything else, disconnect the battery and then reconnect after 10 seconds with the body computer properly connected, as described in the operating procedures. If the battery negative terminal is disconnected, notify the customer that this operation could lead to the My Car custom settings being lost before proceeding. The reading ordered on the instrument panel by the body computer upon vehicle ignition will conform to the value of these signals as indicated in the following table. Gauge/warning light behaviour at the key-on Ton = Temperature reading at key-on. Toff = Temperature reading corresponding to the gauge position at the key-off (which usually corresponds to the actual temperature reading at the key-off). The temperature reading is always guaranteed even in electrical operating limit conditions (9/16V). Temperature warning light and indicator operating logic Operating logic for engine coolant temperature gauge in normal operating conditions I = Scale reading T = Temperature A - Gauge operation by instrument panel B - Warning light operation by c.c.m. C - Start of scale D - Centre of scale E - Start of red sector F - End of scale For temperatures of T £ 50 °C, the pointer should be at the first reference on the scale (start of scale). For temperatures between 50 ÷ 80 °C the pointer should increase in a linear fashion. For temperatures between 80 ÷ 100 °C (normal operation), the pointer should remain in a stable position in the centre of the scale. For temperatures between 100 ÷ 120 °C (uphill) and between 115 ÷ 100 °C (downhill) the pointer should move in a linear fashion. For temperatures of T = 120 ± 1 °C, the pointer should be located at the beginning of the red sector of the scale. For temperatures of T ³ 122 °C the pointer should reach the position corresponding to the beginning of the red sector and, as soon as the engine management control unit sends the warning light on signal, it should be positioned at the end of the scale (t = 1 s); the engine coolant temperature overheating warning light should come on at the same time. In addition: if the warning light on signal coming from the c.c.m. remains in the ON state, the pointer should remain at the end of the scale and the warning light should remain on; if the c.c.m sends the warning light off signal (when the temperature goes below the level usually equal to T = 115 ± 1°C), the instrument panel should instantly switch the coolant overheating warning light off and the pointer should place itself (t = 1 s) in the position corresponding to the (actual) temperature value measured. There is a hysteresis of 5 °C, in other words, for example, the warning light is switched on at 120°C, it is switched off at 115 °C. Engine coolant overheating warning light The panel receives the information that the warning light is switched on/off via the B-CAN line. The software strategy that regulates the switching on/off of the engine coolant overheating warning light and the operation of the pointer in the end of scale position when the temperature levels/limits are reached, both in normal operation and if there is a burst of heat, is contained inside the engine management control unit. Error conditions/diagnosis The instrument panel warning light is activated at each key-on (check stage); after 4 secs. the CCM/NCM sends the panel the command to switch the warning light off. During this check stage the behaviour of the gauge should be as defined in the previous paragraph ("gauge behaviour at key-on"). Through the effect of the warning light coming on, the pointer is not in the end of scale position during the check stage. If the warning light on conditions were present at the key-on (engine coolant temperature overheating and warning light already on at the previous key-off), the c.c.m. keeps the command to switch the warning light on activated and the instrument panel continues to keep the warning light in an ON state and places the pointer in the end of scale position. The mileage covered is shown in an LCD which on some versions also shows the recommended gear or the gear engaged. The display lighting is green and there is an SMD LED. The LCD has 6 digits (with 7 segments for each digit) for the total reading and 4 digits plus a decimal point for the trip reading. Insignificant zeros are not displayed in order to reduce the numbers shown to the important ones only. Pressing the "Escape" button (outside the NQS) for longer than 2 seconds zeroes the trip meter, but not the milometer and the messages on the display are not cancelled neither is the Service mileage. If the same button is pressed for between 50 ms and 2 seconds, this activates the "ESCAPE" function cancelling the messages on the activated matrix. The instrument memorizes the total mileage so that if the battery is disconnected (+30) not more than +/- 1km is lost whilst the total trip meter memory is lost. When the instrument is delivered to the assembly factory the milometer can only be zeroed once within the first 200 km. The possibility of carrying out this zeroing is indicated on the LCD by the letter "H" at the first digit (with 7 segments) on the left of the milometer. If the operation described previously is carried out before 200 km is reached, then the milometer is zeroed and the letter H disappears. If this operation is not carried out, when 200 km is reached/exceeded, the letter H disappears and the mileage is displayed with no possiblity of zeroing the milometer any more. The instrument allows the programming of the total number of km (if it is replaced) on condition that the figure entered is higher than the last value memorized When the maximum mileage is reached on the milometer (699999 km), it is not zeroed but horizontal bars/dashes are displayed. When the trip meter reaches 999.9 Km, it returns to 0.0 With the ignition switched off, nothing is shown on the display; in this case the "ESCAPE" button has no function, when one of the front doors (left/right) is opened/closed the milometer will light up and display the trip meter and total mileage information for about 10 seconds. Warning lights Specifications The warning lights can be switched on or off by the NQS via a command from the B-CAN, for the systems that are connected to the C-CAN the messages are made available at the B-CAN via the NBC gateway or for the direct management of the component connected to the NQS. The warning lights usually come on when there is a fault, but some warning lights also come on at the key-on for less than 4 secs. to indicate the check on the system to which they are connected. "Intelligent" type warning lights are only used for the AIR BAG system failure warning light. The circuit is as follows: A = Towards the control unit The warning lights in the instrument panel are grouped together in the following families: Dedicated warning lights (ABS, VDC, AIR BAG, BRAKE FLUID, EPB) i.e. specific for a single type of information Shared warning lights (EBD, ASR) i.e. shared for several types of information There is a further division that can be made according to the management of the actual warning light, depending on whether it is controlled via the CAN (Body Computer), directly by the NQS or directly by the control unit (DISCRETE) controlling the device to which the warning light refers. The warning lights can also be identified according to the characteristics linked to the check function, in other words there are warning lights whose LED is checked at the key-on and others which are not subject to this check. FM Radio transmission frequency with wavelengths between 8705 and 108 MHz GPS (Global Positioning System) The GPS (Global Positioning System) is a consellation of satellites that orbit the earth transmitting time and position information at every point on the earth 24 hours a day. This information may be received and used by a special GPS receiver. The purpose of the system is to allow all users to establish their individual position on the earth’s surface. The GPS satellite constellation consists of 24 satellites arranged over 6 orbital planes that are angled at 60 to the equator at an average distance of 20,000 km, with an orbital period of about 12 hours. The system was developed for military purposes by the US Defence Ministry. It guarantees an overall, continuous positioning service. A portion of the system is also allocated for civilian use. Three satellites are required to detect a two dimensional position (longitude and latitude) while information on altitude can also be received with a fourth satellite. GSM Communications standard for mobile communication devices (GSM = Global System for Mobile Communication), currently distributed in about 90 countries. Benefits from excellent territorial coverage. This includes information, communication, audio/video and climate control system programming functions (for a description of climate control functions). Il CONNECT Nav +. is equipped with a front panel connected to the main electronic unit. This includes a multifunction display and a series of control buttons used to activate the individual functions. CONNECT Nav + allows a more rational approach to vehicle controls. It allows the driver a more relaxed drive and makes it easier to operate the controls. The system is fitted in the middle of the facia and may be used easily by the driver and passenger. It includes the following systems/services: radio, with tape player and CD player/changer; TV tuner; trip computer; check control display; GSM radio phone wiht voice recognition module; voice mail navigation system. vehicle set-up (door open/close programming, seat position adjustment/store, supplementary heater system programming, parking brake mechanism etc.) 1 - Connect module 2 - Speakers 3 - GPS/GSM aerial 4 - Steering wheel controls (opt) 5 - CDC (opt) 6 - BOSE subwoofer (opt) 7 - Handsfree microphone 8 - AUDIO amplifier 9 - Radio/TV aerials The Info Telematic Node manages the following tasks: receives and sends information on the B-CAN line (e.g.: diagnosis, warning lights, controls, data) adds commands for interaction with the various menus manages a high definition colour display for navigation or TV connects with facia wiring for connection to the vehicle electrical system connects with communications wiring for point/point connection of TV tuner , rear TV camera, video cassette player set-up for connection with components such as DVD, rear multivideo screens etc. interfaces with GPS, GSM and radio aerials by means of coaxial leads The infotelematic node features a thermal protection function that restricts its operation as internal temperature increases. This prevents permanent damage to the system. The system is fully operational for interior temperatures lower than 85 °C. Because normal system operation gives rise to a temperature increase of 20 °C despite a cooling fan in the rear of the NIT, the system interior reaches a limit temperature that leads to deactivation with a passenger compartment temperature of about 65 °C. Self-diagnosis The system comes with a self-diagnostic function that checks whether the NIT unit is correctly connected to all external components. Access to self-diagnostic mode is achieved by pressing the "MAIN" button (1) for at least 10 seconds. The following components/signals can be diagnosed by means of this function: External signal amplifier "Coolant level low" signal [F010] "Window washer level low" signal [F011] +15 signal [F040] Exterior lighting sensor activation level signal [F044] NIT buttons [F153] CD changer [F156] Microphone [F160] Aerial, phone module and SIM GSM card reader [F166] TV tuner and aerial series [F172] GPS receiver and aerial [F174] CD reader and navigation CD [F174] Telephone handset Speakers Infrared remote control (IR) Radio aerial EOL test mode is used to check whether the NIT unit has been connected to all exterior components following system installation on the vehicle. It is not therefore necessary to carry out an operation test on the finished system. Entering test mode Press the MAIN button for at least 10 seconds to enter EOL test mode. Two different test modes may be selected on the main test mode page. The menu opens at the status page, i.e. the first menu item, upon access to EOL test mode. Exiting test mode The system returns to normal mode if no test page is selected for 10 seconds. Test mode is also abandoned if vehicle speed exceeds 7 km/h. If vehicle speed is lower than this threshold, test mode may be abandoned only from the main diagnosis page. This is done by pressing the exit button or waiting for the time period mentioned previously to elapse. Visual representation of test results In test mode, these take the form of a limited number of instructions in text format. Positive or negative test outcomes are indicated by means of colour (green or red). Symbols for tests that may not or must not be carried out yet (e.g. button test) are indicated in yellow. Tests that cannot be carried out automatically (e.g. TV tuner) must be confirmed manually. The person who carries out the tests must press the "passed" or "failed" test button in this case. Storing test results Test results must be stored in a non-volatile memory so that they can be read by the tester at a later stage. Test mode exit date and time are also stored if valid date and time data are available and at least one test procedure has been carried out in the current test mode cycle. Display impementation In test mode, the display may not be turned on or off on the basis of ignition key position. Status page The status page displays all tests that may be carried out automatically. It also shows signal status depending on exterior component availability. e.g. CD changer, TV tuner, telecommunications unit. External signal amplifier The status page shows feedback signal status. This indicates whether the car is fitted with a low or high range sound system (BOSE). Coolant level too low signal [F010] The status page displays a "low coolant level" signal status, that is transferred from the interface processor to the main processor. Screen washer fluid level too low signal [F011] The status page displays a "low screeen washer fluid level" signal status, that is transferred from the interface processor to the main processor. +15 signal [F040] The status page displays ignition signal status. The display and background lighting cannot be deactivated when the signal is turned off. Exterior light sensor activation level signal [F044] The status page displays selected activation level in the form of a number of steps (1, 2, 3) and measured voltage level. This is transferred from the interface processor to the main processor. NIT buttons [F153] This test can be used to test all hard buttons and the two rotary knows on the NIT unit To simplify the test, a button test page on the display displays button and rotary knob symbols. If these buttons pass the manual depression or rotation tests successfully, the symbol colour changes from yellow to green to indicate the function is OK. If the buttons and knobs are not all detected within 30 seconds, the undetected buttons are marked as defective (in red). The connection between NIT and CCA units passes the test if it is possible to enter test mode. CD changer [F156] The test status page indicates whether a CD changer is available and whether the test CD inserted can be accessed. To test connection L, the first sound track of the inserted CD is played when the soft "play" button is pressed. Microphone [F160] The microphone function is tested by recording a short utterance of 4 seconds maximum duration and playing it back after a short pause. While the test utterance is recorded, the person carrying out the test must keep the soft button depressed. If maximum recording time is exceeded, the recording will stop. Playback begins shortly after the recording button has been pressed. Aerial, phone module and SIM GSM card reader [F166] The aerial, phone module and SIM GSM card reader are checked jointly by carrying out a recording test with a GSM network. A SIM card must be inserted in the card reader before the test begins. If the SIM card reader cannot access the SIM card, the SIM card test is recorded as a failure. The symbol colour changes from yellow to red. The same thing happens if it cannot log onto the GSM network within 60 seconds. GPS receiver and aerial [F174] The status page displays the GPS aerial connection. An error message is displayed if the main processor cannot access a GPS receiver. CD Player and navigations CDs [F174] The NIT unit attempts to read some files on the CD containing the navigation database. The result indicates whether access to the CD play and data files was successful. Insert navigation CD before starting this test. Telephone handset To carry out this test, lift the phone handset and then press some number keys and the "call set" button. This call request is suppressed in diagnosis mode. The screen displays phone handset status (replaced or lifted) and the number dialled. Phone handset cable LF line status can be checked only by attempting to make a phone call through the handset. It is not possible to switch the phone handset microphone directly to the audio amplifier. Simple connection test: the connection between phone handset and NIT unit can be checked by lifting the phone handset, i.e. taking it off the hook; phone handset status is indicated on the display. Speakers Check the coils of all connected speakers to run a full check on the sound system speakers. Both sound systems come with 4 corner speakers and 1 subwoofer. The top-of-the-range sound system also comes with a central speaker. In the case of the bottom-of-the-range amplifier, this test requires a sequence of 9 steps, i.e. 4 x (tweeter + midwoofer) + 1 x subwoofer. In the case of the top-of-the-range amplifier, this test requires a sequence of 10 steps, i.e. 4 x (tweeter + midwoofer) + 1 x subwoofer + 1 x central speaker. Corner speakers: the tweeter test is carried out at 10 kHz. the midwoofer test is carried out at 500 kHz. Subwoofer: the test is carried out by simultaneous application of 80 Hz to all 4 channels. Central speaker: the test is carried out by simultaneous application of 1500 Hz to the two front channels. The tested coil is indicated on the display. If the test signal is not audible, the person carrying out the test must press a soft button with the indication "Error". The relevant coil symbol will go red. Otherwise it must go green. Test signal amplitude is programmed by the NIT supplier. If an internal sound module amplifier channel is deactivated due to a short circuit, the screen indicates this by turning the symbol of the relevant corner speaker to red. Simple connection test: a sound signal (e.g. white noise) lasting 1.5 seconds followed by a pause is sent to all four audio channels in sequence. The screen indicates which channel is being tested. If the test signal is not audible, the person carrying out the test must press a soft button with the indication "Error". The relevant coil symbol will go red. Otherwise it must go green. it is not possible to detect open connections of internal amplifier outputs. the NIT unit cannot detect short-circuits in electrical connections between the external amplifier and speakers. Infrared remote control (IR) The test carried out on infrared (IR) remote control buttons is similar to that run on NIT unit buttons: each remote control unit button is displayed on the screen as a symbol. If the button pressed is detected by the NIT unit, the relevant symbol colour changes from yellow to green. If a button is detected, the infrared (IR) connection incicator switches from yellow to green. If the buttons have not all been detected within 30 seconds, the symbols are marked as defective (i.e. red). Simple operation test: to check whether the NIT unit is receiving an infrared (IR) signal, only one button need be pressed. Radio aerial The NIT unit automatically activates the radio and tunes it to a set frequency. The signal intensity is compared with a minimum set level. If the result exceeds this level, the aerial passes the connection test. COMPOSITION General remarks The system communicates with the user by means of a multifunction display used by all systems/components making up the CONNECT system. Acoustic instructions (e.g. for the navigation system) are supplied via the front radio system speakers. The system includes certain internal components and monitors various external components. The main components of the CONNECT system are a control panel (CCA), central unit (NIT) and climate control system panels at front (standard) and rear (optional). The CCA and NIT units may be subdivided into several internal components. A diagram and short list of the main internal and external components of the full multimedia system are shown below. Basic information is also given for each module/component. Components that may be requested as options for each specification level are indicated in the following diagram with OPT A - NIT central unit A1 - CC audio module A2 - CD audio module (Navigation + audio) A4 - Voice Recognition module A3 - GSM module + SIM card reader B - Microphone C - Phone handset (OPT) D - CD changer OPT) E - DSP/low-range amplfier F - DSP/Top-range amplifier (Bose) to replace DSO/Low-range amplifier (OPT) G - Climate control system rear panel (OPT) H - TV tuner (OPT) I - Body Computer L - CCA front panel L1 - Infrared remote control M - Front climate control system panel N - Telematic unit (OPT) (*) O - Amplifier/Diversity aerials FM P - Infrared receiver (*) Future application Multifunction display The video consists of a module with a lighting unit built into the front panel. The video consists of an active matrix colour LCD (TFT technology) measuring 7 inches, with the following technical specifications: resolution, 234 pixels vertically by 480 pixels horizontally (active area: 153.4 mm x 86.4 mm) and RGB (red, green, blue) in row configuration; analogue RGB interface (true color); backlit at 350 cd/m2 with two cold cathode bulbs; surfaces with scratch-resistant antiglare coating; contrast, minimum value 50:1. Two possible display settings can be used to optimise visibility by the user: the first is used for daytime operation. The lighting level is set automatically on the basis of environmental light levels detected by a phototransistor located next to the display. the second, for operation with side lights on. With this setting, the brightness level is adjusted as on other on-board instruments. Function screens The display shows the various screens relating to primary and secondary system functions (refer to the User Manual for user instructions). A function screen is a specific menu that appears on the screen. This provides information to the NIT (Info Telematic Node) on current system status and/or subfunctions that can be selected from the menu or by keys. Main system functions are described below. General remarks A function screen is made up of several parts: a function menu, softkey labels, selection cursor, status bar, identifier (title) of function screen (secondary), a list, icons, point graphics, control boxes, control buttons Function menu (1) The menu consists of several system subfunctions, each of which constitutes a menu item (known also as a selectable item or menu option). The menu may also be defined as a set of all available options relating to a selected function. Each option consistutes a menu item or a selectable item. Softkey labels (2) Each one corresponds to the name of a system subfunction that may be called up (activated) with the corresponding key. Activatable functions are marked by labels containing bigger, brighter characters than non-activatable functions. Selection cursor (3) The cursor takes the form of a coloured rectangle. It may be moved using the JOG key to select a certain menu item or by pressing one of the soft keys (e.g. the key used to change the radio station). The cursor may be in selection mode (only the rectangle outline is coloured) or in highlighted mode (the entire rectangle is coloured). Status bar (4) This is the first row at the top when the screen of a primary function is displayed. This status bar normally shows the time, outside temperature and audio source in operation at a given moment. According to system status, some information supplied by the system must also be displayed on this status bar. Screen title (5) Refers to the function selected/activated in the screen relating to a secondary function. Virtual connection line (6) This line connects the JOG to the menu items, or a selected menu item to another item or another option that represents an item on the list. Check box (7) This is part of the menu and indicates the status of a selected function: the function is off or deactivated if not marked by a cross; the function is on or active when marked by a cross. Telematic module events table. SYSTEM OPERATING STATES During operation, the system will be in one of the following status modes from the user viewpoint. Turned on by means of ignition key (synchronous) The synchronous operating mode is activated by measn of an NIT command. In his mode, system activation and deactivation is linked to ignition key status (Key_ON) - (Key_OFF). If the system is turned off by pressing the knob before key-OFF, the system stays off at the next key-ON. Turned on by button Normal operating mode, available after the user has pressed the rotary volume knob. System activation by pushing the button is possible only after deactivation by means of the ignition key (Key_OFF). Stand-by The display and audio output are off. Some functions (e.g. the positioning function) still continue to remain active in the background. To gain access to stand-by mode, press the rotary volume knob while the system is active and the ignition key is in ON position. Off Complete system deactivation. EXTREME SYSTEM OPERATING CONDITIONS Processor load management Process load is high following simultanous activation of voice recognition, map display and route calculation functions. The CONNECT system guarantees that this does not give rise to unexpected results by managing priorities. The system does not show any reaction, except a time lag for functions with lower priority. The priority sequence is as follows: voice recognition, map display, route calculation. Minimum voltage condition - The system operates without any restrictions within a range between 10 and 16 V. Between 7 and 10 V, system operation may be reduced while the CAN functions are not subject to any limitation. Below 7 V, the system could turn off but this does not interfere with the CAN bus. In the interval between 7 and 10 V, the system enters into a mode similar to STAND-BY. This means that the display backlighting and radio module are deactivated and keypad events (apart from IR remote controls and steering wheel controls) are ignored. If the ignition key is in ON position, the system abandons STAND-BY mode when battery voltage again exceeds 10V. If the ignition key is in OFF position (the system has been reactivated by pressing the On/Off button), the system goes off, e.g. it enters the OFF mode. The system does not save data in its non-volatile memory if supply voltage drops below 10V. Excess tension condition In the interval between 16 and 23 V, the system is disconnected from the battery voltage by means of a hardware switch. The system is again connected to battery voltage when the voltage drops below the overvoltage limit. The overvoltage condition takes the form of a normal battery disconnection. All unsaved information, e.g. user configurations, GPS almanac etc. are lost. Minimum temperature condition The system operates up to a minimum environmental temperature of -30 °C. It is, however, possible for certain internal components to deactivate if their temperature limits differ from this value. These are, in particular, the CD, CC, GSM module and display. A special management system is therefore adopted in cases of low temperature. Components are turned off on the basis of temperature limits, evaluated temperature and temperature of the nearest sensor. The system is not designed to operate at temperatures below -40 °C. If the system is reactivated (e.g. via CAN or a heater remote control), and a temperature of lower than -40 °C is measured, the system is turned off again. External components (particularly the supplementary vehicle heater) may not therefore be turned on if the measured temperature is lower than the system limit. In this case, the system cannot be restarted for the next 5 mintes. This feature allows the system to attempt to restore the temperature to operational levels. Excessive temperature condition The system limit environment temperature is +65 °C, since the internal temperature is some 20 °C higher, the system is able to withstand a temperature of 85 °C. Within a range between +70 °C e +85 °C, the display is dimmed in linear manner from 100% to 20%. Within this temperature interval, the GSM module reduces its transmission capacity. If the system deactivates due to excessive temperature, it cannot be reactivated for the next 5 minutes. This feature allows the system to cool to within the normal operating temperature interval. PRIORITY MANAGEMENT NIT unit priority management affects incoming and outgoing visual and acoustic sources. The concept is based on the following rules. 1. Three priority levels are present: emergency (level 1), urgent (level 2), normal (level 3), 2. Components do not alter priority as a result of external or internal conditions. A function cannot, however, be executed via voice control as long as a phone conversation is in progress (point 11). 3. Outputs are classified on the basis of content and not source. For example, a traffic warning message will take priority regardless of source (TMC or telematic unit). 4. Information or dialogue windows have a minimum display time of 2 seconds. During this period, they cannot be relaced even by messages with higher priority. This is to prevent the display from flashing. 5. Elements with different priorities that are located in different, non-overlapping areas of the screen will not block one another. An icon with higher priority located inside a status line will not therefore affect the display of a window displaying lower priority information in the middle of the screen as long as the relevant visual areas do not overlap. 6. If a component is associated with a visual output and an acoustic output other than a buzzer, each is allocated a different priority. If a resource (acoustic or visual channel) is occupied, the two outputs do not occur simultaneously. In this case, the component output corresponds onlly to the resource, which may be allocated on the basis of a priority table. This rule affects controls relating to manoeuvres and changes of context. The priority subdivision is indicated in the table below. 7. If an item needs an acoustic channel to indicate a visual output (e.g. a buzzer indicates a warning message), this waits until both resources are available to ensure a synchronised output. 8. With the exception of emergency calls and medical support, the user can change the context at any time (e.g. from the main page to the phone page) by pressing one of the hard buttons. 9. Items activated by the user are usually higher priority than items activated from the outside. 10. A phone call is always higher priority than a manoeuvre-related command. 11. During phone calls, it is not possible to carry out certain voice recognition actions. 12. The user may program the mix of sounds generated by built-in audio chips, with the audio source active at that moment. It is not, however, possible to mix sounds that are not generated by an audio chip (e.g. phone rings) with the audio source. These sounds bring about attenuation of the audio source. 13. The user may activate one single entertainment source (radio, CC, CDD, CDC, TV) at a time. This source may be interrrupted or suppressed (e.g. by mixing) by a higher priority source on the basis of the priority table shown below. 14. Traffic information obtained by means of a telematic information source (TMC or Viasat) are graded into 3 different priority categories. high (e.g. driving on wrong side of road), normal (e.g. traffic congestion along the route) and low (e.g. general information). 15. The dark operating mode is deactivated if it is superseded, for example, by a change of context. 16. Any conflict relating to command input sources is resolved on the basis of the following list (from high priority to low priority): remote control on the steering wheel, voice command NIT unit hard buttons, NIT unit soft buttons, NIT unit menu items, remote control.
