them next time the set is turned on. The volume may be adjusted within a range that is subdivided into 50 steps. The volume settings is common to FM, AM, CD, CDC, CC and TV. A special volume adjustment is reserved for traffic announcements, telephone and navigation system messages. For navigation messages, the active sound source volume is reduced by a fixed quantity equivalent to 10 volume steps. It is also possible to activate/deactivate the possibility of selecting 5 different values for volume adjustment on the basis of speed (SDV). Volume limitation upon start-up The NIT unit limits the volume to a presettable maximum value upon activation in order not to disorientate the user. If the volume is adjusted to a value higher than the maximum level when it is turned off, it is set to the programmed value next time the set is turned on. Sound level Sound level can be activated and deactivated (MUTE) by means of a selector by activating the specific field (1) from the NIT page in AUDIO mode. When the volume is low, the system automatically increases the intensity of bass and treble sounds for RADIO/CD/CC/TV entertainment sources only. Bass/treble The bass and treble level is adjustable from - 12 to + 12 in 25 steps. Treble and bass selection values are saved individually for each RADIO, CD, CC and TV entertainment source. When the set is turned off, the settings are saved and then called up the next time the set is turned on. For sources such as TA, phone and navigation system, the bass and treble levels are automatically adjusted to a neutral setting. Fade/Balance Fade and Balance controls are adjustable through 31 steps (from -15 to +15). The Fade and Balance setting applies to all entertainment sources. If the phone is activated, Fade and Balance are set to predefined values that cannot be altered by the user. The previous values are called up again when the phone is deactivated. When TA is activated, fade and balance levels selected at that time are used. These settings can be adjusted while TA is active. The information sources (driving tips) mixed with the front entertainment source channel are not influenced by fade and balance settings. These may be modified when the information source is active, but affect only the entertainment source. Deactivation due to voltage drops When voltage drops below 10V, the audio unit saves its current status and deactivates. As soon as the voltage re-stabilises, the audio unit reactivates automatically with the previous settings. Audio source selection Types of audio source In the CONNECT system, AUDIO sources may be categorised by dividing them into entertainment sources and information sources that may be selected via softkeys (2). The entertainment sources, some of which are options and may not be fitted, are as follows: Radio Tuner Audio CD player CD Changer Tape Player TV programme tuner The information sources, always present, are as follows: Phone Traffic announcements (TA) Driving advice (navigation) User voice command request/confirmation (voice recognition) Information source selection rules Information souces may be mixed with front audio channels (in the case of driving advice) or replace the entertainment source (in the case of announcements relating to traffic, phone, voice recognition dialogue manager and acoustic signals). If an information source has access to audio channels, i.e. if it mixes with or replaces the entertainment source, its volume may be adjusted by means of the volume control knob for as long as it remains active. These volume level changes are not saved permanently. The entertainment source volume level may not be altered for as long as an information source is active. If several information sources are activated simultaneously, the situation is controlled by the priority management function as described previously. Automatic activation of entertainment sources When tape or CD is inserted in the CD and CC player, these are automatically selected as active entertainment sources. When any of the information sources is active, the automatically selected entertainment source may become a background source. The entertainment source is reactivated only when the information source ends and no other requests are pending. Mixing voice commands with sources Navigation module voice commands are distributed through the front speakers. In this case, the entertainment source volume is reduced by a fixed amount equivalent to 10 volume steps in relation to the configured navigation volume. As described previously, as long as the information source is actie, the driving advice volume may be adjusted by turning the volume knob without the entertainment source background volume being altered. The user is free to decide whether to broadcast the driving advice through the left audio channel, the right channel or both. Radio transmission receiver Bands The radio receiver is configured to operate in Europe. It manages the following bands: FM, MW and LW. Upper and lower frequency limits and relevant step sizes are listed in the following table: Band Frequency interval Tuning/search step amplitude FM From 87.5 to 108.0 100 / 100 kHz MW From 531 to 1602 kHz 9 / 9 kHz LW From 153 to 279 kHz 1 / 1 kHz Stations The receiver is able to store 30 stations, divided as follows: 6 FM-AS, 2 x 6 FM (FM-A/FM-B), 6 MW 6 LW Current band and station The receiver comes with a band referred to as a "current" band for temporary storage of the selection made by the user. Similarly, the receiver stores a current station/frequency for each band available. This feature means that the system returns to the last selection set for a particular band when changing from one band to another. Station selection When the recall button is pressed for less than 3 seconds, a stored station is recalled. This operation modifies the current station/frequency. If the station has been stored with RDS active and a PSN was available, the PSN is immediately displayed. If the station was stored with RDS deactivated, the stored station frequency is re-loaded while the RDS function is disabled and some AF check is carried out. If a local station without alternative frequencies is called up while the RDS function is enabled, the stored station frequency is reloaded. The RDS function is activated if it was previously deactivated. The station recall continues until an exact PI is decoded. If synchronisation is not achieved within 6 seconds, the PSN recalled and displayed is replaced by the frequency value and no new station is scanned. If another PI code is decoded on this frequency, the new RDS station is used and this will be stored in automatic mode. Frequency selection Frequency may be altered by means of a rotary encoder within the selected band. This operaration modifies the current station/frequency. If frequency is selected directly (i.e. manually), the RD and TP functions are deactivated and the receiver enters frequency mode. Scanning higher frequencies When this function is used, the system searches for the next station up from the current frequency. If the upper edge of the frequency band is reached, the receiver skips to the lower edge of the band. Search mode stops when: it is suspended by the user, the signal level of a station satisfies the preset threshold (programmable at EOL), the initial frequency is reached again. The search is not started if it is detected that the car is driving through a tunnel. If the RDS is enabled, the next station in the list of stations inside the receiver is selected (RAI MF1 - > RAI MF2 - > RAI MF3). RDS stations are then given priority, but non-RDS stations must also be detected at the end. If TP mode is also active, only TP stations are selected. If the RDS function is disabled, the receiver tunes to the next good-quality station within the frequency band. Scanning lower frequencies When this function is used, the system searches for the next station down from the current frequency. The system behaves in the same way as for the "Scanning higher frequencies" function (described above) except the search is downward. If the lower edge of the frequency band is reached, the receiver skips to the upper edge of the band. Introductory scanning towards higher frequencies When this function is used, the system searches for the next station up from the current frequency. All stations are broadcast for 3 seconds, then the search is resumed from the next station. Introductory upward scanning mode is suspended: if the user presses any button, if the starting frequency is reached again. The new selected station becomes the current station if the function is suspended. The new selected station becomes the current station if the function is suspended. If TP mode is also active, only TP stations are selected. If the RDS function is disabled, the receiver searches up within the frequency band to find good quality stations. If TP mode is active, the system tunes only to TP stations. Non-RDS stations are also accepted. AM bands behave in the same way as FM bands with the RDS function deactivated. The receiver audio is suppressed during the search. The active search mode is shown on the display. Introductory scanning towards lower frequencies The system behaves in the same way as with "Introductory scanning toward higher frequencies" (described above), except the search direction is downward instead of upward. Storing current station The current radio station is stored by pressing the recall button for at least 3 seconds. Alternatively, this function may be carried out by means of a voice command: the user must specify the storage position by means of a number. The user receives confirmation that a station has been stored by means of a short acoustic signal ("received beep") or by means of a short volume drop. PSN and RDS and TP function statuses (on or off) are stored together with the stations. If the PSN is scrolled, the PSN displayed at the time when the user presses the station button is stored. RDS mode is set to off when a non-RDS station is stored. TP selected mode (on or off) is stored together with the station and reset when called up. Automatic store The automatic store function stores the 6 strongest stations corresponding to FM-AS recall buttons. The automatic storage function is not active in AM bands. When the automatic storage function is started, the FM-AS band is selected automatically. The automatic storage function starts from the lower edge of the FM band and ends at the top edge. RDS stations take precedence over FM station. During the automatic storage process, the display shows the frequency. As soon as a PSN is available, this must be displayed instead of the frequency. Broadcasting chains are grouped together if the first element of a chain of stations (e.g. in the case of the RAI MF1, RAI MF2, RAI MF3, …, chain, the first element is RAI MF1) is one of the strongest stations, this station is defined as station number 1. Example: The 6 strongest stations are Pi Code PSN Fs [db?V] 5214 DEEJAY 50 5203 RAI MF3 49 5201 RAI MF1 48 5202 RAI MF2 47 5353 GEMINI 46 5404 RAI MF4 45 - The automatic storage order is No. Pi Code PSN Fs [db?V] 1 5201 RAI MF1 48 2 5202 RAI MF2 47 3 5203 RAI MF3 49 4 5404 RAI MF4 45 5 5214 DEEJAY 50 6 5353 GEMINI 46 RAI chain stations are grouped. The first of the RAI stations (Pi 0x5201 code) is put in first place. The remaining elements are ordered on the basis of their PI code PI (for example DEEJAY 0x5214 is located before GEMINI 0x5353). After automatic storage, the best station is tuned. The automatic storage function takes about 30 seconds. Automatic storage may be interruptd by calling up a station or by means of other interactions with the tuner (e.g. call up of a station and up/down scanning). If it is possible to receive at least 6 stations with sufficient field intensity, the others are not affected. Ignition Upon system activation, the station selected at the time of deactivation is selected. if the last stored station is not available, the first available station after the stored stations is selected. if TP or TMC modes were not selected initially, the receiver takes this into account when selecting a new station. If no station is available in the stored station series, a search is carried out for the next available station using the function "scanning higher frequencies" and taking into account enablement of TP or TMC modes at all times. If no station is available at all, the last stored station is selected. If the car is driven through a tunnel, no search procedure is carried out as long as this condition persists. RDS functions RDS enablement/disablement The functions supported are defined by European RDS standard EN 50067 and is enabled or disabled by the user. RDS functions are available only in the FM band. If the RDS function is disabled or a RDS station that transmits information, the receiver does not use any RDS function (PSN, EON, AF, PTY and TMC). Traffic message channel The NIT unit also allows decoding of TMC information. This may be used for dynamic navigation when made available to the user in text format. If TMC or dynamic route driving via TMC functions are enabled (i.e.the system uses TMC information) and the TMC station weakens, no automatic radio station search is started. The user must selet a new station manually, e.g. by calling up a stored station or starting a station scan. if the new selected station is not a TMC station the user is informed by means of a warning message 20 seconds after station selection. The user is asked to select a new TMC in manual or automatic mode or deactivate the TMC service. Manual selection: A list of all TMC stations that can be received is presented. The user can make a choice from the list. Automatic selection: The TMC station with the highest field intensity is selected from the internal list. TMC service deactivation: If no TMC station is available, the relevant TMC service is deactivated in terms of text display and dynamic navigation and the user is informed by means of a warning message. Traffic programme mode Traffic program mode (TP) is enabled or disabled by the user by means of control (2) from the NIT page in AUDIO mode. If traffic programme mode is enabled and the CC / CD / CDC players are working, when the traffic announcement funciton is activated (TA), the CC / CD / CDC stops and the incoming programme is activated.. When a traffic programe is active, individual programme settings are modifiable and the ser is able to stop the programme at any time. If TP mode is enabled and the selected station weakens (i.e. the signal intensity becomes too low) for a period of at least 30 seconds, the receiver automatically checks to see if another TP programme is available within the entire FM band. If no TP programme is detected, the TP search stops. Otherwise, the receiver automatically selects the next station with a TP signal. The selection starts with a search of stored stations. If no TP stations are found, the receiver searches for a TP station using the "scanning higher frequency" function. If no TP station can be identified using this method either, the frequency to which the set was tuned before beginning the search is re-selected. If the user enables TP mode and the current station is not a TP station, the receiver automatically selects the next station with a TP signal within 6 seconds by means of the procedure described above. If no TP station is detected, the receiver automatically tunes to the station selected before starting the search procedure while the user is informed of the error. TP mode is disabled. Display of programmed station name This function allows the name (PSN) of the programmed station to be displayed, if available. It applies only to FM bands. The PSN is considered valid if successfully received at least twice. If no name is available, the frequency is displayed in place of the PSN. If a station is stored while the RDS function is active (ON), the stored PSN is displayed in the station list. Conversely, if the station is stored while the RDs function is deactivated (OFF), the frequency is displayed in the station list. RDS programme type The RDS (PTY) programme type is selected by means of control (4) from the NIT page in AUDIO mode. This function is used as an RDS station selection filter and allows a particular programme category to be selected from among the options available on the specific submenu. When this function is selected, the radio begins to search from the current frequency and stops if it detects a station with this PTY. If no PTY is detected, the search stops at the frequency from which it started. If a message with PTY 31 code (general emergency situation) is detected, its contents are immediately forwarded. This interrupts all other entertainment sources including phone calls. CC PLAYER The CC player is built into the Audio module and is used to play tapes. Operating modes The tape player can be controlled by means of softkeys in the CC submenu from the AUDIO menu and by means of two hardkeys on the control panel. The following operating modes are available: Pause Play Fast Forward Fast Rewind Scan When the use removes a tape from the player, the player stops. When the user inserts a tape in the player, the player automatically switches to play mode. When the user selects the pause control, the tape player switches to pause mode. The tape player stops during trafic announcements and phone calls. During navigation system announcements, the tape player continues if in play mode and mixing of the two audio sources is managed as described previously. Previous disc and next disc: the presence of empty slots is permitted. Consider, for example, that CDs are inserted in slots 2 and 4. TV TUNER MODE* Main TV functions page The main TV tuner functions page is displayed by pressing the SRC button (1) and selecting the TV mode or directly using the TV multifunction button in the screens where the audio sources are shown at the base of the display (FM - AM - CC - CD -CDC-TV)/ 1 - SRC button 2 - Selector knob 3 - Search / selection button 4 - Search / selection button For safety reasons, the TV tuner video signal is only displayed when the vehicle is stationary (speed below 8 km/h). The audio signal on the other hand is maintained even whilst the vehicle is driving. The main functions are: standard TV; Autostore; Settings TV STANDARD function This function makes it possible to set the standard television for the country you are in. The following alternatives are available: Central European PAL; Italian PAL; GB PAL; Secam East E; Secam France. To set the standard television, select and confirm the TV standard function using the right knob (2), then select and confirm the standard again using the right knob. AUTOSTORE function (automatic programming of transmitters) To activate the Autostore function (automatic memorizing of tranmitters) select it and confirm it using the right knob (2). When this function is activated, the TV tuner automatically stores the 5 transmitters with the strongest signal, for the TV standard set, in decreasing order of signal strength, in its memory. The message "Autostore" will appear on the display during the automatic storage stage. To interrupt the automatic memorizing process, press the "Delete" multifunction button; the TV will tune into the transmitter received before the function was activated. The transmitters tuned into using the Autostore function will be automatically memorized at the preselection buttons (1), (2), (3), (4) and (5). When the memorizing has taken place, the TV will automatically tune into the first transmitter memorized at the preselection button (1). Each station will be stored once only, except in the case of regional broadcasters that could be stored several times under certain circumstances. The behaviour of the equipment whilst the Autostore function is activated is as follows: when the Autostore function is activated all the other functions are disabled; any variation in the volume is not shown on the display; by pressing one of the preselection buttons from 1 to 5 the automatic memorizing process will be interrupted and the broadcaster memorized using this button will be tuned into; to interrupt the automatic memorizing process, press the "Delete" multifunction button; the TV will tune into the transmitter received before the function was activated; pressing the Off multifunction button interrupts the automatic memorizing process and the TV switches off; changing the audio source during the automatic memorizing process does not interrupt the Autostore function. Sometimes the Autostore function may not be able to find 5 stations with strong signals. In this case, only the stations found will be stored.
