The alarm sytem is one of the devices that contributes in protecting the vehicle. AIM The alarm system has the function of protecting the vehicle from unauthorized access, detecting and signalling attempts at intrusion with visual/acoustic warnings. GENERAL DESCRIPTION The alarm system carries out perimeter and volumetric surveillance, surveillance against the vehicle being tilted and surveillance of the supply leads and ignition. The switching on of the alarm system is shown by the direction indicators coming on constantly and a beep from the siren in conjunction with the direction indicators coming on. At this point a deterrent warning light/LED located in each door panel flashes intermittently to indicate the surveillance state. The alarm system is homologated in accordance with directive 95/56/CE and conforms with the requirements of European insurance companies and their associated technical centres. DESCRIPTION OF THE SYSTEM COMPONENTS The basic alarm system components are: Body Computer Node (NBC) Alarm siren Volumetric sensors Tilt sensor Perimeter sensors (door, boot lid and bonnet switches) Transmitter in key-remote control or in CID Body Computer Node (NBC) The NBC is also dedicated to the management of the alarm system. Several functions are also implemented that make it possible to co-ordinate and manage the alarm system sending and receiving commands from the external modules on the A-BUS serial line. Alarm siren The alarm system is equipped with a self-supplied siren. The siren carries out two functions: 1. Acoustically signalling an attempt to break in and damage the vehicle. 2. Emitting the system beep signalling noises. Specifcations The main specifications of the siren are: sealed casing (IP66) NiMH green batteries for independent supply if the main vehicle battery supply leads are interrupted dialogue with the NBC and other alarm system components on the serial line autodiagnostic function maximum permitted current consumption: Sound power (when supplied): 107 - 118 dBA/2 metres SIREN OPERATING STATE ABSORPTION MAXIMUM CURRENT (at 12.5 V) REST 2.5 mA battery recharging 15 mA SURVEILLANCE 5 mA ALARM 2 A The siren is equipped with a 4-way sealed connection designed to receive a sealed female holder connector with the pin out described in the table: PIN I/O Imax FUNCTION 1 IN 2 SUPPLY POSITIVE (+30) (PROTECTED BY NON DEDICATED FUSE) 2 IN - OUT 10 mA SERIAL COMMUNICATION LINE WITH BODY COMPUTER 3 IN 2 GND 4 N.C. --- N.C. Operating limits: Voltage range: 9 - 16 V. Below the minimum voltage the siren receives a supply from its own internal battery. Temperature range: - 40° / + 85°C (if connected to the main supply); -20° / + 85°C (if receiving its own supply) Serial connection The siren is connected to the A-BUS serial line, therefore it is connected with the NBC and all the sensors/actuators for the vehicle protection sub-systems. This connection allow the exchange of commands between the two units (siren and NBC). If this connection fails, the possibility of communication is lost. In addition, if the serial line is overloaded, the siren functions take priority over other communication on the line. If the main supply leads are cut and the internal batteries are charged, the siren can: with the +30 cut, communicate in two directions with the earth cut, receive, but not reply (this produces alarm signals) If the batteries are run down, in both of the above mentioned cases, the siren reverts to WAREHOUSE mode and when the supply is restored later on a hardware reset is produced. Hardware reset A hardware reset is a temporary state that allows the siren to go from the WAREHOUSE condition to the REST condition. A hardware reset cannot be carried out from the outside. Device operating states There are 5 different operating states for the siren: WAREHOUSE REST SURVEILLANCE ALARM DIAGNOSIS WAREHOUSE This is the state that the component in supplied in. It is the state the component is in when the main supply and that from the internal batteries starts to fail. This mode represents a protective state in addition to the starting point for the generation of the hardware reset. We come to the WAREHOUSE state: from the REST state (if the outside supply fails) from the ALARM state (at the end of the signals for cutting the supply leads) REST This is the state the component is fitted on the vehicle in, connected to the main supply, if it is not activated by the reception of a switching on signal. In this condition it is possible to disconnect the battery supply leads to carry out servicing operations without causing the siren to produce acoustic signals. During the rest state the siren is in the minimum consumption condition (see table). If there is a fall in voltage ( < 7V), the siren waits fro 16 secs after which it enters the WAREHOUSE mode. In this operating state, and if there is a +15 signal, the batteries inside the siren can be recharged. The command is sent by the NBC to the siren and it is asked to manage the recharging strategy. the recharging ends when: there is no + 15 signal the siren receives a command to switch on 5 secs after the key-on It is possible to move from the REST state to the following states: SURVEILLANCE: using the control for switching the siren on ALARM: if the acoustic warning siren cycle is activated WAREHOUSE: following a decrease in the supply DIAGNOSIS: following a specific command SURVEILLANCE This siren operating state corresponds to the user switching the vehicle alarm system on. The siren is set in this operating mode by the NBC which, having received the command to switch the alarm system on, in turn, sends the command to switch the siren on. The command sent by the NBC to switch the siren on is accompanied by a random 2 byte code. This code is memorized by the siren. When there is a request to switch the alarm system off, the NBC should send the command to the code which should correspond with the one memorized by the siren. In this way the system is protected against possible attempts at intrusion with the aim of deactivating the siren. In this configuration the component needs to move to the alarm state following the verification of predetermined events. These events are: a fall in the main supply voltage: if the battery voltage goes below 3 V, the siren sets of the alarm cycles. Cutting of +30 lead: in this case the siren starts the acoustic alarm cycle until normal supply conditions are restored or the alarm is switched off. The maximum number of alarm cycles implemented by the siren corresponds to the figure transmitted by the NBC at the time it is switched on. Cutting the earth lead: the siren does not immediately set off the alarm cycle, but waits for the NBC to make itself available. In effect, in normal operating conditions, to check the condition of the connection, the NBC sends the siren a signal known as a heart-beat approximately every 500 ms. If the siren does not receive this signal for a maximum time of 0.5 secs, the alarm cycles commence. When the alarm cycles are over, the siren goes into the WAREHOUSE state. Given that the NBC is not capable of transmitting the heart-beat signal below certain battery voltage values, if the emission of the signal is interrupted, the siren checks that the battery voltage is above 7.5 V and, if it is below this, the alarm acoustic signals are inhibited. Cutting the serial communication line cable: the reaction logic is the same following the cutting of the earth lead. The only difference is that, at the end of the alarm cycles, the siren moves to the REST state. It is possible to move from the SURVEILLANCE state to the following states: ALARM REST: if the command to switch off is received. DIAGNOSIS: following a specific command. ALARM If the alarm system detects an attempt to break into the vehicle, tamper with it or enter it, it configures the siren in the ALARM state In this state the siren produces acoustic signals. The activation of the acoustic alarm is always managed and activated by the NBC and not by the siren. The signalling consists of a succession of alarm cycles. An alarm cycle is defined as the issue of a sound (managed by the NBC) lasting 26 secs (max 29 secs for cable cutting) followed by a 5 second pause, in accordance with the regulations laid down in directive 95/56/CE. DIAGNOSIS When it is switched on the alarm system sends the siren a request, via the serial line, to carry out an autodiagnosis on its sub-systems. The siren should send a response command within 3 secs. If it is not possible to carry out the autodiagnosis, the system uses the information received the previous time. Volumetric sensors The main purpose of the volumetric sensors is to detect an attempt to intrude into the passenger compartment using ultrasound. A variation in the volume inside the passenger compartment, identified by the waves, produces a signal which is sent to the NBC which implements the appropriate alarm procedure. The volumetric sensors are integrated in the Roof Node (NIM). It manages the software functions, houses the on/off button and operates the LED which is incorporated in the button and which warns about the implementation of the control. The switching on/off of the sensor is controlled by the A-BUS serial line. Specifcations The volumetric sensor has a 4-way connector with the following pin out: 1 = Supply positive (+30) 2 = Negative (earth) 3 = +15 4 = Serial line (A-BUS) Operating limits: Voltage range: 8 - 16 V. Temperature range: - 40° / + 85°C Wave emission frequency: 40 Khz Maximum permitted current consumption: SIREN OPERATING STATE ABSORPTION MAXIMUM CURRENT (at 12.5 V) REST 2.5 mA SURVEILLANCE = 10 mA Device operating states There are 4 different operating states for the siren: REST SURVEILLANCE ALARM DIAGNOSIS REST This is the state of the component, fitted on the vehicle, connected to the vehicle battery. In the REST state the volumetric module should be in the minimum consumption conditions in order to reduce the battery current absorption. In the REST state, with the alarm system switched off and the key-off, it is possible to manually exclude the volumetric protection by pressing the exclusion button in the courtesy light (NIM). The exclusion of this protection involves the sensors not being switched on. This exclusion is shown by the LED in the NIM exclusion button flashing and involves sending the exclusion signal to the NBC via the serial line. If more than 1 minute has elapsed since the key-off, a new key-on must be carried out in order to exclude the sensors. The volumetric protection exclusion situation persists until the next command to switch off the alarm: from this time onwards the sensors can be activated once again. It is possible to move from the REST state to the following states: SURVEILLANCE: using the control for switching the ultrasound on DIAGNOSIS: following a specific command SURVEILLANCE The volumetric sensors are in this configuration if the alarm system is switched on and they have not been excluded previously. During the SURVEILLANCE stage, the sensors protect the passenger compartment, checking for the presence of moving bodies. If an intrusion is detected, the NIM sends a signal to the NBC which produces a command for the alarm system to signal a theft attempt. If the battery voltage is below 8.5 V for longer than 30 mins, this causes the volumetric sensor module to be switched off in order to safeguard the life of the battery and to be able to start up the engine later on. It is possible to move from the SURVEILLANCE state to the following states: ALARM: as a result of the detection of an intrusion REST: following a switching off command ALARM This is the configuration the sensors are in if an intrusion is detected during the SURVEILLANCE state. This situation is communicated to the NBC by sending an appropriate signal. In order to prevent false alarms, these sensors have self-adaptation and temperature compensation functions to reduce their sensitivity to the variations in air density due to temperature and the type of fabrics used for the interior trims. It is possible to move from the ALARM state to the following states: SURVEILLANCE: following adjustments after an intrusion REST: following a command to switch off the alarm DIAGNOSIS At the time the alarm system is switched on, the NBC requests the sensor module state by sending an appropriate command. The sensors should respond to the autodiagnostic request within 4 secs. The diagnostic request can only be carried out if the sensors are in the REST state. If the sensors are not working they will not be activated and the cause will be stored in the diagnostic memory. Tilt sensor The main function of the tilt sensor is to detect a change in the angle of the vehicle and signal this to the NBC in order warn that the vehicle is being raised or an attempt is being made to steal part of it (e.g. the wheels). The tilt sensor is incorporated in the NIM, from which it receives a supply. It is operated by the A-BUS line managed by the NBC which uses the NIM to house the tilt sensor. The NIM also has the button for excluding the module and operates the LED which is incorporated in the button and which warns of the implementation of the control. Specifcations The volumetric sensor has a 4-way connector with the following pin out: 1 = Supply positive (+30) 2 = Negative (earth) 3 = +15 4 = Serial line (A-BUS) Operating limits: Voltage range: 8 - 16 V. The nominal supply voltage is 13.5 V with an absorption = 3mA Temperature range: - 40° / + 85°C Device operating states The tilt sensor should detect and signal a variation in the vehicle geometry angle in relation to the longitudinal and transverse axes of the actual vehicle. There are 4 different operating states for the siren: REST SURVEILLANCE ALARM DIAGNOSIS REST This is the state the tilt sensor is in when the alarm system is not switched on; no operation is activated in this stage. In the REST state, with the alarm system switched off and the key-off, it is possible to manually exclude the tilt protection by pressing the exclusion button in the courtesy light (NIM). The exclusion of this protection involves the sensors not being switched on. This exclusion is shown by the LED in the NIM exclusion button flashing and involves sending the exclusion signal to the NBC via the serial line. If more than 1 minute has elapsed since the key-off, a new key-on must be carried out in order to exclude the sensors. The tilt protection exclusion situation persists until the next command to switch off the alarm: from this time onwards the sensors can be activated once again. SURVEILLANCE The tilt sensors is in this configuration if the alarm system is switched on and it has not been excluded previously. During this stage the sensor begins the check on the angular position of the vehicle at the two axes which ends 30 secs after it is switched on. This check is designed to create a reference position. No alarm is generated during this period. The calculation of the angular references for the 2 axes is carried out through successive sampling. The position calculated at the end of the 30 secs is memorized. During the SURVEILLANCE stage the sensor should constantly monitor the angle of the vehicle, filter alterations due to slight swaying, parking near interference and wind conditions, sounding the alarm in the case of a theft attempt. The reference calculated when the alarm system is switched on is zeroed when: the alarm is triggered. The difference between the angles is zeroed. 5 minutes elapse without detecting an alarm. Alarm due to temperature drift. ALARM The tilt sensor is able to produce an alarm condition when a change in angle in relation to the reference position memorized is detected as a result of a rotation around the longitudinal or transverse axis of the vehicle at a speed of 0.5°/min. In this condition the alarm is produced before a tilt of 3° is reached. No alarm conditions should be created for rotation speeds of less than 0.5°/min. The alarm signal is sent to the NBC via the A-BUS serial line. DIAGNOSIS At the time the alarm system is switched on, the NBC requests the sensor state by sending an appropriate command. The sensor should respond to the autodiagnostic request within 3 secs. The diagnostic request can only be carried out if the sensor is in the REST state or the SURVEILLANCE state. If the sensor is not working it will not be activated and the cause will be stored in the diagnostic memory. Perimeter sensors These sensors are designed to detect unauthorized intrusion into the passenger compartment, the engine compartment and the luggage compartment. Transmitter in key-remote control or CID Both these devices are designed to make the authorized user in possession of them recognizable to the vehicle. These devices allow the alarm/anti-theft system to be switched on and off. SYSTEM STATES There are eight different possible states for the alarm system: DEACTIVATED REST ON SURVEILLANCE ALARM OFF PROGRAMMING DIAGNOSIS Deactivation This is the state the alarm system finds itself in each time the CODE system or the Passive Entry system recognizes an enabled key or CID. The alarm system is not switched off if the vehicle is released using the mechanical insert. This results in the anti-theft system being switched off. When the alarm system is deactivated it does not respond to the commands from the receiver or the Passive Entry system. It is possible to move from the deactivated state to the REST state by turning the key to key-off. If it is not possible to unlock the vehicle using the remote control or using the Passive Entry system (as a result of electro-magnetic interference or if the batteries are run down), access to the vehicle can be gained using the mechanical insert: the alarm system is activated when the driver's door is opened and the siren starts to sound. To interrupt the emission of the sound and deactivate the alarm, simply activate the instrument panel as follows: insert the key in the ignition and turn it to the ON position (for systems with a mechanical key). Activate the instrument panel using the control button, if necessary placing the CID in the Garage position. Rest It is the basic state the alarm system finds itself in. It is possible to move from the REST position to the following states: DIAGNOSIS: activated by connecting the Examiner to the NBC. SURVEILLANCE: when you wish to protect the vehicle through an insertion command. DEACTIVATED: when an enabled key or CID is recognized by the CODE/Passive Entry system. In the REST condition, the NBC always controls the +15 which, if fitted, prevents the move to SURVEILLANCE and, above all, to ALARM. In the REST condition it is possible to exclude the volumetric and tilt sensors within 1 minute of the key-off by pressing the relevant buttons in the courtesy light trim. Switching on Switching on is the operation that allows the alarm to move from the REST condition to the SURVEILLANCE state. This operation is always inhibited if there is a +15. SWITCHING ON the alarm system takes place the moment the doors are locked (using the remote control or through the Passive Entry system) and is signalled by the direction indicators coming on synchronized with the siren. When the NBC receives the command (remote control, Passive Entry) it activates the alarm SWITCHING ON procedure as follows: SIGNALLING OF SWITCHING ON IN PROGRESS. The operating mode is identified. The diagnosis of the alarm system modules is activated. The visual and acoustic signals for the time of SWITCHING ON are activated. SYSTEM DIAGNOSIS. The plausibility of the door switches (2 or 4), the boot switch and the bonnet switch are checked and, if one of these entry points is found NOT to be closed, this entry point is excluded from the surveillance. SENSOR STATE CHECK. If the siren is NOT OK after a maximum of 3 secs, the system causes the direction indicators to flash twice. After a maximum of 4 seconds after the system has been SWITCHED ON, the NBC receives the OK/NOT OK information from the volumetric sensors module and the tilt sensor. (see signalling modes in the next point). If the results on the state of these modules do not arrive within 4 seconds, then the respective module is declared non operational signalling the alarm sytem failure. DIAGNOSTIC INFORMATION DISPLAY. The signalling of faults at the time of SWITCHING ON takes place via: 1 warning beep 4 seconds after the central locking/alarm on command. The signalling of the type of problem through the deterrent LED takes place in the following ways: A) flashing at 8 Hz for 2.5 seconds for volumetric failures. B) LED on constantly for 10 seconds for a siren failure or tilt sensor failure. Obviously, the system component found to be faulty will not be switched on. MODULE SWITCHING ON: after the responses to the diagnosis are received, the operating modules, excluding the siren, are switched on SIREN SWITCHING ON. If the siren is working properly, the management of the HEART-BEAT on the A-BUS serial line is activated, in other words a signal that is exchanged every 500 msecs. between the NBC and the siren to constantly check the condition of the communication line. SWITCHING ON ENDED: the alarm system declares the SWITCHING ON stage over. Lastly, the deterrent warning light is controlled by the central locking system. If a command to unlock the doors (corresponding to the SWITCHING OFF of the alarm sytem) is received during the SWITCHGING ON stage, the procedure is interrupted and there is a move to the SWITCHING OFF stage. If visual and acoustic signals are in progress, they should be interrupted to implement the SWITCHING OFF signals. Automatic switching on This operation allows the alarm system to move from the REST state to the SURVEILLANCE state in an automatic, timed fashion. There are two self-switching on modes: 1. From key-off 2. PASSIVE mode (from the last door). 1. From key-off the key-off is detected. the self-switching on counter begins counting. The counter reaches the "SELF-SWITCHING ON TIME" value. The NBC checks whether a valid transponder/CID is present. If there is no valid transponder, the self-switching on takes place irrespective of the door status. 2. PASSIVE mode (from last door): the key-off is detected. The first self-switching on counter starts counting (fixed time of 2 mins). If an open/closed transition takes place, within 2 minutes, at the driver's door or at the last door, boot or bonnet, a second counter starts counting The second counter reaches the "SELF-SWITCHING ON TIME" value. The NBC checks whether a valid transponder/CID is present. If there is no valid transponder, the self-switching on starts. For both modes described, during the self-switching on cycle, the system should constantly check that there is no +15. If the +15 signal returns with a valid, recognized transponder/CID, then the procedure should be interrupted. During the self-switching on stage the system diagnosis takes place in the same way as during the normal switching on stage. The central locking is not activated during the self-switching on stage. Switching on again The operation of switching on again allows the sytem to move automatically from the REST stage to the SURVEILLANCE stage when, after an authorized switching off, the doors/boot/bonnet are not found to be open. The procedure for switching on again is as follows: the alarm system is switched off. The switching on again counter begins counting. If a closed/open transition is detected at any of the driver's doors or the bonnet or the boot then the switching on again is cancelled. The counter reaches the "SELF-SWITCHING ON TIME" value. The alarm is switched on taking into account any system exclusions (volumetric protection, siren,...) made at the last switching on. Surveillance During the surveillance stage, the NBC reads all the signals/commands on the A-BUS operating the siren, via the A-BUS, if these signals/commands involve its activation. The move to the alarm state is activated if the NBC verifies one or more of the following conditions: the presence of a +15 signal without a prior switching off command. Change of state for inputs coming from the doors, boot and bonnet (intrusion attempt). Command at the A-BUS for the external modules such as the ultrasound sensors, tilt sensor or from the siren (for cable cutting). If the NBC detects a battery voltage of less than 8.5 V for longer than 30 minutes, then it switches off the external modules in order to safeguard the life of the battery and allow the engine to be started up later on. If the user makes their intention to open the boot known (through the button on the remote control or by using the handle directly) and the system is in the SURVEILLANCE state, the NBC disables the volumetric/tilt external modules, disables the boot from the perimeter protection (with the doors and bonnet lid perimeter protection remaining activated) and activates the signalling through the blinkers. If, however, within 1 second of the command (from the remote control), the boot switch does not change status, the system switches the protection back on again. This timing makes it possible to ensure the protection of the vehicle even with the boot/rearscreen entry point faulty. If, on the other hand, the boot/rearscreen is left open and then the alarm is switched on, the volumetric/tilt protection is switched on. Alarm If one of the sensors involved in the surveillance identifies an irregular situation (attempted or actual intrusion or theft of the vehicle), the alarm sytem moves to the ALARM state, activating the siren and blinkers. If an alarm cause is detected during the surveillance stage, the NBC should implement the appropriate number of alarm cycles (visual+acoustic). At the end of the maximum number of cycles (visual+acoustic), if further alarm signals are needed, they are only produced through the blinkers (flashing of the direction indicators). If the NBC detects another alarm cause during an alarm cycle it ignores it. In effect, the NBC is only enabled to receive new alarm causes at the end of the alarm cycle. The system is required, for diagnostic purposes, to keep track of the alarm causes recognized by the NBC. The NBC memorizes the last 10 alarm causes, associating the cause and alarm system state at the time the system wash switched on with each of the causes. It is possible to move from the ALARM state to the following states: REST: with a switching off command or through the recognition by the CODE system at the key-on of an enabled key or recognition by the Passive Entry system. SURVEILLANCE: when the alarm cycles set off are ended. Switching off The system can be switched off in both the SURVEILLANCE and ALARM states It is carried out by the remote control or the Passive Entry system; the NBC commands the switching off of the alarm system the moment the doors are unlocked. At the time of SWITCHING OFF, the NBC interrupts the perimeter protection and, if present, al the counter-measures activated. The SWITCHING OFF controls the activation of the visual + acoustic signals. The SWITCHING OFF command is also accepted if there is a +15 signal. The alarm system can also be switched off in the following ways: by turning an enabled key to the ON position through the detection of a valid CID in the passenger compartment or in the GARAGE position (this last operation is necessary, for example, when the CID is run down, the customer opens the driver's door using the pawl and the alarm is consequently activated: by placing the CID in the GARAGE position the alarm can be deactivated). At the first key-on after the SWITCHING OFF, the NBC commands the display of an alarms that have taken place, by means of a series of messages shown on the panel display. Programming The configuration of the alarm system installed on the vehicle can be programmed at the end of the line. This configuration can be read, but not modified, by the diagnostic equipment which will adapt its diagnostic procedures depending on the configuration present. Diagnosis No diagnostic checks are required for the perimeter protection switches. The NBC should carry out the diagnosis for the operation of the serial line connected to the siren and to the external modules. The diagnosis of the external modules is entrusted to the functions that manage them. The diagnostic information obtained at the time when the alarm system is switched on should be memorized to guarantee help for the system. If an external module is recognized as not functioning, it is excluded for the entire surveillance cycle. The next time the system is switched on, the diagnostic check is carried out again on the modules which should be reactivated if they are recognized as working.

CONSTRUCTION SPECIFICATIONS Fastened securely to the bodyshell, the doors make an important contribution towards both frontal and side impacts. They have been strengthened by a waist level crossmember which has the function of stabilizing the doors in the case of frontal impacts, preventing them from opening accidentally during the impact, at the same time guaranteeing easy opening after the impact. Their behaviour during side impacts has been improved by high-resistance tubular steel bars. 1 - Lock 2 - Outer handle with micro 3 - Manual button 4 - Control panel (NPP) 5 - Wind trim 6 - Seal 7 - Rear view mirror with courtesy light 8 - Window opening device 9 - Passive entry aerial Window opening devices The vehicle is equipped with electric windows operated by a drive cable. The switch for operating the window is located in the armrest on each door; in particular, there are switches for operating the electric windows for all four doors on the left front armrest and the switch for activating/excluding the rear electric windows with a signalling LED. All the electric window control buttons are recessed to prevent them from being activated accidentally. The front windows (driver and passenger) are equipped with an automatic function for opening and closing them. Anti-theft windows are available as an optional extra: they are side windows made from two sheets of glass with a film of plastic material in between. These windows offer the following advantages: they prevent injury in the case of an accident because they do not produce splinters like the glass used in normal windows; they guarantee good resistance to attempts to break into the vehicle; in the case of small impacts from the outside (such as, for example, stone chipping) only the outside layer of glass breaks, guaranteeing the full functioning of the window. Seals The door seals have been designed to ensure a perfect seal against wind resistance. Traditional door housing seal; Wind seal on the entire perimeter of the door housing; Additional seal on the door frame which, together with the door housing seal, produces a perfect seal against wind resistance. There is a special safety sensor on the window guide seal for each door which guarantees the reversal of the movement of the window each time something is placed between the window and the actual seal.

SPECIFICATIONS There are three lids on the vehicle, the bonnet lid, the boot lid and the fuel filler flap. The bonnet lid and the boot lid are made from an outer covering assembled on a support frame. Layers of sealant are applied between the covering and the frame which, in addition to limiting vibrations also increase the strength of the assembly. The fuel filler flap is made of plastic which is matched to the colour of the bodywork. Bonnet lid The bonnet lid, completely covered in a sound insulation material, is supported when it is open by two gas springs. There is a single central locking unit for its control and locking. The control system is a bowden cable. The bonnet lid has a frame with pre-established collapse lines; this safety feature prevents the lid from going through the windscreen in the case of an impact. Composition 1 - Bonnet lid 2 - Lid hinges 3 - Retaining hook 4 - Telescopic struts 5 - Wind seals 6 - Lid lock 7 - Sound insulation lining Boot lid The boot lid is entirely lined with a sound insulation material and is supported by telescopic struts with gas springs. The rear section (no. plate holder) houses the rear light clusters for the reversing lights and rear fog lamps, the electric handle and the key lock. The boot is opened: using the key directly in the lock which makes it possible to release the boot lid by turning the mechanical insert in a clockwise direction (with the battery run down); using the button in the tunnel cover console which operates the lock electrically; using the electric handle (micro); using the remote control. For further details see NVB (See assembly ) 5505A multi-function components Composition 1 - Rear tailgate 2 - Tailgate lock 3 - Telescopic strut 4 - Tailgate hinges 5 - Upper inner lining 6 - Side / lower lining 7 - Third brake light 8 - Inner rear lamp Fuel filler flap View of the fuel filler flap 1 - Fuel filler flap 2 - Hook 3 - Flap retaining lock The fuel filler flap is made of plastic which is matched to the colour of the bodywork. The flap is opened depending on the state of the driver's door: driver's door locked - flap locked; driver's door unlocked - flap unlocked. It is also possible to open the flap, in emergencies, using a cable located in the luggage compartment on the right hand side.

An electrically operated sun roof, which can also be operated from a distance using a remote control, is available on request for all vehicles. The sun roof can be adjusted, using a selector, in nine positions in addition to closed, allowing and excellent intake of outside air into the passenger compartment. To guarantee safety during the various movements, the sun roof is equipped with a special safety device which stops movement if there is an obstacle present. SPECIFICATIONS The sun roof has a sliding glass element, electrically operated by means of an electric motor and can be adjusted by means of a selector into nine positions (three tilted and six retracted sliding positions) in addition to the closed position. There is a seal along the edges of the sun roof which is in contact with the roof profile. The sun roof is also fitted with a rigid trim which slides together with the glass panel. The selector is located on the roof near the courtesy light which, by means of a control unit, controls the action of the electric motor. Movement takes place by means of two flexible racks to which the slides which drive the pullies supporting the sun roof are secured. In order to limit possible damage, to passengers or objects, caused by the movement of the roof, there is a safety function that is activated the whole time that the roof is closing, both during the sliding of the panel and the tilting movement. There are also drainage channels, at the front and rear of the frame, that drain the water, through suitable pipes fitted with anti-reflux valves, that could penetrate through the seals when it is raining or when the vehicle is washed. COMPOSITION The diagram illustrates the sun roof components 1 - Thermal tinted glass 2 - Seal 3 - Trim 4 - Drainage pipe 5 - Drainage channel 6 - Deflector 7 - Guide mechanisms 8 - Motor 9 - Selector 10 - Flexible racks 11 - Supporting mechanism 12 - Mechanism shield 13 - Solar cells The system consists of: an electric movement motor fitted with Hall effect speed and position sensors; a sliding frame equipped with a flexible rack drive system; an electronic control unit, integrated in the electric motor group; a selector for the different sun roof positions, fitted with an inhibitor control. solar cells incorporated in the roof panel to supply the air conditioning system fan and thereby reduce the temperature in the passenger compartment (with the vehicle stationary). OPERATION The sun roof is moved along sliding guides, on the frame, by means of an electric motor than can be controlled either manually using the selector or remotely by means of a command sent by the Body Computer to the control unit. (Vedere sottogruppo ) 5505 CIRCUITI ELETTRICI DEGLI STRUMENTI/INDICATORI The action of the motor moves the flexible driving racks, housed in special housings in the frame, to which the mechanisms for supporting the sun roof are secured, with the sun roof moved to the desired point or position. The sun roof is also fitted with a blind underneath which slides together with the glass panel and acts as a finishing trim. The roof can be moved manually, using the selector, in the following conditions: with the ignition key in the ON position (key-on); with the ignition key in the OFF or PARK position (key-off) with the doors closed or with one of the front doors open if the selector is operated within two minutes then the roof is enabled; after this period has elapsed the sun roof is disabled. If the sun roof is open its operation is managed by the remote control on the Body Computer (DF5505) and is activated by signals coming from: (Vedere sottogruppo ) 5505 CIRCUITI ELETTRICI DEGLI STRUMENTI/INDICATORI remote contro; key lock in the door; The sun roof should complete the movement from open to closed automatically within 15 seconds; irrespective of the position of the selector during this stage it is possible to manually stop the movement of the roof within 10 seconds by a vertical impulse on the selector or by turning its position. The roof ignores the remote command and assumes the new position. The antipinch function is always active during sliding/tilting movement operations (including operations commanded by a remote unit). never disconnect the battery or the sun roof supply whilst it is moving or less than 5 seconds after the roof has stopped moving. If this is the case, the control unit loses its memory and it must be restored by following the procedure described in the appropriate paragraph. Anti-crush safety function In order to limit possible damage, to passengers and/or objects, caused by the movement of the roof, there is a safety function that is activated the whole time that the roof is closing, both during the sliding of the panel and the tilting movement. Following the detection of a force above a certain level, which is notified by the control unit as a possible obstacle, the latter commands the immediate stopping and the reversal of the movement by about 10cm in the case of sliding or by a position in the case of tilting. When the obstacle has been removed, press the control selector vertically (inhibitor function) to close the roof. The antipinch function is inhibited during this operation. If the obstacle is present, the sun roof will be mechanically locked. This condition can damage the sun roof. Selector View of the manual control selector 0 - Roof closed position B1 - Minimum tilt position B3 - Maximum tilt position S1 - Minimum sliding position S6 - Maximum sliding position The manual control selector can be adjusted: by turning the knob in an anti-clockwise direction, at three pre-defined heights for tilting the spoiler from "B1 to B3"; by turning the knob in a clockwise direction, in six pre-defined sliding positions from "S1 to S6"; position "0" corresponds to the roof closed. This position can also be recognized by the longer duration of the click; in the "inhibitor" position (all the selector connections are earthed) the selector is pressed in a vertical direction. Control unit The movement of the sun roof is managed by an electronic controlunit, housed in the casing on the motor, which processes the signals coming from the selector or the remote command, via the Body Computer, also controlling the safety protection function. This function is managed by the control unit which receives information from both the position and speed Hall effect sensors, on the motor. Following the detection of a force of more than a certain level, corresponding to a greater current absorption and notified as being a possible obstacle, the control unit commands the immediate stopping and reversal of movement by about 10 cm. The control unit also receives a vehicle speed signal because, depending on the speed, through the effect of the vacuum, the force required for closing the roof changes and in certain circumstances this could be perceived as an impediment. The control unit therefore uses this signal in order to mistakenly stop the movement. Resetting control unit memory The sun roof may lose the movement memory as a result of a break in the supply whilst the roof is moving. To reset the memory, follow the procedure described below: place the selector in the maximum tilt position (end of rotation in anti-clockwise direction B3); press the selector vertically, keeping it in this position until the roof stops in the maximum tilt position (once the maximum position is reached the racks move back about one centimetre); release the selector and, within five seconds, press the selector again, keeping it pressed; wait until the roof completes a full travel from maximum tilt position to maximum open position - from maximum opening to closed; release the selector and return it to the closed position (0). At this point the control unit memory is reset. Emergency manoeuvre View of intervention points for emergency movement. 1 - Electric contol motor 2 - Operating key If the electric device for moving the roof fails, the sun roof can be moved manually proceeding as described below: detach the courtesy light; introduce the key into the housing in the motor; turn the key in a clockwise direction to open the roof or in an anti-clockwise direction to close it. Alignment Alignment procedure on the vehicle During repair operations on the vehicle which involve removing the sun roof and the motor at the same time, when refitting, if it is unsure whether the position of the sliding guides has been maintained, before refitting the parts, the two guides must be aligned because the alignment of the sun roof can no longer be guaranteed and this could result in malfunctions and wind noise. 1 - Supporting lever 2 - Drive guide To restore the alignment of the guides with the motor disconnected, follow the procedure described below: manually place the supporting guides in the fully forward position on both sides, checking that the sliding is complete; refit the motor; reconnect the motor to the electrical system and the selector to the control unit; carry out the control unit memory resetting procedure described in the relevant paragraph; refit the sun roof on the supports, suitably adjusting their position to ensure that the alignment is correct and the seal perfect; attach the finishing blind. Alignment procedure at the bench (with the sun roof assembly at the bench) Following a procedure which has involved disconnecting the motor or the moving or sliding parts, to align the sun roof guides and position the moving parts correctly, follow the procedure described below: fit the detached parts with the exception of the motor; manually place the supporting guides in the fully forward position on both sides, checking that the sliding is complete; refit the motor; refit the sun roof on the vehicle and carry out the control unit memory resetting procedure, as described in the relevant paragraph. refit the sun roof on the supports, suitably adjusting their position to ensure that the alignment is correct and the seal perfect; attach the finishing blind. ROOF PANEL (SOLAR CELLS) View of sun roof with solar cells. 1 - Panel 2 - Solar cells 3 - Contacts There is a battery with 21 mono-crystalline solar cells in the glass panel which is capable of providing a total power of 24 W. The solar cells come into operation when the vehicle is under the following conditions: Vehicle parked with key OFF; Front and rear doors closed. Boot lid closed CAN in Sleep On status or disabled. Sunroof closed or in spoiler position. The electrical energy produced by these cells (with the vehicle stationary and the ignition key in the OFF position, sun roof closed or in spoiler position) supplies the air conditioning system fan. When the car is in the situation described previously a remote control switch inside the air conditioning fan cuts off the direct power supply from the battery so that electrical power produced by the solar cells can supply the air conditioning fan in first speed position and cut out the vehicle air conditioning system management unit. When the CAN is re-awoken (by opening a door or the boot lid), the remote control switch cuts off the power supply from the solar cells so the air conditioning system can operate normally. The advantages of this solution are: reduction in the high temperature inside the passenger compartment produced by the rays of the sun; support for the air conditioning system, reducing its workload. This function is only activated with the sun roof closed or in the spoiler position, whilt it is inhibited from the first opening position. Each time the system is switched off, after having memorized the status of the controls/implementations, it forces the recirculation open, thereby preparing fthe operating conditions for the "solar cell roof" option.

SPECIFICATIONS An (electric) rearscreen blind operated by pressing the button in the centre console and on the rear seat armrest is available on request. The blind is housed in the rear parcel shelf and amply covers the rear windscreen preventing the rays of the sun from entering the vehicle whilst at the same time it remains possible to see outside from the inside. COMPOSITION The system comprises an electric movement motor (4) to which the rods (3), that move the levers (5) are connected; the levers slide on guide cams on the trim (1) to which the cloth (2) is secured and the rubber rollers (6) rest againt the rearscreen glass at a predetermined force to prevent noise. The unwinding/rewinding time is less than around 8 seconds. 1 - Trim. 2 - Cloth. 3 - Rods. 4 - Electric motor. 5 - Levers. 6 - Rubber rollers. OPERATION The operation is controlled by an end of travel device (window mechanism type); if the blind is operated it cannot assume intermediate positions: it is either fully raised or fully lowered. if the blind is raised and lowered at least four times within 25 seconds, then its operation is inhibited for a period of 30 seconds. The last manoeuvre before this inhibition must be completed, the last accepted manoeuvre being the opposite to the starting manoeuvre.

CONSTRUCTION SPECIFICATIONS The windscreen and the rearscreen are bonded to the bodyshell and, as structural elements, contribute to its strength. The windscreen is the stratified type and consists of two layers of glass bonded to one another by a film. If the windscreen breaks even though it is cracked it maintains its position and sufficient visibility. The windscreen has centering pins to ensure correct matching with the window housing. It also has a heating resistance in the area where the windscreen wiper blades are parked and in the area of the interior rear view mirror for the rain/dusk sensor for the automatic activation of the windscreen wiper and the lights. The tempered type rearscreen is produced by means of a thermal process during which the surface of the glass is subjected to strong compression. If the rearscreen breaks it shatters into small pieces. The rearscreen has two centering pins which have the same function as those for the windscreen. COMPOSITION Windscreen and rearscreen 1 - Windscreen 2 - Perimeter trim 3 - Centering pins 4 - Windscreen wiper blade heating resistance 5 - Rain/dusk sensor 6 - Rearscreen 7 - Perimeter trim 8 - Centering pins 9 - AM aerial 10 - FM aerial 11 - TV aerial 12 - RF aerial Windscreen The shape of the lower part of the windscreen is asymmetrical to allow the windscreen wiper blades to park in a position below the bonnet lid. This solution means that the windscreen wiper blades cannot be seen from either the inside or the outside of the vehicle and involves: the elimination of a visual obstacle with advantages in terms of aesthetics; the elimination of wind resistance at high speeds. The windscreen surround trim is equipped with special ducts for the rain to flow through which prevent the fouling of the side windows and the windscreen if it is raining. Rearscreen The rearscreen surround trim is fitted with similar ducts for the rain to flow through as those on the windscreen surround trim. In addition to the demisting resistances there are also radio and TV reception aerials on the rearscreen.

SPECIFICATIONS All the vehicle interior trims, designed to satisfy the most stringent international standards governing flammability, are slow burning, do not ignite through accidental contact (for example if a cigarette is dropped), do not develop flames and, in the presence of severe overheating, are subject to combustion that produces strong, dense smoke. The one-piece dashboard is secured to a high-resistance steel crossmember, in turn secured to the bodyshell. The design of the dashboard and the surrounding trims is aimed at producing a high level of comfort and a high degree of passive safety, achieved by eliminating all projections which could be dangerous to the occupants of the vehicle in the case of an impact. The passenger Air Bag module is housed under the dashboard trim, protected by a "programmed" breakage cover. COMPOSITION Exploded view of the dashboard

CENTRE REAR COURTESY LIGHT The rear courtesy light is located in the end section of the roof. It contains three lamps, one centre and two side. SPECIFICATIONS The front seats have been designed for optimum driving comfort and maximum safety, guaranteeing the ideal specifications for lateral containment and lumbar support. In the front part of the seating area there is an excellent structure for anti-submarining, to prevent the body sliding forward under the seat belt in the case of strong deceleration (frontal impacts). The backrest frame is mae from a pressed steel structure which improves the capacity for energy absorption in the case of strong acceleration (rear impact). The seats are available in two versions: semi-manual. electric. Semi-manual seats The lengthwise adjustment and the adjustment of the head restraint take place through mechanical movement. The adjustment of the backrest (lumbar and height) is through electrical movement. Electric seats Seat adjustments 1 - Lengthwise adjustment 2 - Front tilting and rear cushion 3 - Head restraint adjustment 4 - Backrest adjustment 5 - Lumbar adjustment On both versions of the seat the heater function is available with three temperature settings: temperature 1 - 36°C; temperature 2 - 39°C; temperature 3 - 44°C. COMPOSITION Structure of the front seat (electrically adjusted) 1 - Lower cushion 2 - Lengthwise adjustment switch 3 - Seat lifting switch 4 - Guide 5 - Angle adjustment switch 6 - Motor for lumbar adjustment 7 - Motor for seat sliding 8 - Motor for raising front cushion 9 - Motor for raising rear cushion 10 - Motor for tilting backrest 11 - Seat heating regulator 12 - Head restraint 13 - Head restraint adjustment motor 14 - Control unit (NAG) (NAP) 15 - Side Bag 16 - Belt stalk Head restraints They are equipped with a height/angle adjustment device that allows them positioned stably in various intermediate positions with a travel of around 60 mm. Seat belts The front seat belts, with pretensioners, have a dual mounting on the seat. The belt therefore follows the seat in the various positions that it can assume, adjusting to guarantee maximum safety conditions in all situations. There is a sensor on the seat belt stalk that signals the fastening status of the belt (control unit). Side Air Bags The Side Bag module is fitted on the outside of the seat backrest frame. This solution, as opposed to installation on the pillar or the door, means that the Bag is always in the optimum position in relation to the occupant, irrespective of the adjustment of the seat or the size of the occupant. Passenger presence sensor The passenger presence sensor is a device capable of identifying the presence of a weight on the passenger front seat cushion (up to about 12 kg). The sensor is fitted in the seat between the upholstery and the cover and covers the entire seating area with the exception of the side panels. Armrest There is an arm rest between the front seats which can be opened and is height adjustable (4 positions) whch is secured to the lower centre trim. There is a lever in the arm rest housing which allows the air conditioning vents to be opened and closed. OPERATION Adjustment The shape of the seat and the extensive adjustment possibilities, together with the possibilities of adjusting the steering wheel and the exterior mirrors, means that the optimum driving position can be achieved for drivers of different sizes with different driving styles. In addition to the adjustments (lengthwise, height, tilt, head restraint, lumbar) there is also a three position memory function (where fitted) for the driver's seat which, when the vehicle has been switched off and then started up again places the seat in the position memorized previously. Control panel There are controls on the outside of the seat cushion for the following adjustments 1 - Lumbar adjustment 2 - Heater pad temperature adjustment 3 - Backrest and head restraint adjustment 4 - Front/rear tilt and lengthwise adjustment 5 - Memory buttons Memorizing The memorizing of the position of the driver's seat is carried out using one of three buttons (known as 1, 2 and 3) after having personalized the position of the seat, the steering column and the exterior rear view mirrors. The memorizing is carried out by pressing one of the three buttons for more than 3 seconds. To confirm that the memorizing has taken place the control unit (NAG) sends a message, via the CAN, to sound the confirmation buzzer. The following simultaneous movements are not allowed during manual adjustment: COMFORT SEATS Adaptation and massage function The adaptation and massage functions are achieved by using a system that comprises of air bags, located between the cover and the upholstery. The quantity of air contained inside the bags is managed by an electronic control unit in order to produce the optimum pressure distribution depending on the dimensions, weight and position of the occupant of the seat. The massage function is produced by partly inflating and deflating the bags according to a predefined cycle. The system usually works at between –20°C and + 65°C. System features The system components are illustrated in the figure below. 1 - Cushion metal structure 2 - Backrest metal structure 3 - Cushion fan spacer 4 - Backrest shield 5 - Pneumatic pump 6 - Head restraint 7 - Backrest air bag 8 - Cushion air bag 9 - Air flow distributor cap 10 - Cushion fan 11 - Cushion upholstery 12 - Backrest upholstery 13 - Air flow distributor cap 14 - Air flow distributor cap 15 - Air flow distributor cap 16 - Air flow distributor cap 17 - Seat controls trim 18 - Outer cover 19 - Nag / Nap 20 - Massage control unit 21 - Control unit bracket 22 - Cushion fan 23 - Backrest rear panel 24 - Cushion wiring 25 - Front cover 26 - Backrest fan The "Adaptation" and "Massage" function management system components are: an electronic control unit comprising an electronic card and pneumatic vales which have the function of regulating the amount of air in the individual bags; an air pump; air bags located in the cushion in the front and side areas and in the backrest in the lumbar region; the wiring, connecting the electronic control unit and the air pump, the supply leads and the control signal transmission cables; the pneumatic connecting pipes between the electronic control unit valves and the air bags and between the electronic control unit and the air pump. The adaptation function is activated by the occupant; this activation features: an initial stage for completely inflating the bags; a second deflation stage controlled according to the pressure exerted by the occupant until an optimum distribution situation is reached. Once the optimum configuration is reached, a check on the pressure distribution is carried out every four minutes giving rise to a new adjustment of the quantities of air in the bags. All the bags are involved in the adaptation function. The massage function involves all the bags except for the ones located in the sides of the cushion. The occupant requests a massage with the cycle lasting four minutes, afterwards the system automatically returns to the adaptation cycle (for about 60 secs.) and then a new four minute cycle starts again. The intensity of the lumbar support can be regulated during the massage stage. The massage and adaptation functions cannot be activated simultaneously since they are produced by the same system: as a result, if a massage cycle is activated, the seat adaptation function cannot be activated at the same time. The intensity of the massage cycle is different for the driver and passenger seats. The massage cycle sequence is as follows: 1 left and right rear areas simultaneously 2 lower lumbar support 3 upper lumbar support 4 lower lumbar support 5 left and right rear areas simultaneously Ventilation function The ventilation function is produced by means of three fans (two in the cushion and one in the backrest) that produce a flow of air towards the occupant directed through the use of ducts in the foam and distributed evenly by means of special layers of breathable material. The heating is produced by means of a special highly permeable heater layer between the cushion and the backrest (with a temperature sensor in the cushion). The ventilation is concentrated in the rear and side areas of the cushion and in the backrest. The cover is made from perforated leather. The rear panel is perforated in the centre to allow air to circulate inside the backrest The fans are controlled simultaneously by the NAG/NAP control unit at pre-defined constant speeds. The occupant can select three temperature settings for the heating. 1 - Backrest fan 2 - Cushion fan 3 - Backrest upholstery ducts 4 - Cushion upholstery ducts Function management The comfort functions for the front seat are managed using the controls on the seat trim and through the NIT user interface (screen with buttons in the dashboard). The "NIT comfort menu activation" control is located on the trim. 1 - Left trim 2 - NIT comfort menu activation 3 - Right trim The following controls are managed through the NIT panel user interface: Adaptation activation / deactivation Massage activation / deactivation Ventilation activation / deactivation Seat heating levels adjustment

SPECIFICATIONS The rear seats have a backrest with a structure guaranteed to ensure maximum safety for the occupants through a metal partition designed to prevent any objects in the luggage compartment entering the passenger compartment in the case of an impact. In order to increase the capacity of the luggage compartment, a split folding rear seat (40%/60%) is available on request. The rear cushions have a pressed steel base with a structure that ensures an anti-submarining effect. There are three height adjustable head restraints that are operated manually. The head restraints can be placed in the lowest position through a single, electrically controlled action, increasing rear visibility. There is an armrest, on the backrest, between the two side seats, that opens and can be folded back. There are buttons in the housing for operating the seat heating function, the sun blind and the sliding of the right front seat (where fitted). Access to the ski holder compartment is possible with the armrest lowered. The outer sides of the backrest have two padded covers in keeping with the style of the backrest. They house the Side Bag modules which are designed to protect the chest of the occupants in the case of side impacts. COMPOSITION Assembly view 1 - Side head restraint 2 - Centre head restraint 3 - Backrest cover and padding (folding) 4- Backrest structure 5 - Armrest 6 - Cushion cover and padding 7 - Fixed backrest 8 - Side Bag modules COMFORT SEATS Adaptation and massage function The adaptation and massage functions are produced using the same component. This component is a system comprising air bags, located between the cover and the upholstery. The quantity of air contained inside the bags is managed by an electronic control unit in order to produce the optimum pressure distribution depending on the dimensions, weight and position of the occupant of the seat. The massage function is produced by partly inflating and deflating the bags according to a predefined cycle. System features The system components are illustrated in the figure below. 1 - Cushion frame 2 - Seat wiring 3 - Massage control unit 4 - Hydraulic pump 5 - Crossmember 6 - Container 7 - Resistance 8 - Rear backrest 9 - Backrest bags 10 - Backrest heater pad 11 - Backrest wiring 12 - Head restraint 13 - Controls in rear seat armrest The "Adaptation" and "Massage" function management system components are: an electronic control unit comprising an electronic card and pneumatic vales which have the function of regulating the amount of air in the individual bags; an air pump; air bags located in the cushion in the front and side areas and in the backrest in the lumbar region; the wiring, connecting the electronic control unit and the air pump, the supply leads and the control signal transmission cables; the pneumatic connecting pipes between the electronic control unit valves and the air bags and between the electronic control unit and the air pump. The adaptation function is activated when the occupant requests by pressing the function button for about two seconds. This activation features: an initial stage for completely inflating the bags; a second deflation stage controlled according to the pressure exerted by the occupant until an optimum distribution situation is reached, lasting about 30 secs. When the best configuration is produced, the pressure distribution is read/checked every four minutes with a new adjustment of the amount of air in the bags. The massage is carried out when the occupant requests and lasts four minutes, after which the system carries out an adaptation stage and then a new massage cycle until the occupants switches the massage control off. The system moves to the adaptation regime and the "adaptation off" control must be selected to switch it off permanently. The lumbar support can be adjusted, to a certain extent, whilst the massage function is in progress. The massage and adapation functions cannot be activated simultaneously the same as for the front seat. if the occupants have switched both functions on then the system will give priority to the massage function. Any "adapation on" signal is ignored during this cycle. When the ignition key is turned off, the system ends the massage and adaptation functions cycle. When the vehicle is started up again, the "adaptation" or "massage" function has to be reselected whilst the lumbar support function setting is maintained. The massage cycle sequence is as follows: 1 left and right rear areas (simultaneously) 2 lower lumbar support 3 upper lumbar support 4 lower lumbar support 5 left and right rear areas (simultaneously) The bags are activated alternately, i.e. the cycle goes in increasing order from point 1 to point 5 and then in decreasing order from point 5 to point 1. Function management The comfort functions are managed through special buttons located in the armrest. There are two sets of buttons, on the left and right sides, each set comprising 6 buttons with the following functions and symbols: A: Adaptation activation OFF Adaptation deactivation M Massage activation OFF Massage deactivation L+: Lumbar support increase L-: Lumbar support decrease There are also switches for the following functions inside the armrest on the business trim level: selecting the heater temperature settings (right + left); moving the front passenger seat; moving the rearscreen sun blind. As the (front and rear) seat conformation is very different and as the position/shape of the bags that produce the massage has been evaluated to give the best physiological results, the massage intensity cycles for the front and rear seats are very different.

CONSTRUCTION SPECIFICATIONS The front and rear bumpers are made from a crystalline thermoplastic resin (polypropylene) which is produced from the polymerization of propylene. It is a material resistant to humidity, oil and solvents and can withstand temperatures of up to 170 °C. The bumpers contain impact absorbing buffers made from expanded polypropylene, a material whose resistance specifications remain constant to variations in temperature, ageing and possible distortion. The wheel housings are protected by special liners made from a semi-rigid plastic material and have the function of protecting part of the engine compartment and the inside of the wing from foreign bodies and dirt, of providing insulation against noise for the passenger compartment and, lastly, of embellishing the parts of the housings that can be seen. The lower part of the engine compartment is protected by a cover fixed to the chassis and the bumper. The other elements (grilles, trims, etc.) are designed to enhance the style of the vehicle. 1 - Radiator grille 2 - No. plate holder 3 - Stem 4 - Front bumper 5 - Rear bumper 6 - Front wheel arch liner 7 - Rear wheel arch liner 8 - Parking sensors 9 - Headlamp washers DESCRIPTION The bumpers are colour-matched to the bodywork and constitute an important element. The parking sensors (where fitted) are present in the front and rear bumpers. The front bumper also houses the fog lights and the telescopic type headlamp washers.

SPECIFICATIONS The vehicle is fitted with seat belts with three mounting points, even for the third rear passenger, with an automatic inertia reel. The seat belts for the front seats, which are height adjustable, are fitted with electrically controlled pretensioners with a load restricter. The seat belt fastening sensors are fitted on the seat belt stalks. This electronic device detects whether the seat belt is fastened and transmits this information to the Air Bag control unit. There is a warning light in the instrument panel for driver's seat belt only indicating that it is not fastened. The side rear seats have seat belts with pretensioners fitted on the crossmembers under the rear parcel shelf whilst the centre seat has a seat belt on the same crossmember with an inertia reel and three mounting points. COMPOSITION View of the seat belt layout on the vehicle 1 - Front seat belt 2 - Electrically controlled pretensioner 3 - Front seat belt stalk 4 - Air Bag control unit 5 - Rear side seat belt 6 - Electrically controlled pretensioner 7 - Rear centre seat belt 8 - Inertia reel 9 - Rear seat belt stalk Reel with pretensioner and load restricter The reels for the front and side rear seat belts are fitted with electrically operated pretensioners, controlled by the Air Bag control unit [DF5580C] with a load resricter device. This device, introduced to improve passive safety, is capable of reducing the loads that are normally exerted by the seat belts on the shoulders and the chest following an impact, minimizing the trauma resulting from the effect of the seat belts. Operation Section of pretensioners before and after activation 1 - Toothed wheel 2 - Toothed wheel 3 - Toothed bush 4 - Rack piston 5 - Pyrotechnic charge 6- Propellant A - Before activation B - After activation The moment in which a given (sudden) sufficiently serious deceleration of the vehicle takes place, the electronic sensor located in the control unit sents a signal which primes the pyrotechnic charges for the gas generators (5). The combustion of the propellant (6) develops a chemical reaction forming (inert) gas whose pressure produces a force which pushes the rack piston (4) upwards rotating the toothed wheel (1) which is connected to the toothed wheel (2). The later, engaging with the toothed bush (3), changes the rotary movement of the chuck to the opposite direction of the belt winding, rewinding it by a few centimetres. After any impact that caused the activation of the pretensioner, the seat belt can no longer be used and must be replaced.

Version Without Keyless Go The alarm system comes on automatically the moment the doors are locked using the remote control or the PASSIVE system in Belgian mode. The remote control receiver is integrated in the Body Computer Node and is fitted with an aerial for receiving the signal. STEP OPERATIONS TO BE CARRIED OUT TEST RESULTS 0 PRELIMINARY CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that: the doors close mechanically using the keys which come with the vehicle the remote controls are both working Move on to Step 1. The doors do not lock using the key Continue following the instructions in the table P10 CENTRAL LOCKING NOT WORKING 2. Only one remote control is working Move on to Step 3. Both remote controls are not working Move on to Step 1 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment to the diagnostic socket and check the following at the Body Computer Node: In parameters ambient: that there are no faults; the presence of the alarm system the programming state of the remote controls Move on to Step 1. The doors do not lock using the key 1. Continue following the instructions in the diagnostic table 2. Only one remote control is working 2. Check the conformity of the vehicle 3. Both remote controls are not working 3. Carry out the programming procedure for the keys and remote controls 2 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment to the diagnostic socket and check the following at the Body Computer Node In parameters ambient: the number of remote controls programmed the plausibility of the remote control button parameter the charge state of the remote control batteries Move on to Step 1. The number of remote controls programmed is less than the number of remote controls which come with the vehicle 1. Programme the remote control, if possible, or replace the key and remote control and programme again 2. The remote control button parameter state does not change (pressed/released) 2. Replace the remote control and carry out the programming 3. The remote control batteries are run down 3. Replace the batteries 3 CHECK ON CORRECT OPERATION ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the fault is no longer present Move on to Step Fault persists Replace body computer See in Op. 5505A32 BODY COMPUTER - R.R.

(Version Without Keyless Go). The alarm comes on normally but the doors not lock lock; The alarm system comes on automatically the moment the doors are locked using the remote control. The command to lock the doors and boot comes from the Body Computer Node to the Driver's Door Node, Passenger Door Node and Luggage Compartment Node. If one of the doors is not properly shut or the door sensor is signalling this condition, the door cannot be properly locked and this is signalled by a warning beep and the flashing of the direction indicators and the door LEDs for 3 seconds STEP OPERATIONS TO BE CARRIED OUT TEST RESULTS 0 PRELIMINARY CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that: the doors can be locked using the keys that come with the vehicle. Move on to Step The doors do not close Continue following the instructions in the table P10 CENTRAL LOCKING NOT WORKING 1 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment to the diagnostic socket and check the following at the CAN: that there are no Nodes activated that there are no faulty control units Move on to Step 1. Driver's door node, passenger door node, luggage compartment node not activated 1. Check the node supply and condition (Wiring Diagram ) E7015 ALARM 2. Driver's door, passenger door, luggage compartment and Body Computer Node faulty 2. Carry out the fault diagnosis and follow the instructions for the diagnostic equipment. 2 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Keeping the Examiner diagnostic equipment connected to the diagnostic socket, check the following at the Body Computer Node in active diagnosis ambient: the operation of the door locking and unlocking control Move on to Step The doors do not close Replace body computer See in Op. 5505A32 BODY COMPUTER - R.R. 3 CHECK ON CORRECT OPERATION ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the fault is no longer present

The siren is connected to the Body Computer Node via the A-BUS dialogue line. The siren is operated and controlled by the Body Computer Node via a series of encrypted messages; if there is a failure the Body Computer Node detects and memorizes the causes of the malfunction. STEP OPERATIONS TO BE CARRIED OUT TEST RESULTS 1 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment to the diagnostic socket and check the following at the Body Computer Node in parameters ambient: In errors ambient: the presence of the siren that there are no faults with the siren that there are no faults with the A-BUS Move on to Step 1. Siren faulty Move on to Step 2. Fault at A-BUS Move on to Step 3. Siren not present 3. Check the conformity of the vehicle 2 ELECTRICAL SYSTEM CHECK. ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the siren supply and earth (Wiring Diagram ) E7015 ALARM Move on to Step Fault with electrical equipment Restore the electrical connection (Wiring Diagram ) E7015 ALARM 3 ELECTRICAL SYSTEM CHECK. ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the continuity and the insulation of the A-BUS line between the Body Computer Node Computer and Siren (Wiring Diagram ) E7015 ALARM Move on to Step Fault at A-BUS line Restore the electrical connection (Wiring Diagram ) E7015 ALARM 4 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment to the diagnostic socket and check the following at the Body Computer Node in parameters ambient: the operation of the siren Move on to Step The siren is not activated Replace the siren See in Op. 5580E40 ANTI-THEFT SIREN - R.R. 5 CHECK ON CORRECT OPERATION ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the fault is no longer present Fault persists Replace body computer See in Op. 5505A32 BODY COMPUTER - R.R.

When the alarm is switched on using the remote control, the system is activated correctly but the volumetric sensors do not intervene. The volumetric sensors are located in the roof node and are connected to the Body Computer Node via the A-BUS dialogue line. The volumetric sensors are operated and controlled by the Body Computer Node via a series of encrypted messages and can be excluded by the customer using the special button. If there is a failure the Body Computer Node detects and memorizes the causes of the malfunction STEP OPERATIONS TO BE CARRIED OUT TEST RESULTS 1 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment to the diagnostic socket and check the following at the Body Computer NodeIn parameters ambient: In errors ambient: the presence of the volumetric sensors that there are no faults with the volumetric sensors Move on to Step 1. Volumetric sensors faulty 1. Replace the sensor module integrated in the courtesy light [PR.5580E50] 2. Volumetric sensors not present 2. Check the conformity of the vehicle 2 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment to the diagnostic socket and check the following at the Body Computer NodeIn active diagnosis ambient the operation of the volumetric modules Move on to Step The volumetric module is not working Replace body computer See in Op. 5505A32 BODY COMPUTER - R.R. 3 CHECK ON CORRECT OPERATION ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the fault is no longer present

The tilt sensors are located on the roof node and are connected to the Body Computer Node via the A-BUS dialogue line. The tilt sensor is operated and controlled by the Body Computer Node via a series of encrypted messages and can be excluded by the customer using the special button. In the case of a failure the Body Computer Node detects and memorizes the causes of the malfunction. STEP OPERATIONS TO BE CARRIED OUT TEST RESULTS 1 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment to the diagnostic socket and check the following at the Body Computer Node:In parameters ambient In errors ambient the presence of the tilt sensor that there are no problems relating to the tilt sensor Move on to Step 1. Tilt sensor faulty 1. Replace the sensor module integrated in the courtesy light 2. Tilt sensor not present 2. Check the conformity of the vehicle 2 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment to the diagnostic socket and check the following at the Body Computer Node:In active diagnosis ambient the operation of the tilt module Move on to Step The tilt sensor is not working Replace body computer See in Op. 5505A32 BODY COMPUTER - R.R. 3 CHECK ON CORRECT OPERATION ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the fault is no longer present

the height adjustment is controlled by a joystick on the seat connected to the Driving Position Node; the possible adjustments are: completely raising or lowering the seat or tilting backwards or forwards. The Driving Position Node is connected to two motors located under the seat for the adjustments. The potentiometric sensors connected to the motors are designed to memorize the seat position. When the speed of the vehicle exceeds 10 Km/h the adjustment of the driver's seat by recalling the position memorized is not possible.
