1. Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment pressure transducer to the return pipe to the tank (1a). Turn the ignition key to the ON position. Within 30 seconds check that the pressure reading on the gauge is less than 1 bar. The fuel pump in the tank should switch off after 30 seconds. Make sure that the taps and the adjustment screws at the side of the pressure gauge are open (except the ones of the ducts not connected to the system).

1. Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment pressure transducer between the diesel filter (1a) and the pressure pump (1b) (connect it to the filter outlet). Turn the ignition key to the ON position. Within 30 seconds check that the pressure reading on the gauge is less than 1 bar. The fuel pump in the tank should switch off after 30 seconds. Make sure that the taps and the adjustment screws at the side of the pressure gauge are open (except the ones of the ducts not connected to the system).

Disconnect the electrical connections from all the injectors. 1. Disconnect the fuel recirculation pipes from all the injectors. Constrict the pipe so that no fuel comes out during the test. Turn the ignition key to the AVV position for 5 seconds and visually inspect the amount of recirculation fuel coming out of the injector connections making sure that it is even and not very extensive.

Disconnect the electrical connections from all the injectors. 1. Disconnect the fuel recirculation pipes from all the injectors. Constrict the pipe so that no fuel comes out during the test. Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment. Display the "diesel pressure measured" and "engine rpm" parameters on the "Control Unit Test" parameters screen. Turn the ignition key to the AVV position for 5 seconds and check that the fuel pressure is above 300 bar with the engine speed above 200 rpm.

Disconnect the pressure sensor from the intake manifold Connect tool n° 1.870.752.000 to the intake manifold Description Code Function . Connector 1.870.752.000 Turbocharging pressure check Connect the pressure transducer to the tool. Position the Examiner / Examiner Plus diagnostic equipment in the passenger compartment and make the connections. Select "pressure gauge" on the Examiner / Examiner Plus and prepare for the acquisition of data in "intake pressure" mode with a 2000 mmHg end of scale and selection time of 10 seconds. Road test the vehicle (sticking to the speed limits in force) as follows: On a motorway route, let the vehicle reach 2000 rpm in 4th gear. Initiate the acquistion by pressing start on the diagnostic equipment and 2 seconds later fully depress the accelerator pedal until the engine speed is 3500 rpm. Once this speed is reached completely release the accelerator pedal. Display the resulting graph and in the pressure constant section, with the exception of the initial peak, the reading should be 1900 - 2100 mbar (1444 - 1596 mmHg) corresponding to a supercharging value of 900 - 1100 mbar. On a motorway route, let the vehicle reach 2000 rpm in 4th gear. Initiate the acquistion by pressing start on the diagnostic equipment and 2 seconds later fully depress the accelerator pedal until the engine speed is 3500 rpm. Once this speed is reached completely release the accelerator pedal. Display the resulting graph and in the pressure constant section, with the exception of the initial peak, the reading should be 1900 - 2100 mbar (1444 - 1596 mmHg) corresponding to a supercharging value of 900 - 1100 mbar.

Visually inspect that during starting (ignition key in AVV position) the turbocharger actuator connecting rod (turbine stator vanes adjustment device) moves by around 10 mm in the direction of the actuator. CHECK USING THE EXAMINER With the engine switched off, connect connector EX09 and transducer EX06 in the section of pipe between the actuator and the solenoid valve. Select intake pressure measuring gauge in the instrument ambient. Start up the engine and let it idle, then wait until pressure pressure stabilizes. The reading should be between 250 and 350 mmHg (2400 Stage 3 engines). The graphic acquisition of the pressure trend can be carried out by selecting either the 2000 or 4000 mmHg scale.

Discharge the vacuum in the brake servo, with the engine switched off, by repeatedly pressing and releasing the brake pedal forcefully Start up the engine without accelerating with the pedal depressed. After a few seconds, check that brake pedal is operating in accordance with the increase in pressure due to the action of the brake servo. Release the brake pedal and swith off the engine without operating the pedal again. After about 10 minutes with the engine switched off, operate the brake pedal and check that when it is operated for the first time the extent it is lowered corresponds to the brake servo and that the operation becomes gradually harder.

With the engine switched off, connect connector EX09 and transducer EX06 in the section of pipe between the actuator and the solenoid valve. Pre-select intake pressure measuring gauge in the instrument ambient. Start up the engine and let it idle, then wait until pressure pressure stabilizes. The reading should be between 250 and 350 mmHg (2400 Stage 3 engines). The graphic acquisition of the pressure trend can be carried out by selecting either the 2000 or 4000 mmHg scale.

The test should be carrried out at an outside temperature TE of between 18° C and 30° C, on a vehicle stablized at that temperature. If the vehicle comes from an outside ambient with a temperature < 18° C or > 30° C, it must be stabilized for 1 hour with the windows open. Open the ventilation vent flaps (in the dashboard) and insert a thermometer (or suitable tool) about 3 mm into the centre vent through the fins. Close the doors and windows. Start up the engine and keep it idling, with the air conditioning system switched off (button 1 pressed for at least 1.5 seconds on the air flow rate decrease control side. Switch off the recirculation (button 2 with LEDs off) Place the temperature selector in the MAX cold position (one of the 3 knobs turned in an anti-clockwise direction until LO appears on the two temperature displays). The system is automatically in the Mono and Vent position. Switch off the air conditioning (LED in button 4 off). Place the fan speed selector in the top speed position (button 1 pressed on the flow rate increase control side until 12 bars are shown on the centre display). 1 minute after the previous operations have been completed read the temperature T 0 on the thermometer and make a note of it. Check that it does not exceed the outside temperature T E by more than 5° C Switch on the air conditioning (LED in button 4 off). 2 minutes after switching on the air conditioning, check that the temperature reading on the thermometer has decreased by at least 8° C compared with the initial value T 0 . 5 minutes after switching on the air conditioning, check that the temperature reading on the thermometer has decreased by at least 12° C compared with the initial value T 0 .

Start up the engine and keep it idling. Connect the air conditioning system repressuring equipment [5040A10] in order to be able to read the low pressure (1°) and high pressure (1b) values. Make sure that the compressor is switched off. Switch off the recirculation (LED in button off). Press the fan speed selector until 6 full bars are shown on the monitor. Turn the temperature selector until it is in the maximum cold position (LOW). Check, on the repressurizing equipment low and high pressure gauges, that the pressure values are within 5 bar for T E at around 20°C, and around 6 bar for T E at about 30°C Switch on the air conditioning (LED in button on). Within 1 minute check that the reading on the low pressure gauge is 2. 5 - 3.0 bar and the reading on the high pressure gauge is 15 - 16 bar. Wait until the engine cooling fan comes on. Check that the pressure reading on the low pressure gauge is 1.5 - 1.8 bar, whilst the reading on the high pressure gauge is 10 - 12 bar. Check that the engine cooling fan switches off when the high pressure goes down to 11 - 12 bar.

- Procedure for draining the system. - Position the vehicle on the lift. See in Op. 7040D50 ENGINE COMPARTMENT UPPER SOUND INSULATION SHIELD - R.R. - Raise the lift. - With the engine cold, remove the engine coolant reservoir plug. - Position a suitable container for collecting the fluid under the vehicle. - Press the lower radiator hose fastening tabs and release the hose from the connector on the radiator in order to drain the coolant. - Instructions for refilling the system. 1. Reconnect the lower radiator hose and fasten it by pushing the rapid connector until the clip engages. 2. Open the bleed screw (2a) on the radiator and the bleed screw (2b) on the heater supply hose. - Slowly introduce coolant via the filler located on the expansion tank until it comes out of the bleed screw on the radiator outlet hose. - Then close the bleed screw on the radiator. - Continue with the refilling until coolant comes out of the bleed opening on the heater supply hose, then close the screw on the actual bleed opening. Facilitate the removal of the remaining air by repeatedly squeezing the engine/radiator hose. - Continue refilling until the coolant in the reservoir is at the level of the MAX notch on the tank. 3. Tighten the engine coolant reservoir cap. - Start up the engine and let it idle for about 2 minutes. - Check that the air conditioning system is switched off. - Then carry out gradual, periodic (every 30 secs.) acceleration until the engine speed is around 3/4 of maximum power rpm. - This operation should be carried out so that the radiator fan cuts in. - After the fan cuts in, keep the engine idling for a further 4 minutes. - Make sure that hot air comes out of the passenger compartment vents to confirm that the coolant is circulating. - Then switch off the engine and leave it to cool down. - After having let the engine cool down, check the level of the fluid in the tank, topping it up, if necessary, until it reaches the MAX reference. At the end of this operation, make sure that at least the same amount of water collected after the circuit was drained has been introduced otherwise repeat the heating operation to allow all of the air to be removed from the circuit and then introduce the remaining coolant. - Below is a description of the manual procedure and the procedure using the diagnostic equipment for the electronic injection/ignition control unit self-learning. Carry out the following operations, the first time the vehicle is started up, each time the throttle casing or the engine management control unit is replaced. Do not press the accelerator pedal, the brake pedal or the clutch pedal during this procedure, from the moment the instrument panel is supplied to the end of the learning procedure. - Procedure with diagnostic equipment. - Make sure that the ignition key is in the OFF position. - Connect the equipment to the diagnostic socket and place the knob in position 3. Description Code Function . MPX 97 Switch 1.806.365.000 Control unit self-learning - Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment. - Turn the ignition key to the ON position (engine switched off). - Wait for the throttle casing check to be carried out, until the positive result of the learning procedure is confirmed on the diagnostic equipment. - Turn the ignition key to the OFF position. - Using the Examiner, check that the idle self-learning procedure has been correctly completed (THROTTLE LOWER END OF TRAVEL POSITION SELF-LEARNING - Completed). If the self-learning procedure is not correct, turn the ignition key to the OFF position and repeat the procedure described above. If the problems persist, check that the diagnostic cable is correctly connected and that the equipment is working properly. - Manual procedure. - Turn the ignition key to the ON position (engine switched off). - Wait for 60 seconds, the time required for the control unit to check the spring inside the throttle casing and the minimum/maximum throttle angle positions. - Turn the ignition key to the OFF position. - Wait for 10 seconds, the time required for the control unit to record the values learnt in the Eprom. After having carried out the self-learning procedure, the supply to the engine management control unit can be removed (battery disconnected), if necessary, without losing the data recorded.

Avoid rapid recharging at all costs. In order to recharge the battery correctly it is necessary to use a battery charger recommended by the Service Department (e.g. ISEAT CB1): these battery chargers operate at a "constant voltage" and recognize the condition of the battery and automatically determine the best recharging cycle; in this way the battery can be almost 100% recharged Always disconnect the negative battery terminal before recharging. Never touch the battery terminals with your hands whilst recharging and keep naked flames away from the battery. Only operate the battery charger after connecting the leads to the battery. If the no load battery voltage measured is less than 12.10 V, then recharging is not advisable and the battery should be replaced (see op. 5530B10)

- With batteries that have a "water gauge" it is possible to monitor the level of the electrolyte and the battery charge depending on the colour of this indicator: - a bright colour indicates that the electrolyte level is too low; top up with distilled water; - a dark colour without a green area in the middle indicates that the electrolyte level is correct, but the charge is low: recharge the battery; - a dark colour with a green area in the middle indicates that the electrolyte level and the charge are correct: no intervention is required. - For further details see Description and Operation 5530 - Current generation. - The above device does not, however, offer absolute guarantees surrounding the correct measurement of the battery charge which must be checked more thoroughly in a service situation. - Proceed as follows: - check the no load battery voltage using the test equipment recommended by the Service Department (e.g. "MICRO 360"). - Depending on the voltage figures measured for the battery charge, proceed as follows: See in Op. 5530B10 BATTERY - R.R. - with the voltage below 12.10V, replace the battery See in Op. 5530B14 BATTERY- Recharging - with the voltage above 12.10V, but below 12.50V, recharge the battery - with the voltage above 12.50V, the battery is working properly. - If necessary, top up the electrolyte as follows: - carefully remove the cap band; - top up using distilled and deionized water, taking care not to spill the electrolyte. The electrolyte liquid is acidic and could cause damage to eyes, hands and clothing. A low electrolyte level often indicates a problem with the operation of the alternator, in particular the electronic voltage regulator.

- Check the tyre inlation pressure and, if necessary, correct it. - Check that the tank is at least 50% full. - Check the vehicle geometry and, if necessary, correct it. - Check that the load carrying compartment is empty. - Check that the battery voltage is > 10.5 V. 1. Position the vehicle in the specially designed calibration area as illustrated in the diagram below, trying to position it at right angles to the sliding guide (1a) for the radar mirror (1b) at a distance of 120 cm (± 5 cm), referring to the lines traced on the ground. If the difference for the driving axis of the vehicle is > 5°, then alignment is impossible. - Connect the diagnostic socket and make sure that all the doors are closed and remain so throughout the entire alignment procedure. 1. Fasten the adjustable radar mirror (1a) to the sliding guide (1b) on the same side of the vehicle as the radar is fitted using the locking lever (1c). 2. Check that the mirror (2a) is positioned centrally in relation to the reference lever (2b). 1. Move the rapid tightening clamp as illustrated in the diagram. 1. Secure the rapid tightening clamp to the radar side rear wheel. If the vehicle is fitted with polished alloy wheels, they must be protected in the area where the rapid tightening clamps are fitted to avoid damaging the surface. It should be borne in mind that the protection fitted should be the same size in order not to alter the support plane for the rapid tightening clamps. 2. Fit the laser wheel in the special housing in the rapid tightening clamp. 3. Place the laser wheel in a horizontal position and secure it tightening the locking bolt. - Position the radar mirror opposite the laser source. 1. Using the radar mirror spirit level (1a), adjust the vertical position of the mirror using the special knob (1b). - Switch on the laser source. NEVER look directly at the laser source ! - Make sure that there is noone and/or nothing in the area between the radar mirror and the laser source. 1. Loosen the radar mirror horizontal alignment device adjustment screw. 2. The horizontal position of the mirror should be adjusted, using the screw, until the laser beam (2a) from the laser wheel, is reflected by the mirror on the vertical line (2b) for the projection surface (2c) of the actual laser wheel. If the laser reflection point does not appear on the projection surface, move the laser source until it is displayed. - In order to prevent alignment errors due to possible distortions of the alloy wheel rims, rotate the rapid tightening clamp by around 30° in a clockwise direction and memorize the laser reflection point on the laser wheel surface, repeat the operation rotating the clamp through 30° in an anti-clockwise direction in relation to the original position. 1. If the alloy rim is not distorted, the three laser wheel reflection points should be along a vertical line. 2. If the alloy rim is distorted, the two reflection points ( +30°, -30°) may be on the laser wheel emission surface. In this case, position the clamp so that the laser is reflected about halfway between the points. After this the horizontal position of the mirror should be adjusted, using the special screw, until the laser beam is reflected on the vertical line for the laser wheel projection surface. 1. Rest the diaphragm on the floor and place it directly in front of the laser wheel. 2. Adjust the height of the diaphragm, loosening the vertical adjustment screw (2) so that the radius of the laser (2b) passes through the slot in the diaphragm and is reflected on the mirror. 1. Position the diaphragm on the floor by the axis for the radar side front wheel hub centre line. 2. Check that the laser beam passes through the slot in the diaphragm and is reflected on the radar mirror. Otherwise, adjust the laser wheel so that the beam is aligned with the diaphragm slot. - Position the diaphragm once again in contact with the laser wheel in order to check that the diaphragm is correctly adjusted. If the laser beam does not pass through the slot in the diaphragm, adjust the height of the latter using the special screw. Carry out a further check, positioning the diaphragm by the axis for the centre line of the front wheel hub. Proceed as described until the laser radius passes through the slot in the diaphragm by both wheels (front and rear). - Remove the diaphragm. 1. Adjust the position of the mirror (1a) in accordance with the vertical axis, using the knurled screw (1b), until the laser beam (1c) is reflected near (within a circular area of 1cm in diameter approx) the outlet opening (1d) of the laser wheel projection surface (1e). If, whilst adjusting the angle of the mirror in relation to the vertical axis, there is a non alignment in relation to the horizontal axis, correct this by regulating the horizontal adjustment screw as described previously. 1. Read the values shown on the scales "V" (1a) and "H" (1b), for the radar mirror vertical and horizontal adjustments, respectively, and make a note of them. - Switch off the laser wheel. - Remove the laser wheel from the rapid tightening clamp. - Remove the rapid tightening clamp from the rear wheel. - Carry out the same operations on the opposite side of the vehicle. 1. Position the radar mirror (1a) in front of the radar (1b) and secure it. - Check that the mirror is positioned centrally in relation to the reference lever. - Check the planarity of the radar mirror using the spirit level and, correct it, if necessary. - Take the average of values "H" and "V" measured during the alignment of the mirror on the two sides of the vehicle and set the average values in the radar mirror using the adjustment screws. - Carry out the radar beam alignment procedure using the Examiner. - In order to check the operation of the Adaptive Cruise Control, after having aligned the radar beam to the vehicle thrust axis, the following road test must be carried out on all vehicles. The road test should be carried out following the road traffic regulations in force. - Start up the engine and let the vehicle reach a speed above 30 km/h. - Activate the Adaptive Cruise Control (if it was already activated, switch it off and then back on again) and check that there are no malfunction signals in the control panel. 1. Adjust the steering column switch unit lever from low (SET+) and from high (SET-) and remove your foot from the accelerator pedal. - Check that the speed set is shown on the instrument panel display and that the same speed is shown by the vehicle speedometer. - Operate the SET+ control to set a speed of 70 km/h on the Adaptive Cruise Control: check that the vehicle accelerates correctly. - Operate the SET - control to set a speed of 30 km/h on the Adaptive Cruise Control: check that the vehicle slows down and the braking system intervenes. - Get behing a vehicle B which is driving slower than the speed set for vehicle A being tested and check that the Adaptive Cruise Control intervenes slowing down vehicle A and assuming a constant distance from B: check that the presence of vehicle B is shown by the instrument panel display and the time delay of A in relation to B. When overtaking vehicles that are driving more slowly in the right hand lane there should not be inappropriate braking. The test should be carried out on a straight road or round bends of more than 500 m and the speed between vehicles A and B should not exceed 50 km/h. - Select a different time distance using the special control and check whether the distance between the two vehicle increases or decreases. The variation in the distance between the two vehicles is only noticed at an ambient temperature of > 3°C. If the ambient temperature is equal to 3°C the Adaptive Cruise Control is automatically positioned at the maximum distance.

Release and remove the seal following the procedure described below. - Use a bodywork drier which produces hot air at between 35 and 40°C. - Point the air towards one of the two ends for 10-15 seconds from a distance of around 20-30 cm. - Remove about 5-10 cm of the end avoiding rapid movements or angles that could cause breakages. - Lift up the end removed previously and point the hot air between the adhesive and the paintwork from around 20-30 cm away for 15-20 seconds, then start pulling the seal towards you continuing to heat it using the drier to facilitate its removal and reduce the presence of any residues of adhesive or foam. Refitting Removing - Clean the door surround using paper soaked in heptane starting from the top centre line of the door working downwards in a clockwise direction and from the top centre line working downwards in an anti-clockwise direction until the door surround is completed. Removing Refitting Open the boot lid. Turn the ring nut in an anti-clockwise direction to the end of travel position. 1. Insert a screwdriver with a flat blade (1a) in the buffer (1b) between the ring nut and the support. Use the screwdriver to get the ring nut out completely. 1. Remove the buffer. Proceed in the same way with the remaining buffer. Refitting Removing Place the buffer in position and place the ring nut in the end of travel position by pressing it manually. Turn the ring nut in a clockwise direction to the end of travel position. Proceed in the same way with the remaining buffer. Close the boot lid placing sheets of paper between the buffers and the stops on the bodyshell. Check that there is a slight clearance between the buffers and the stops (the sheets of paper should not tear when they are removed). If the clearance is too small, check the alignment of the boot lid and the adjustment of the lock striker. Op. 7025B10 BOOT LID - SQUARE and repeat the check on the clearance. If there is no clearance between the buffers and the stops this involves excessive force and results in the boot lid electric lock not working properly.

Description The electrical system is designed to increase the car's safety level and prevent the possibility of fires and other consequences of electrical malfunctions. State-of-the-art connectors have been introduced to rule out the possibility of many connection defects. Power is distributed via the junction units and/or fuses boxes. These are connected to control elements (relays and static actuators) to ensure maximum electrical protection and minimum complexity. All wiring looms have been made modular by changing the way functions are distributed inside the connectors and replacing welds with short-circuiting joints. The main safety solutions adoptd are as follows: power supplies protected by maxifuses for the electrical system switch, in the case of short circuit, immediately downstream of the battery (see detail below); the only leads excluded from the maxifuses (starter motor and alternator) are located in protected areas; the layout of the whole system is optimised to reduce the risk of damage in the case of faults or accidents; wiring installation has been optimised to reduced incorrect positioning and noise due to vibrations; all wires offer high resistance to abrasion; the wires in the engine are of special type , resistant to high temperature and protected with piping sheaths; wires in the passenger compartment are protected by corrugated pipes and felted tapes to reduce noise levels; the main connections coem with secondary lock terminals and lever locks to prevent terminal deformation. All systems and electrical equipment are supplied by the battery at a voltage of 12V. The battery is recharged by the alternator during engine operation See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING The main supply lines are protected by maxifuses grouped in a box located directly on the positive battery terminal and connected directly to the terminal. A protective plastic case prevents accidental contacts with the battery positive terminal. The maxifuse control unit contains an automatic battery disconnector device in line with the battery terminal that cuts off supply to the starter motor/recharging lead The box contains the follwoing maxifuses that are labelled according to the circuits protected: CVM: engine compartment junction unit supply CPL1: underfacia junction unit supply; CPL2: underfacia junction unit supply; CVB: load compartment junction unit supply Some circuits are continuously supplied, even with the car at a standstill and the key out because they are connected directly to the battery. Other circuits are supplied by turning the ignition key to various positions: insert the key and turn it through one click to ON. This supplies numerous circuits that are described as ignition-operated (INT and 15/54 lines); the second click - AVV position - supplies the starter motor (line "50"). Other circuits (those that absorbe most power) are now disconnected to ensure a maximum current flow to the motor; (INT/A line) when the ignition is removed, the Exterior Lighting Control unit may be set to PARK to supply the side lights even with the key out ("STAZ" and "POS" lines); See E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. PLATE LIGHTS the lines used to distribute power to the various services are shown in the wiring diagrams for the various functions and systems. This general diagram shows all lines as they leave the battery and the MAXIFUSE box and the ignition key. See specific diagrams for greater detail.

Operational Description All electrical systems and circuits are supplied by battery A001. The main supply lines are protected by the maxifuse box on battery B099 that contains fuses labelled according to the circuits protected: CVM: engine compartment junction unit supply CPL1: underfacia junction unit supply; CPL2: underfacia junction unit supply; CVB: load compartment junction unit supply Other circuits are supplied by turning the ignition key H001 to various positions: in MAR position, numerous protected ignition-operated circuits are supplied (INT and 15/54): pin 2 connector B and pin 1 connector A; AVV starter motor is supplied; (line "50"), relay R20 to inhibit start-up of engine bay junction unitB001, steering lock control unit M089 responsible for releasing the steering See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING in PARK position, side lights (POS and STAZ line) are supplied from the Exterior Lighting Control Unit H092. Boot control unit M063 controls the automatic battery disconnection device function. It receives as input a signal from inertia switch I050, which cuts out the circuit and thus stops dangerous fuel outflows, and forwards it to the battery disconnection switch from pins 33 and 34 of connector F respectively. A switch on the fuse box B099 cuts off the supply of all circuits.

Description The electrical system is designed to increase the car's safety level and prevent the possibility of fires and other consequences of electrical malfunctions. State-of-the-art connectors have been introduced to rule out the possibility of many connection defects. Power is distributed via the junction units and/or fuses boxes. These are connected to control elements (relays and static actuators) to ensure maximum electrical protection and minimum complexity. All wiring looms have been made modular by changing the way functions are distributed inside the connectors and replacing welds with short-circuiting joints. The main safety solutions adoptd are as follows: power supplies protected by maxifuses for the electrical system switch, in the case of short circuit, immediately downstream of the battery (see detail below); the only leads excluded from the maxifuses (starter motor and alternator) are located in protected areas; the layout of the whole system is optimised to reduce the risk of damage in the case of faults or accidents; wiring installation has been optimised to reduced incorrect positioning and noise due to vibrations; all wires offer high resistance to abrasion; the wires in the engine are of special type , resistant to high temperature and protected with piping sheaths; wires in the passenger compartment are protected by corrugated pipes and felted tapes to reduce noise levels; the main connections coem with secondary lock terminals and lever locks to prevent terminal deformation. All systems and electrical equipment are supplied by the battery at a voltage of 12V. The battery is recharged by the alternator during engine operation See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING The main supply lines are protected by maxifuses grouped in a box located directly on the positive battery terminal and connected directly to the terminal. A protective plastic case prevents accidental contacts with the battery positive terminal. The maxifuse control unit contains an automatic battery disconnector device in series with the battery terminal that cuts off the supply for the starter motor/recharging lead. The box contains the follwoing maxifuses that are labelled according to the circuits protected: CVM: engine compartment junction unit supply CVB: load compartment junction unit supply CPL2: underfacia junction unit supply; CPL1: underfacia junction unit supply; Some circuits are continuously supplied, even with the car at a standstill and the key out because they are connected directly to the battery. Other circuits are supplied by turning the ignition key to various positions: insert the key and turn it through one click to ON. This supplies numerous circuits that are described as ignition-operated (INT and 15/54 lines); the second click - AVV position - supplies the starter motor (line "50"). Other circuits (those that absorbe most power) are now disconnected to ensure a maximum current flow to the motor; (INT/A line) when the ignition is removed, the Exterior Lighting Control unit may be set to PARK to supply the side lights even with the key out ("STAZ" and "POS" lines); See E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. PLATE LIGHTS the lines used to distribute power to the various services are shown in the wiring diagrams for the various functions and systems. This general diagram shows all lines as they leave the battery and the MAXIFUSE box and the ignition key. See specific diagrams for greater detail.

Description This vehicle is equipped with a CAN (Controller Area Network) system of electrical connections it involves a software and hardware solution which is designed to manage the resources on the vehicle efficiently allowing: the sharing of information between the various electronic units; the intergration of several electronic units through the network; a high network information exchange speed; advantages in economic terms because there is a considerable reduction in the wiring/connectors inside the vehicle; considerably improved quality and reliability. The advantage of using a CAN system stems from the fact that the communication between the various electronic control units takes place with a large number of signals to be managed. For this reason the signals travel on a CAN type serial bus where one wire is high level (H) and the other low level (L); these signals on the CAN bus are differential types, i.e. the value assigned to the bit is represented by the difference between the CAN-H and CAN-L voltage levels. The different electronic units which make up the system, known as network nodes, are connected to the CAN by means of communication interfaces known as transreceivers; these connection interfaces, integrated in the electronic units, constitute the gate for sending/reading the information at the CAN or at the serial lines. The exchange of information at CAN type serial lines is only possible using a transmission protocol which is the collection of rules that allow communication between two or more nodes. The main element of the network is the body computer. The body computer control unit is entrusted with waking up the network when the ignition key is turned to the ON (INT) position, if there is a problem with the body computer this task is entrusted to the instrument panel. The body computer also carries out the functions of checking the network which make it possible to provide information on: the network activities status; the functional failure status of the individual electronic units (nodes); a possible CAN failure status. The various electronic units process the various signals coming from the corresponding sensors both for their own management and for other control units to which they are sent via the CAN. The structure consists of three CAN communication networks which connect nodes belonging to the three different areas (vehicle dynamic control and bodywork functions) and a certain number of complementary serial lines used for diagnosis and other specific functions: C-CAN for dynamic vehicle control (high speed); B-CAN for the management of standard bodywork functions (low speed); I-CAN for transporting data and commands relating to on-board information (low speed); w serial line for immobilizer recovery (release code at the engine management control unit when the C-CAN at the Body Computer is not working properly); k diagnostic line for the engine management control unit / automatic transmission control unit; k diagnostic line for the Air Bag control unit; k diagnostic line for the braking system control unit; k diagnostic line for the dashboard area (power steering control unit, headlamp alignment corrector control unit) k diagnostic line for the rear area (electric braking control unit, controlled suspension control unit); k diagnostic line for the front area (cruise adaptive control unit, braking system check control unit, additional heater control unit); A-BUS serial line for management of wipers, safety, exterior lighting which connects the body computer, roof control unit, alarm siren control unit, windscreen wiper cotnrol unit; serial line for info-telematic control unit/climate control system control unit for data display; two-way serial line for body computer/rear lights control unit for the fault diagnosis of the rear light clusters. The C-CAN and B-CAN networks are connected to one another by a gateway for transferring joint information located in the body computer. The fault diagnosis of the nodes connected to the B-CAN is carried out via the CAN, whilst for those connected to the C-CAN this is carried out by means of the specific K lines See E8010 DIAGNOSTIC MULTIPLE CONNECTOR Both flow into the EOBD connector on the Body Computer. the engine management control unit; the braking system control unit; the braking system control unit; the electric braking control unit; the slewing control unit; the steering angle control unit; the steering geometry control unit; the cruise control system control unit. The following nodes are connected to the body computer via the C-CAN: The following nodes are connected to the Body Computer via the B-CAN: the climate control system control unit; the steering wheel node control unit; the driver's door control unit; the passenger door control unit; the roof control unit; the luggage compartment control unit; the passive entry control unit; the parking sensors control unit; the instrument panel control unit; the steering lock control unit; the info-telematic control unit. The following are connected via the I-CAN: the info-telematic control unit to the TV tuner, managing the television controls. The power distribution takes place by means of the junction units and/or fuse boxes, connected to the control elements (relays and static actuators) in order to ensure the maximum level of electrical protection and the least complex wiring See E1010 SUPPLY

Description The side lights are activated by means of a wheel on the exterior side light control unit POS, with the key on MAR. They may be activated with the key (or keyless-go knob) in STOP position and the exterior lighting control unit ring in PARK position. The number plate light and numerous other interior lights for lighting the passenger compartment, instruments and controls are activated together with the side lights (these are described and explained in the wiring diagrams for the relevant components). Information on activation and/or deactivation is sent via the CAN network: the side light warning light on the control panel is also turned on this way. if the turn signals are not active, the parking lights are turned on on both sides of the car. The number plate lights and side light warning light are also turned on if the turn signal is turned on on one side, the parking lights are turned on only on the corresponding side. The number plate light and side lights are not turned on. Description The left and right direction indicators are switched on by raising or lowering the special lever on the left of the steering column switch unit; the function is activated with the key-on. The hazard warning lights (left and right direction indicators operated simultaneously) are activated via a button in the centre of the dashboard and all the direction indicators are activated at the same time. The switching on of the direction indicators/hazard warning lights is managed by the Body Computer which also controls the flashing frequency and sends it via the CAN serial network to the other nodes. The instrument panel receives the command to switch on the two direction indicator warning lgihts via the CAN: which, together with the flashing of the warning lights, also provides a low frequency acoustic signal. The correct operation of the lights is controlled by the direction indicators check function and the following is controlled for each of the two circuits (right and left branches of the vehicle): open circuit or bulb missing for charges of 21 W (right front, right rear, left front, left rear) short-circuit to earth (bulb s.c. or wiring s.c. to earth) short circuit to VB (wiring short circuited to Vbatt). When one of the situations described above is ascertained, the Body Computer makes the failure status available to the CAN: this information is displayed on the instrument panel. There is also a failure signal for one of the 21 W front or rear bulbs with an increase in the nominal flashing of the warning lights in the instrument panel and the buzzer. The flashing frequency of the exterior lights remains unchanged. The direction indicators are also lit up to signal the reception of the door locking/unlocking command from the remote control (or CID transponder). See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING See E7015 ALARM An LED at the back of the control button also comes on synchronized with the flashing of the exterior lights; this function is always activated.

Description The logics for switching the (front and rear) courtesy lights on/off are centralized in the Body Computer. If some of the courtesy lights are not operated directly by the Body Computer but by other nodes, the command to switch on/off is sent via the CAN from the Body Computer to the latter via a signal composed of two bit in order to differentiate between switching on and switching off with or without a dimmer. The dimmer time of 2 seconds is always aded to the times described, for both switching on and switching off. all Passive Entry versions The (unstable) button the front courtesy light acts for both the front courtesy light and the rear courtesy light: in effect, if the courtesy lights are off, they are switched on when the button is pressed; if the courtesy lights are on, they are switched off when the button is pressed. The left/right front map reading lights, like the rear ones, are activated independently of the opening of the doors, via a specific command; the functions are completely local. The timed activatation of the front and rear courtesy lights is basically determined by four different operating logics: the front/rear door states (open/closed); in a key-off situation (OFF); according to the locking/unlocking of the doors via the Passive Entry control unit; the activation of the inertia switch. For the first functional logic, opening any door (front or rear) causes the front and rear courtesy lights to come on, both for a timed period (managed by the Body Computer) of 3 minutes. If during the period of 3 minutes (or with any door open) another door is opened, the current timed period is rest and starts again for another 3 minutes. At the end of the timed period both courtesy lights should go off. If, during the timed period of 3 minutes, all the doors are closed again, the timing of 3 minutes is interrupted and a second timed period of 20 seconds is activated which is interrupted if the ignition key is turned to the key-on position (INT). In all the cases described, the courtesy lights should come on and go out simultaneously and with a dimmer effect. In the second logic, when the key is extracted from the ignition (key-off) a timed period of 20 seconds is activated leading to a dimmed switching off. If the (unstable) button in the front courtesy light is pressed in the key-off (OFF) condition, a timed period of 15 minutes is activated. The front and rear courtesy lights respectively are activated in the door locking/unlocking function via the Passive Entry control unit; in the unlocking stage for 20 seconds; in the locking stage, on the other hand, for 1 second. In both cases the courtesy lights go out gradually. Lastly, if the inertia switch is activated the front and rear courtesy lights come on for 30 minutes. If the inertia switch is reset, the courtesy lights should go off.

Description When the boot is opened the light in the luggage compartment comes on and goes out when the boot is closed. Description Six ground lights (puddle lights) are located on the two front doors, the two rear doors and the door mirrors. The function is active under Key-on conditions (INT), Key-off conditions (STOP). The light activation strategy is managed by the Body Computer and also by various control units in the front doors and in the boot compartment by means of a CAN network. The puddle lights on the door mirrors are activated again when the doors are released via the remote control. When one of the two front doors is opened, the relevant puddle light comes on for 3 minutes. The light goes off at the end of this period. If the door is closed before the end of the set period, the bulb goes off immediately. When the "driver/passenger front door open" status is received on the CAN network, both control units on the front doros turn on the puddle lights on the driver and passenger side door mirrors. When one of the two rear doors is opened, however, both rear lights are turned on and the 3 minute timer is restarted. If both rear doors are closed within the timing period, the two puddle lights must go off. Both rear bulbs are connected in parallel.

An exterior door release control from the remote control unit is sent via alarm and door lock aerial P093 to the Body Computer M001 (pin 21 and 31 of connector B). Description The car is equipped with numerous light sources for optimal lighting of interior instruments and controls. Some of these are light under Key-on conditions (INT), others with the side lights on. Others are dimmable in accordance with a rheostat-controlled adjustment strategy managed by the Body Computer. The following controls are lit when the ignition is turned to INT: driver-side front handle lighting led; passenger-side front handle lighting led; left and right side rear handle lighting led. With the key in INT position enablement and side light command positions, the Body Computer manages the lighting of: ashtray; cigar lighter surround; power point in rear armrest; rear power point. Key-on (INT) and side light command (+lights) status are transmitted via the CAN network for other functions. Adjustment of interior lighting intensity level is activated by direct turning of the rotary control (potentiometric) on the exterior lighting control unit (CLE). The instrument panel downloads the adjustment command, shows the level (1 to 9) on the interior display and sends it via the CAN network to the other control units affected by the function. When the light dimmer adjustment control on the upper part of the display is adjusted, a "control brightness adjustment" message is displayed and the segments on a lighted bar at the bottom of the display are lit up/extinguished. The instrument panel fault warning light leds must not be subject to adjustment. If the side lights are deactivated, the displays are lit up and may be adjusted at all times.

Description The vehicle is equipped with a horn system consisting of two horns with different tones: one high tone horn and one low tone horn; the two horns sound simultaneously. The horns are operated by pressing the sides of the steering wheel cover. The horn circuit is protected by a fuse and is controlled by a special relay, both located in the engine compartment junction unit. For safety reasons, the horns can be operated at any time, even with the ignition switched OFF or the key extracted.

Operational Description The horn system is supplied by the R3 horn relay in the luggage compartment junction unit B001, the line protected by fuse F10 in the same junction unit and directly by the battery. The relay supplies the high tone horn P010 and the low tone horn P011.

Description The windscreen wash/wipe system is activated by the steering column switch unit located on the right of the steering wheel, with the following functions: there are five possible positions for the lever to which the following functions correspond: windscreen wiper off (stationary); intermittent/automatic operation (4 positions or 4 rain sensor settings); continuous slow operation (first speed); continuous slow operation (first speed); anti-panic temporary fast operation (unstable position). In the intermittent/automatic operation position there are four different functions for the steering column switch unit managed by the windscreen wiper control unit. Intermittent operation is also a function of the rain and dusk sensor (interfaced on the roof control unit) which, sends the windscreen wiper control unit a signal when the steering column switch unit is placed in the intermittent position. The frequency of the windscreen wiper strokes is automatically adjusted depending on the amount of water on the windscreen detected by the sensor. The Body Computer control unit acquires all the information both concerning the speed of the windscreen wiper strokes per minute and any possible failure of the rain sensor. In the latter case, or if the Body Computer does not receive information from the rain sensor via the A-BUS serial line (3 second timeout), the Body Computer sends a signal, via the CAN, to the instrument panel which displays the fault on the matrix display; as a result, the windscreen wiper control unit operates manually depending on the position of the steering column switch unit ring nut/lever. On receiving an insufficient windscreen washer fluid level signal, via the CAN, the instrument panel also displays the appropriate symbols and message on the display. The transmission of messages between the sensor and the windscreen wiper control unit takes place via the A-BUS serial line. The activation of the rain sensor involves a windscreen wiper arm stroke as feedback to confirm that it has been switched on. There are 4 possible settings for the sensor which is adjusted using the ring nut on the steering column switch unit lever. The "intelligent" windscreen washer logic is as follows: on a command to wash the windscreen, the windscreen wiper control unit activates the windscreen washer pump; after the pump has been activated for 0.5 seconds, the windscreen wiper is activated at the first speed; the pump and the windscreen wiper remain activated for the entire period that the command to wash the windscreen exists; when the control is released, the windscreen wiper control unit no longer activates the pump, whilst it still operates the windscreen wiper for a further three strokes; there is an additional stroke after six seconds at the first speed (if the windscreen wiper is not already activated). The device is temporarily excluded during starting (INT/A). The windscreen wiper and the windscreen washer can only be activated with the ignition switched ON (INT), with the functions being disabled with the ignition switched OFF.

Operational Description The electronic device inside the steering column switch unit H005 is supplied at pin 2 of connector A by the line contrlled by the ignition (INT) protected by fuse F51 of the junction unit under the dashboard B002. According to the function selected (windscreen wiping and/or washing), the steering column switch unit H005 (connector A) sends the following signals to the windscreen wiper control unit M079 (electro-mechanical and electronic control unit integrated in the windscreen wiper motor): from pin 9 for continuous slow operation (first speed) to pin 8; from pin 8 for continuous slow operation (first speed) to pin 7; from pin 11 for intermittent operation, determined by the steering column switch unit or the rain sensor, to pin 5; from pin 12 for the activation of the windscreen washer pump to pin 6. The windscreen wiper control unit M079 is supplied at pin 1 directly by the battery via the relay R12 and fuse F43, both housed in the junction unit under the dashboard B002. The windscreen washer pump, interfaced at the front/headlamp washer coupling D098, is supplied from pin 3 of control unit M079 at pin 4. The signal for enabling the intermitten function via the rain and dusk sensor K125, is sent via the A-BUS line from pin 10 of the windscreen wiper control unit M079. If the windscreen washer fluid level inside the reservoir is insufficient, then the info-telematic control unit M065 receives a negative signal, at pin 21 of connector A, from the switch interfaced with the front/headlamp washer coupling D098 (pin 2); this signal is sent via the B-CAN (pins 1 and 3 of connector A) to the instrument panel E050 (pins 3 and 4 of connector A) which displays the message and the symbol. Body Computer M001 receives an INT/A (key-on) signal from ignition switch H001 at pin 27 of connector D via fuse F31 of underfacia control unit B002. The Body Computer M001 also acquires information concerning the on/off status of the windscreen wiper and a possible failure of the rain sensor through the same line. These signals are transmitted via the B-CAN for other functions; the instrument panel E050 shows the failure of the sensor on the display thanks to the signals acquired at pins 3 and 4 of connector A.

Description The headlamp washer function is only activated if the dipped or main beam headlamps are switched on. The monostable activation command for the headlamp washer function is not a specific command, but it is the same as the one given via the steering column switch unit for the front windscreen washer function. The Body Computer acquires both the signal to activate the function and the one to control the dipped/main beam headlamps, thereby implementing the timed operation of the headlamp washer relay. The latter activates the headlamp washer pump with successive impulses lasting about half a second. The headlamp washer circuit is protected by a fuse located in the engine compartment junction unit. When the instrument panel receives an insufficient windscreen washer fluid level signal via the CAN, it shows the relevant symbols and message on the display. This function is only enabled with the ignition switched ON (INT).

Operational Description The relay F17 for the engine compartment junction unit B001 is supplied directly by the battery from the line protected by fuse F9 (also located inside junction unit B001) and is energized by the line controlled by the ignition INT/A via fuse F31 in the junction unit under the dashboard B002. When the Body Computer receives an activation command from the steering column switch unit H005 (pin 5 of connector A) at pin 13 of connector A, having already received a command to switch on the dipped headlamps (pin 4 of connector E) or the main beam headlamps (pin 33 of connector C), it sends a negative signal, from pin 14 of the same connector, to control the coil for relay R17 which supplies the headlamp washer pump interfaced with the front/headlamp washer coupling D098 at pin 5. If there is insufficient windscreen washer fluid in the reservoir, then the info-telematic control unit M065 receives a negative signal, at pin 21 of connector A, from the switch interfaced with the front/headlamp washer coupling D098 (pin 2); this signal is sent via the B-CAN (pins 1 and 3 of connector A) to the instrument panel E050 (pins 3 and 4 of connector A) which displays the message.

Description In the case of poor visibility it is possible to activate the demisting of the rearscreen, the exterior rear view mirrors and the windscreen. The control button, located on the climate control system control unit, sends a signal via the CAN to the Body Computer which, depending on the logics described later on, manages the heating of the resistances for the components. These resistances absorb a considerable amount of energy and are therefore controlled and, possibly, deactivated after they have been working for a certain length of time. The activation of the demisting function for the rearscreen, rear view mirrors and windscreen can only occur if the INT (+15) signal is present. The Body Computer acquires this condition during starting (INT/A) and does not energize the relay inside the junction unit under the dashboard. The deactivation of the demisting function, on the other hand, is possible: manually: by pressing the unstable button on the climate control system control unit again or if there is no INT (key-off) signal; automatically: after 20 minutes effective operation with the control activated. The automatic operation of the device is also linked to the engine speed; the switching on/off logic is as follows: the first ten minutes operation is not dependent on the engine speed; the period after this depends on the engine conditions, namely: if the engine speed is below 950 rpm, then the device should be switched off after 10 seconds; if, on the other hand, the engine speed is above 1000 rpm for at least 5 seconds, then the rearscreen and the other components can be switched on or remain switched on if they are already on until they have been working effectively for 20 minutes. The automatic activation of the demisting function is also determined by the outside temperature conditions: the Body Computer acquires information concerning the outside temperature, via the CAN, from the sensor inside the driver's rear view mirror and, if the temperature is below the level of 3 degrees, then the rearscreen, the exterior rear view mirrors and the windscreen need demisting. During the entire period of automatic operation the heated rear windscreen relay should be switched off if the battery voltage goes below 8.5V for 0.5 seconds. The relay is restored when the battery voltage increases to 9V for a period of half a second. A tolerance of ±5% applies to all the values described The automatic activation cycle (20 minutes) is restored each time a command is received via the special button. The heated rear windscren warning light is managed by the climate control system control unit depending on the command send via the CAN from the Body Computer. During automatic operation the warning light should remain on constantly, even during periods in which the demisting function may be deactivated, following the logic described previously. When the MAX-DEF control is activated using the button on the climate control system control unit, it is possible to activate the functions of switching on the heated rear windscreen, demisting the windscreen (with the possibility of manually increasing or decreasing the speed of the fan) and the forced recirculation of the air, all for a predefined period which starts the moment the engine coolant reaches operating temperature See E5020 ENGINE COOLING The deactivation of the MAX-DEF control only involves switching off the heated rear windscreen if the command to switch it on came from the MAX-DEF button; if, on the other hand, the command was given via the heated rear windscreen button, it remains on.

Operational Description The heated rear windscreen relay R11, located in the junction unit under the dashboard B002, directly controls the simultaneous engagement of the demisting function and the heated rear windscreen P055 (line protected by fuse F40) and the heated windscreen P056 (line protected by fuse F41). The driver's M066 and passenger M067 front door control units (pin 10 of connector A and pin 33 of connector C) on the other hand enable the demisting function for the exterior view mirrors P060 and P061 (pins 7 and 8), respectively via the B-CAN managed by the Body Computer M001. Description The exterior rear view mirrors are electrically adjusted in two directions (horizontally and vertically) using a joystick; the left or right mirror is chosen using a selector. The driver's front door control unit acquires the adjustment commands and transmits them, via the CAN, to the passenger side. There are three buttons on the driver's front seat controls used for the automatic recall of the positions memorized. See E3076 ELECTRICALLY-ADJUSTABLE SEATS See E3035 STEERING WHEEL ADJUSTMENT See E3077 FRONT HEAD RESTRAINT ADJUSTMENT This memory funcion is managed by the driving position control unit, which downloads seat and steering column positions directly and also door mirror positions via the CAN network. The control unit stores all the above positions when one of the three buttons is held down for at least three seconds. A buzzer inside the instrument panel goes off when the positions have been stored. The memory recall function is inhibited when the car is travelling faster than 10 km/h, via a signal sent via the CAN network from the Body Computer to the driving position control unit. If command come simultaneously from the joystick and the steering control unit, the former have priority, thereby cancelling the return of the exterior rear view mirrors to the position memorized. The rear view mirrors contain 3 motors: one for movement on the horizontal axis, one for movement on the vertical axis and one used for folding back the actual mirror. The folding function is also managed by the control unit at the driver's door which acquires the command from a button near the joystick. The folding always applies to both mirrors, irrespective of the current position of the selector. The rear view mirror folding function is automatically deactivated by the Body Computer on the acquisition of a speedometer signal where the speed of the vehicle is above 40 Km/h. When reverse gear is engaged (see Wiring diagram E2022 Reversing lights) thanks to the presence of a rain and dusk sensor, the electro-chromic interior rear view mirror (interfaced with the roof control unit) is immediately darkened, like the exterior rear view mirrors, allowing improved visibility. See E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS All the functions described are enabled in the key-on condition (INT).

Operational Description The Body Computer M001, supplied by the lines controlled by the ignition (INT) and directly from the battery (protected by fuses F37 and F53 of the junction unit under the dashboard, respectively) transmit the switch discharge signal, via the B-CAN (pins 10 and 28 of connector D) to the left front door M066 and right front door M067 control units (pins 31 and 32 of connector C) which enable the adjustment and folding functions for the exterior mirrors P060 and P061. The adjustment/folding control H031 contains the joystick and the selector: from pin 12 to pin 14 of connector A of the driver's front door control unit M066 sending the mirrors movement signal from the joystick; from pin 7 to pin 5 of the same connector selecting the exterior mirror to be moved. If the passenger side mirror P061 is selected, the driver's door control unit M066 sends the command, via the B-CAN, to the passenger door control unit M067 which adjusts the appropriate mirror (pins 24, 25 and 26 of connector C). The two front door control units are supplied by the line directly from the battery protected by fuse F61 of the luggage compartment junction unit B045. The mirrors folding function is managed by the two front door control units via pin 34 (mirror opening) and pin 36 (mirror closing) of connector C. The Body Computer M001 acquires the disabling signal for the folding function, at pin 7 of connector A, if the speed of the vehicle exceeds 40 Kh/m signalled by the braking system control unit M051 (pin 16). The steering control unit M076 manages the return to the positions memorized by the driver's seat controls H066 via pins 3C and 7C of connector B and sends the signal managed by the Body Computer M001, via the C-CAN (pins 4A and 3B of connector C), which enables the two control units for the front doors via the B-CAN. The steering position memorizing function is signalled by the buzzer inside the instrument panel E050 thanks to a signal received through the B-CAN at pins 3 and 4 of connector A. The roof control unit M062 directly supplies and inhibits the darkening of the electro-chromic interior rear view mirror P065 (pins 9, 13 and 16 of connector A); the darkening of the right exterior mirror P061 and the left exterior mirror P060 (pins 9 and 15) is managed through pins 2 and 3 of connector B. The rain and dusk sensor K125 is connected to the roof control unit M062 at pins 2, 8 and 12 of connector A. The Body Computer receives the reverse gear engaged signal at pin 3 of connector H. See E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS

Description The vehicle is equipped with a special electric steering wheel height adjustment device which is useful for the driver for ensuring the best driving position; there are two main movements for the steering column: longitudinal and axial. The electric steering wheel adjustment device is managed by the steering position control unit: this movement can be made either manually, using the joystick on the left of the steering wheel or automatically by recalling one of three memorized positions using the buttons in the driver's seat controls. The electrical movement of the steering wheel (manual and automatic) is only activated with the ignition ON (INT); when the ignition is switched OFF a timed period of around a minute starts during which the completely automatic operation of the memory recall is guaranteed. he device is excluded temporarily during start-up (INT/A). The "Easy Entry/Exit" function is activated to make to easier for the driver to get into and out of the car: it consists in the upwards movement, as far as the end of travel position, of the steering column and, at the same time, the backwards movement of the driver's seat by about 5 cm when the key-off condition is ascertained and the driver's front door is open. See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING The steering wheel and seat return to the positions set by the user when stable conditions are restored, i.e. door closed nad key-on. Three buttons on the front driver seat are used to call up stored positions automatically. The control unit stores all the above positions when one of the three buttons is held down for at least three seconds. Operational Description Driving position control unit M076 is supplied by two lines: one to pin B8 of connector C via service relay R21 and fuse F56 of boot junction unit B045 (used to supply the drive motors), the other to pin C7 of connector C via a line protected by fuse F69 of B045. Service relay R21 is activated from a signal from boot control unit M063 (pin 24 of connector F), which enables (via the B-CAN network) movement of the various loads even during the timed period (one minute) following Key-off. The controls on the driver's front seat H066 are connected from pin A3 to pin 3C of connector B of the steering control unit M076 for the memorizing/recall function for the three positions. Driving position control unit M076 maintains the three head restraint positions in the memory by means of a potentiometer that supplies its own analogue return signal: at pin A5 of connector C from the potentiometer inside the engine unit N028 (axial position of the steering column); at pin B45 of connector C from the potentiometer inside the engine unit N029 (vertical position of the steering column); Memory store is indicated by a buzzer inside instrument panel E050 via a signal received on the B-CAN network at pins 3 and 4 of connector A. Absence of INT (Key-off) and driver side front door opening signals is detected by Body Computer M001 at pin 9 of connector H and pin 8 of connector F, and determines activation of the "Easy Entry Exit" described above. The luggage compartment control unit is supplied by the line protected by fuse F61 of junction unti B045. The steering wheel adjustment controls H093 are connected to connector C of the steering cotnrol unit M076: to pin 3A for axial forwards/backwards movement via motor N028 (from pins B1 and C1 of connector C); to pin 6A for vertical lifting via motor N029 (from pins A1 and B2 of connector C); to pin 5B for vertical lowering via motor N029 (from pins A1 and B2 of connector C, polarized in the reverse way to the lifting). Body Computer M001 receives a car speed signal from braking system control unit M051 at pin 7 of connector A: if this speed exceeds 10 Km/h, the Body Computer (pins 5 and 7 of H) inhibits any motion (automatic and/or manual) of the driver side seat via the B-CAN network. Driving position control unit M076 downloads this condition via the C-CAN network at pins A4 and B3 of connector C. Body Computer M001 receives an INT/A (key-on) signal from ignition switch H001 at pin 27 of connector D via fuse F31 of underfacia control unit B002.

Description The simultaneous operation of the door locks takes place via: the key; the door switches (knobs); the buttons on the driver's door; the remote control. Since the central locking can control the individual locks separately, the repulsion function is not carried out. The lock realignment strategies for the individual doors is therefore not implemented. The lock is locked with the door open. the number of consecutive locking/unlocking manoeuvres. If 10-11 opening/closing manoeuvres are carried out within a period of 25 seconds, the system is inhibited for 30 seconds. - the reception of locking/unlocking signals inhibiting the system for 0.5 seconds for access to the vehicle, thereby preventing any overlapping of commands from the outside with the exception of the "double pressing" to activate the dead-lock. through setting the locking/unlocking strategy in the info-telematic control unit for all the doors or for the passenger door only or the boot only. The dead-lock function is automatically engaged via the mechanical key the moment the doors are locked by turning the key a second time within a second of the locking manoeuvre through both pawls in the front doors. With the ignition switched on the signals coming from the door (and boot) open switches display the message on the instrument panel display and there is an acoustic signal. The remote control located in the key has three separate buttons: one for locking, one for unlocking and one for releasing the boot. Description The Passive Entry system allows access to the vehicle passenger compartment passively without having to use any control components (key, remote control, etc.) for locking and unlocking the doors. The unlocking action is carried out automatically when the exterior handle is pulled once the CID (Customer Identification Device) Passive Entry control unit has been recognised. The CID contains a passive entry electronic management circuit and a mechanical key. The key is no longer retractable but simply extractable because it is used only in case of emergencies. Once the Passive Entry control unit recognizes the CID, the doors are not unlocked, this only happens the moment the handle of the door is operated allowing access to the passenger compartment. This stategy is displayed on the door in as far the LED in the panel stops the deterrent flashing to signal that access to the passenger compartment is possible, whilst the direction indicators signal the unlocking of the doors. The vehicle central locking action is activated by pressing any of the handles from the outside. The Passive Entry system has an auto-close function which allows the automatic locking of the locks after moving away from the vehicle. This function can be activated/deactivated on request through the menu in the instrument panel of the info-telematic control unit display. The dead-lock function is engaged the moment the doors are locked by pressing the handle a second time within 1 second of pressing it the first time. The command actions available at the door locks take place by: the presence of the CID pressing one of the vehicle's outside handles turning the mechanical key in one of the knobs. The operation of the locks is managed by the body computer which controls: the effective status of the doors through the signals that arrive from the switches in the locks (signals which are also used for the timed delay of the lights): in this way the locking command is only carried out with all the doors properly shut and the locks released; conversely, the unlocking command is only carried out with the locks locked; the position of the switches. Since the central locking can control the individual locks separately, the repulsion function is not carried out. The lock realignment strategies for the individual doors is therefore not implemented. The lock is locked with the door open. the number of consecutive locking/unlocking manoeuvres. If 10-11 opening/closing manoeuvres are carried out within a period of 25 seconds, the system is inhibited for 30 seconds. the reception of locking/unlocking signals inhibiting the system for 0.5 seconds for access to the vehicle, thereby preventing any overlapping of commands from the outside with the exception of the "double pressing" to activate the dead-lock. through setting the locking/unlocking strategy in the info-telematic control unit for all the doors or for the passenger door only or the boot only. With the ignition switched on the signals coming from the door (and boot) open switches display the message on the instrument panel display and there is an acoustic signal. The receiver aerial for recognizing the CID is connected directly to the Passive Entry control unit which implements the following strategy: locking/unlocking the doors and the boot (Wiring Diagram ) E3045 BOOT OPENING - FUEL FILLER FLAP - COMPARTMENT MOTOR switching on the alarm (Wiring Diagram ) E7015 ALARM closing the electric front windows See E3050 ELECTRIC FRONT WINDOWS closing the electric rear windows (Wiring Diagram ) E3051 ELECTRIC REAR WINDOWS closing the electric sun roof See E3060 SUN ROOF and, if necessary, engaging the dead-lock function.

The lid is unlocked to allow the boot to be opened only at the moment when the handle is pulled. The boot handle moves in both directions: pull to open the boot and push to lock the car. The entire car can be locked (all doors locked) by pressing the handle/button on the boot. The boot control unit downloads the lock/release signal and controls the boot in accordance with the following strategy: the boot is released when the key is pressed; the boot is released if the key is pressed for longer than one second. If the "independent driver's side door unlock" option is active, the boot is not unlocked because the only car access point is the front driver's side door. The boot can be set to one of two modes from the instrument panel: boot controlled by door lock (default): boot status reflects door status. When the car is locked, the boot is locked. When the car is unlocked, the boot is unlocked; boot independent: the boot is permanently locked (to protect the contents) and can be opened by means of a button on the facia. Because the front driver door can be unlocked and operated independently of the other doors, fuel filler flap status is linked to the locked/unlocked status of the front driver side door: fuel filler flap locked with door locked fuel filler flap unlocked with door unlocked The fuel filler flap is managed directly by the body computer. The boot compartment control unit receives glove compartment flap opening command from a switch on the facia. This command can be activated even with key-off The unlocking action is carried out automatically when the exterior handle is pulled once the CID (Customer Identification Device) Passive Entry control unit has been recognised.

Description The front electric window can be activated only with key-on (INT) except when the windows are closed/opened centrally via remote control and during the timed period with key off. Operation of the front windows with key off (STOP) must be possible only in manual mode unless one of the doors is opened (when all movements are deactivated) and in any case within the timed period calculated and managed by the Body Computer. This applies during the first few minutes following transition from Key-on (INT) to key-off (STOP). During start-up (INT/A), the device is temporarily cut off. The driver and passenger side motors are thus controlled in both manual and automatic mode in accordance with the following strategy: Movements of the driver side window are managed by the relevant door control unit in accordance with local commands. if the length of time for which the control key is pressed is between 50 and 300 milliseconds, operation is manual. the glass goes up/down only with the key pressed; f the key is pressed for longer than 300 milliseconds, operation is automatic: the window continues to go up/down until it reaches the end of its travel or the control key is pressed again; if the key is pressed for less than 50 milliseconds, this is ignored (it is treated as an accidental knock). Passenger side window movement is managed by the relevant door control unit on the basis of local commands or commands received via the CAN network via the driver's side door control unit: management of manual or automatic operation (up/down) of the passenger side window from the driver's side controls is similar to that of the driver's window; the window can be raised using the local control only in manual mode; descending operation is controlled locally in accordance with the following strategy: when the control is pressed for a period from 50 to 300 milliseconds, operation is manual. Movement is automatic when the pressure exceeds 300 milliseconds. Inputs on both control units receive information from their own doors. These indicate the presence of a possible obstacle in the way of the rising windows (antipinch function). This occurs in both manual and automatic mode. If this happens, the relevant control unit must immediately interrupt the glass travel and then reverse the direction for 300 ms. If the antipinch protection is activated, the node that manages window movement receives a signal indicating that the seal has been compressed by means of a resistive sensor fitted into a coating applied to the upper driver or passenger window seal. If the instrument panel receives one or more fault messages from the window antipinch seal coatings via the CAN network, it displays the relevant message on the matrix display. The window central locking function (also applicable to the sun-roof) can be activated by means of specific signals sent to the Body Computer: See E3060 SUN ROOF by the climate control sstem control unit that detects the presence of exhaust gas by means of a special sensor (with key-on); See E3020 WINDSCREEN WASH/WIPE pressing the remote control key or door handle pawl for a few seconds until the end of the manoevre (with key off) See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING using a signal from the rain and dusk sensor the window central opening function is activated solely from the remote control under conditions of key-off (STOP).
